noteworthy:

author: eisenhauer
body:
Re-implement the DAOS engine around a per-rank DAOS array for data. Each writer rank issues async daos_array_write submits during AddToVec; EndStep drains and flushes any tail synchronously.  No aggregator.

Highlights:
  - DaosChunkV (new ChunkV subclass) issues async daos_array_write once a chunk-fill byte threshold is crossed, with a multi-iov SGL over a single contiguous array range.
  - ChunkV gains cross-step chunk recycling and an m_NoShrink flag for subclasses with in-flight async I/O against chunk memory. Stable chunk addresses keep the libfabric MR cache hot and eliminate per-step first-touch zeroing.
  - data_oids.txt at the dataset root maps writer rank to per-rank DAOS array OID; the reader parses it at Init.
  - daos_fini intentionally not called at Close: libdaos's reinit path after fini is unreliable.  Per-handle close is.

Per-rank metadata location is selected by the DAOS_METADATA_LAYOUT env var (default 'array-1mb-aligned'; also 'array' and 'kv'). Engine parameters narrowed to those actually used by the DAOS path. Profiling output is the standard <dataset>/profiling.json; BP5Serializer-side and DaosChunkV-side counters mirror into registered timers via SyncExternalCountersToProfiler.

Removes legacy data-path variants (TwoLevelShm, TwoLevelShm_Async, EveryoneWrites_Async) and their associated aggregator / burst- buffer / async-thread infrastructure.

Limitations: Append mode is rejected; Span Puts are unsupported.

Docs: developer_docs/daos_engine.md, user_guide engines/daos.rst.

author: conradoboty
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip orchestrates AI agents and manages their execution workspaces (git worktrees + dev servers)
> - Agents start runtime services (pnpm dev, etc.) inside their execution workspaces during issue work
> - When an issue reaches a terminal state (done/cancelled), those services are never stopped — they leak until reboot or manual pkill
> - On 2026-05-06, COD-104 and COD-145 left 22+17 orphan processes 7h after closing, holding ~3.9 GB of swap (93.5% — see COD-187)
> - The root cause: issue closure does not signal the workspace to tear down services
> - The fix: emit an integration event from the Issue context on terminal transition; the ExecutionWorkspace context subscribes and stops services when no live issue retains the workspace
> - This PR implements the full event-driven binding described in [COD-193 ADR](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/discussions) and tracked in internal issue COD-196

## What Changed

- **`packages/shared/src/constants.ts`**: Added `"issue.lifecycle.terminated"` to `PLUGIN_EVENT_TYPES` (plugins can now subscribe to this event too)
- **`server/src/services/issue-lifecycle-handler.ts`** (new file):
  - `IssueLifecycleTerminatedPayload` type — v1 payload `{ issueId, terminalStatus, closedAt, executionWorkspaceId | null }`
  - `emitIssueLifecycleTerminated()` — builds and publishes the event via `publishPluginDomainEvent` (fire-and-forget)
  - `registerIssueLifecycleHandler()` — registers an internal subscriber on the plugin event bus using `forPlugin("system.workspace-lifecycle")`; handler: resolves workspace, checks for surviving non-terminal owners, calls `stopRuntimeServicesForExecutionWorkspace`, retries 3× with exponential backoff, posts a failure comment tagging `@InstanceOps` on permanent failure
- **`server/src/routes/issues.ts`**: Calls `emitIssueLifecycleTerminated` after the PATCH db commit when status first transitions to `done` or `cancelled`; fire-and-forget so PATCH response is not blocked
- **`server/src/app.ts`**: Calls `registerIssueLifecycleHandler(db, eventBus)` immediately after `setPluginEventBus(eventBus)`
- **`server/src/services/issue-lifecycle-handler.test.ts`** (new file): 8 unit tests covering payload shape, happy-path stop, live-owner skip, idempotency (archived/missing workspace), and failure-comment path via fake timers

## Verification

```bash
# Type-check (all packages)
pnpm typecheck

# Unit tests for the new handler
pnpm vitest run server/src/services/issue-lifecycle-handler.test.ts
# → 8 passed

# All server service tests
pnpm vitest run server/src/services/
# → 16 passed
```

Manual E2E flow (requires a running Paperclip instance):
1. Create an issue with an execution workspace that has a running runtime service
2. PATCH the issue to `status: "done"`
3. Within 60s, verify the runtime service record shows `status: "stopped"` and no child processes remain under the worktree path

## Risks

- **Idempotency**: re-delivery of the same `IssueLifecycleTerminated` event is guarded by the workspace `status === "archived"` check (no-op) and the live-owners query. Tested.
- **Shared workspaces**: The live-owners check (`WHERE executionWorkspaceId = $id AND status NOT IN ('done','cancelled') AND id != $issueId`) correctly skips teardown when any other issue retains the workspace. Tested.
- **Retry delays**: 3 retries with 5s/10s/20s backoff; total worst-case before failure comment is ~35s, well within the 60s AC bound.
- **Silent failure guard**: failure comment posting uses a nested try/catch so a comment failure is logged but doesn't suppress the outer error log.
- **Event schema**: `IssueLifecycleTerminated v1` is additive (new event type, not modifying existing events). No existing event interfaces changed.
- **Low risk overall**: the PATCH response path is unchanged (fire-and-forget emit). No new DB schema. No migration needed.

## Model Used

- Provider: Anthropic
- Model: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (`claude-sonnet-4-6`)
- Mode: Agentic tool use (Claude Code / Paperclip Coder agent)
- Context: 200k token window

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have specified the model used (with version and capability details)
- [x] I have checked ROADMAP.md and confirmed this PR does not duplicate planned core work
- [x] I have run tests locally and they pass
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable
- [ ] If this change affects the UI, I have included before/after screenshots — N/A (server-only change)
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation to reflect my changes
- [x] I have considered and documented any risks above
- [x] I will address all Greptile and reviewer comments before requesting merge

**Reviewer:** @CTO requested for architectural sign-off (event naming, payload shape, bounded-context boundaries) per COD-196 description.

author: sawapi
body:
## Summary

Aligns `ulcerIndex` with the original Peter Martin & Byron McCann (1987) definition:

1. `rolling_max[j] = max(close[j-N+1..j])`
2. `drawdown[j] = (close[j] - rolling_max[j]) / rolling_max[j] × 100`
3. `UI[i] = sqrt(mean(drawdown[i-N+1..i]^2))`

Each per-bar drawdown is now measured against that bar's own rolling peak. The previous implementation shared a single peak across the whole window, which the docstring already described canonically — the code is now consistent with the docstring.

## Breaking changes

- **Warmup**: `2 × period - 1` bars (was `period`). First non-null at index `2 × period - 2` (was `period - 1`).
- **Values**: change for every period combination — callers that pinned numeric outputs need to refresh expected values.
- **State schema**: `UlcerIndexState` replaces the single `buffer` field with `prices` and `drawdowns` buffers. Per-bar drawdowns aren't recoverable from the old shape, so `createUlcerIndex(..., { fromState: oldSnapshot })` now throws a clear `"legacy state snapshot detected"` error on the old format. Re-warm from candles.

## Why this is needed

The previous implementation was numerically inconsistent with the published Ulcer Index definition. A flat peak across the window underweighted older bars' drawdowns, producing systematically lower values than the formula in Peter Martin's 1987 paper and the StockCharts / Wikipedia descriptions. A cross-validation regression test now pins the canonical behavior at 9-decimal precision against an independent reference fixture.

## Scope

- `packages/core/src/indicators/volatility/ulcer-index.ts` — batch
- `packages/core/src/indicators/incremental/volatility/ulcer-index.ts` — incremental + state-schema guard
- `packages/core/src/indicators/__tests__/ulcer-index.test.ts` — refreshed unit tests for the new formula and warmup
- `packages/core/src/indicators/incremental/__tests__/volatility-indicators.test.ts` — added `legacy state snapshot is rejected` test
- `packages/core/cross-validation/__tests__/cross-validation.test.ts` + new `fixtures/ulcer-index.json` — regression guard
- `packages/core/cross-validation/__tests__/formula-verification.test.ts` — refreshed expected formula
- `packages/core/cross-validation/python/generate_fixtures.py` — adds the Ulcer fixture
- `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md` — breaking note

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter trendcraft test` — 5020/5020 passing
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter trendcraft build` clean
- [x] Cross-validation suite: 67/67 passing (was 66; +1 Ulcer parity test)
- [x] Batch and incremental output now match within 1e-10 across the full 200-bar synthetic dataset

## Summary

Hardens the human-facing K3 WISE postdeploy summary so it no longer renders `Internal trial signoff: PASS` for contradictory evidence.

- explicit `signoff.internalTrial="pass"` now still requires `ok=true`, `authenticated=true`, and `summary.fail=0`
- inferred PASS from older evidence without a `signoff` block also requires `summary.fail=0`
- inconsistent evidence keeps the renderer non-fatal but renders signoff as `BLOCKED` with a direct reason
- adds development and verification notes

## Why

The separate signoff gate can fail machine checks, but operators also read GitHub Step Summary. A stale or hand-edited evidence file should not visually show PASS when the same JSON says the smoke failed, skipped auth, or has failed checks.

author: anajuliabit
body:
**Branched off main.** Pins the structured-error contract every agent integration relies on.

## What
26 new tests in \`src/__tests__/command-error-paths.test.ts\` covering the pre-flight error paths of every shipped command. Each test asserts a specific \`code\` value on stderr's structured JSON.

## Approach
Spawn the CLI binary via \`execFile\` with synthetic env (\`REPPO_PRIVATE_KEY=0x11..11\`). Pre-flight errors fire **before** any chain call, so no mock RPC is needed. The few error codes that require a chain read (\`NOT_LOCKUP_OWNER\`, \`ACCESS_ALREADY_GRANTED\`, \`DURATION_OUT_OF_BOUNDS\`, etc.) are out of scope here — they belong to integration tests against an anvil fork.

## Coverage
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Test count | 62 | **88** |
| Test files | 7 | **8** |
| **v8 % (statements)** | 33.75% | **21.35%** ⚠️ |

The v8 percentage went **down** despite adding 26 passing tests. Reason: \`execFile\` spawns a child Node process; v8 coverage only tracks the parent vitest process. The spawned CLI's code paths aren't instrumented. **The tests validate the contract end-to-end correctly — they just don't show up in coverage numbers.**

A future module-mocked suite (mock \`viem\` at the module level, import command classes directly, invoke them) could close this gap. This PR prioritizes pinning the public agent contract over shifting the coverage number.

## What this prevents
- Renaming an error code without updating the test → CI fails (e.g. \`INVALID_AMOUNT\` → \`AMOUNT_INVALID\` would be caught)
- Reordering pre-flight checks so a different error fires first → CI fails
- Removing pre-flight validation entirely (e.g. delegating to the chain instead of catching at parse time) → CI fails

## Notes
- \`unlock\` tests deferred — command lands in PR #23 (sibling of this PR). When #23 merges, add 3 more tests (\`INVALID_LOCKUP_ID\`, \`INVALID_ADDRESS\` (\`--to\`), \`MISSING_PRIVATE_KEY\`).
- The test runner takes ~15s for 26 cases because each test spawns a fresh tsx + Node process. Could be faster via a long-lived child or by importing command classes directly with mocked viem; deferred to a follow-up.

## Test plan
- [x] \`npm test\` — 88/88 passing
- [x] \`npm run lint\` exits 0
- [x] \`npm run typecheck\` exits 0
- [x] \`npm run build\` emits \`dist/bin.js\`

author: milotic3005-design
body:
## 💡 What
Replaced the asynchronous `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256')` algorithm used to generate cache keys in `src/lib/cache.ts` with a simple synchronous string normalization (`query.toLowerCase().trim()`). Also added comments to explain the optimization logic and removed unnecessary `await` keywords in `src/lib/aggregator.ts`.

## 🎯 Why
The application was using a cryptographic hash to generate keys for a standard JavaScript `Map` functioning as an in-memory TTL cache. This is a severe anti-pattern because:
1. `crypto.subtle.digest` is asynchronous and forces the event loop into a microtask delay.
2. It generates unnecessary CPU overhead and memory allocations (via `TextEncoder` and `Uint8Array`).
3. JavaScript `Map` objects natively and efficiently handle string keys without the need for hashing them to hex representations.

## 📊 Impact
* **Performance:** Reduces cache key generation time by >99% (measured drop from ~1.7ms down to ~0.001ms).
* **Throughput:** Removes async blocking behavior on every single cached query, leading to drastically reduced latency on warm searches and higher parallel request throughput.

## 🔬 Measurement
To verify the performance jump:
1. Create a script measuring key generation (as demonstrated in earlier testing).
2. Start the local server and profile network requests to the `/api/v1/suggest` route, noting latency reduction on repeated requests.

## Summary

Fix de la causa raíz de Issue #5 — bug que generaba **$225,503 MXN de overhead artificial** en `cost_entries` por plantillas recurrentes duplicadas.

**Cleanup ya ejecutado en producción** (74 rows borrados, backup en `_cost_duplicates_backup_2026_05_05`).
Este PR previene que vuelva a pasar.

## Bug raíz

En `Sistema/js/costs.js:saveCost`, master_admin podía crear N plantillas recurrentes con misma `(branch_id, category, amount, period_type)` porque:

```js
branch_id: isMasterAdmin ? (document.getElementById('cost-branch')?.value || currentBranchId) : currentBranchId,
```

Si no seleccionaba el dropdown `cost-branch`, el fallback silencioso usaba `currentBranchId`. Resultado: 4 plantillas de "Línea Amarilla $10,000 mensual" para 4 sucursales acababan TODAS con el mismo branch_id activo, solo diferenciadas por la nota.

Después, cada vez que se ejecutaba `generateRecurringCosts()` mensualmente, las 4 plantillas generaban 4 instancias del mismo costo → $40K/mes inflados solo en linea_amarilla. Acumulado a hoy: $130K.

## Cambios

### `Sistema/js/costs.js` (saveCost)
- Master_admin que crea recurring **DEBE** seleccionar branch en dropdown — no más fallback silencioso a `currentBranchId`
- Verificación pre-save: si ya existe plantilla con misma `(branch_id, category, amount, period_type, recurring=true)`, se rechaza con mensaje claro

### `backend/routes/costs.js` (POST /)
- Mismo check anti-duplicado server-side (defense in depth)
- Devuelve **409** con `existing_id` si encuentra plantilla previa

- [ ] Como master_admin, crear "linea_amarilla $10000 monthly Sucursal A" → OK

author: ericson2314
body:
Add a `Socketfile` that declares sockets for `hydra-server` and `hydra-queue-runner`, so foreman can pass sockets to them just like systemd socket activation would. This means that development with foreman is once again exercising the same code paths that production will use.

The foreman start scripts are updated accordingly:

- `hydra-server` switches from `hydra-dev-server --port` to `hydra-server -f` (Starman with fork mode), picking up the socket via the `Net::Server::Systemd::PreFork` personality.

- `hydra-queue-runner` gets `--rest-bind - --grpc-bind -` to use socket activation for both its REST and gRPC servers.

- All services now `wait_for_hydra_db` before starting, since with socket activation the listen port is open before the server is ready, so `wait_for_hydra_server` alone is no longer sufficient.
The foreman fork (Ericson2314/foreman@socketfile, PR https://github.com/ddollar/foreman/pull/816) adds the `Socketfile` feature. Foreman is packaged from source in `packaging/foreman/` because it was not clear how to override the Nixpkgs version which gets its source from rubygems.

> [!NOTE]
>
> I would not use forked projects when I am far from sure that upstream would accept the change in production, but foreman is just a developer convenience in the dev shell. That to me makes this OK --- it's just for developer convenience.

----

The previous two commits are good regardless.

author: austinvazquez
body:
### Issue

When containerd shuts down its metadata or mount plugin never explicitly close the underlying bboltdb file deferring cleanup of the lock file to the underlying OS. The issue encountered is this causes variable delay for use cases where graceful teardown is desirable to reliably reset containerd.

### Summary

This change adds closing of the metadata and mount boltdb to server shutdown.

#### Garbage collection consideration

The GC plugin currently does not implement Close, thus is skipped in server stop.

Closure of the metadata database should occur after acquiring the read-write lock to ensure no GC cycle is occurring concurrently. Transactions post-closure will result in `ErrDatabaseNotOpen`. This should be fine as these resources can be scheduled for collection on the next containerd process invocation.

### Testing

Updated existing unit tests to close via plugin/manager rather than directly on the raw bolt handle.
Added new test cases to verify the underlying bolt Db is closed by asserting a new transaction returns ErrDatabaseNotOpen.

body:
The bot was using a price-above-EMA-200 AND RSI-below-50 signal which, combined with a misconfigured `DEFAULT_SYMBOLS` list using USD pairs instead of USDT, meant no trades were ever placed.

## Changes

- **`config.py`**: `DEFAULT_SYMBOLS` corrected to USDT pairs (`BTC/USDT`, `ETH/USDT`); `SIMPLE_ALGO_SHORT_PERIOD` changed from 50 → 20 to match the requested 20/50 EMA pairing.
- **`trader.py` — `get_indicators()`**: Now returns `ema20`, `ema50`, `prev_ema20`, `prev_ema50`, and `rsi` (drops `ema200`). Fetches `SIMPLE_ALGO_LONG_PERIOD + RSI_PERIOD + 10` candles (74 vs. 224 previously).
- **`trader.py` — `should_buy()`**: New signal requires both:
  1. EMA-20 crosses above EMA-50 (`prev_ema20 ≤ prev_ema50` and `ema20 > ema50`)
  2. RSI < `config.RSI_OVERSOLD` (50)

```python
crossed_above = (
    indicators["prev_ema20"] <= indicators["prev_ema50"]
    and indicators["ema20"] > indicators["ema50"]
)
rsi_below = indicators["rsi"] < config.RSI_OVERSOLD
signal = crossed_above and rsi_below
```

- **`tests/test_trader.py`**: `TestGetIndicators` and `TestShouldBuy` updated to cover the new signal logic, including crossover-fires-but-RSI-too-high and already-crossed (no new signal) cases.

author: ggreif
body:
## Summary
Extends the same `max_jobs=1` workaround used by `gc-tests` in #6009 to the `tests` matrix on `arm64-linux-16`. `ubuntu-24-large` keeps `max-jobs=auto`.

## Why
`tests (arm64-linux-16, release)` and `tests (arm64-linux-16, debug)` have been OOM-killed by the runner whenever `nix-build-uncached --max-jobs auto` schedules three parallel ~3 GB derivation builds. Most recent observation: https://github.com/caffeinelabs/motoko/actions/runs/25409615273/job/74528169567 (initial CI on the `pocket-ic` bump PR #6088 — failure was unrelated to the bump itself).

## Why max-jobs=1 (not 2)
We probed a higher ceiling but it's not stable enough to ship:

- PR #6090 ran `gc-tests` and `tests` at `max-jobs=2` against a cache-busted `test-runner` and **appeared** to pass.
- PR #6088 with a *different* cache-buster (forcing a different content hash than #6090's, and therefore a real cold rebuild of the GC-variant derivations) hit OOM on `gc-tests (arm64-linux-16, 2)` after ~2.5 minutes:
  ```
  building 'test-drun-compacting-gc.drv'...
  building 'test-drun-generational-gc.drv'...
  Killed   nix-build-uncached -build-flags "--max-jobs 2"
  ```
  Run: https://github.com/caffeinelabs/motoko/actions/runs/25411132891/job/74532926605

The result depends on which derivations happen to be cachix-cached vs cold-rebuilt at any given moment. An asymmetric `gc-tests=1, tests=2` configuration would also be brittle: a future test addition could shift the memory profile of `release-systems-go` and silently reintroduce OOMs. Going uniform `max-jobs=1` is slower but stable.

## Test plan
- [x] CI green
- [x] No `tests (arm64-linux-16, *)` OOM on the resulting run

author: joaquinrivero
body:
## Why

Sync `.github/workflows/pinata-code-review.yml` with the canonical version on [Adobe-acom/pinata](https://github.com/Adobe-acom/pinata) `stage`. The workflows had drifted across multiple harness releases.

## What changed

| # | Hunk | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | YAML indentation 4-space → 2-space | Cosmetic |
| 2 | Concurrency key: branch-scoped → PR-number-scoped | Prevents cancellation across re-pushes |
| 3 | Timeout 15 → 30 min | Matches harness reviewer runtime |
| 4 | `actions/checkout` SHA pin → `@v6` | Adopts harness pinning policy |
| 5 | `create-github-app-token` SHA pin → `@v3`, `app-id:` → `client-id:` | **Breaking — see Risk** |
| 6 | Single token reused across checkouts (separate harness-token step removed) | Simplifies auth flow |
| 7 | `Install Claude Code` step → `pinata-install.sh` | Matches harness install path |
| 8 | Harness checkout: `ref:` conditional added | Self-host PR base ref when on Adobe-acom/pinata; default branch otherwise — no behavior change for this repo |
| 9 | `Validate inputs` step removed | Subsumed by skill-side validation |
| 10 | `Run` step: `--model`, `--allowed-tools`, tee, skill-fail guard | Adopts harness reviewer invocation contract |
| 11 | `Verify review was posted` step (new) | Confirms the bot posted before workflow exits |
| 12 | Lint-gate comment block disabled | Matches harness — gate not yet enforced |
| 13 | `name:` quotes removed | Cosmetic |

Hunks adopted as DRIFT (assumed safe). One hunk skipped: harness uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, pinata-reviewer]`; this repo has no `pinata-reviewer` runner label, so `ubuntu-latest` is preserved.

## Risk

`create-github-app-token@v3` renamed the input from `app-id` to `client-id`. If the `MAS_GH_APP_ID` (or equivalent) secret in this repo is registered under `app-id` only — not `client-id` — the next workflow run fails auth. Verify secret name before merge.

## Test

YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`). No removed steps; all changes are step-level config or new steps. Workflow can be dispatched manually after merge to confirm auth.

URL for testing:

- https://chore-sync-pinata-code-review-workflow--mas-pinata--adobecom.aem.page/

body:
## Summary

Adds two new reusable composite actions for F´ CI workflows:

### `build/action.yml`
Generate and build an F´ deployment or module. Inputs:
- `working-directory` — directory to run fprime-util from (default `.`)
- `cmake-args` — extra CMake flags for generate
- `target-platform` — target platform/toolchain (e.g. `native`, `aarch64-linux`)
- `build-all` — pass `--all` to build all modules
- `jobs` — parallel job count: a number, `"random"` (1-32), or empty to omit `-j`

### `run-unit-tests/action.yml`
Generate, build, and run F´ unit tests. Same inputs as build (minus `build-all`) plus `CTEST_OUTPUT_ON_FAILURE=1` for clear diagnostics.

Both actions support three modes for the `jobs` input to help catch implicit build ordering dependencies:
1. **Empty** — omit `-j` entirely (tool default)
2. **A number** — use that exact count
3. **`"random"`** — randomize between 1 and 32 inclusive

These actions are consumed by the new modular CI workflows in [JPL-Devin/fprime#43](https://github.com/JPL-Devin/fprime/pull/43).

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] Verify the action inputs/defaults make sense for your deployment patterns
- [ ] Test by referencing `JPL-Devin/fprime-actions/build@devin/1778027440-build-and-ut-actions` from a workflow to confirm it works end-to-end

### Notes
Follows the existing repo structure (top-level directory per action with `action.yml`). Once merged to `devel`, the fprime workflows can be updated to reference `nasa/fprime-actions/build@devel` and `nasa/fprime-actions/run-unit-tests@devel` instead of local `.github/actions/`.

author: ickshonpe
body: # Objective Support `Overflow` clipping for transformed nodes. Fixes #17630, #21775, #25126 (and probably quite a few others) ## Solution `CalculatedClip` is now an enum with `Rects` and `FullyClipped` variants. `Rects` holds a list of `Rect` in node local coords and `Affine2` world-to-local transform. `bevy_ui_render` has a new `clipping` module with a `clip_polygon` function that intersects UI elements with the clipping rects and chops off the non-visible regions and returns a list of vertices that forms a triangle fan. Uses a simplified version of the Sutherland–Hodgman algorithm. --- - Performance isn't too bad, but text suffers a bit when clipped as there's no broad phase atm, instead it tests and breaks up each glyph individually. The clipping geometry also needs to be cached somewhere and updated incrementally. - I didn't try to optimise this branch too much yet as I suspect the required changes would probably end up being much larger and more complicated than the clipping implementation itself, and it might better to leave them for follow up PRs. - Currently this only supports rectangular clipping regions but it can easily be expanded to support any covex shapes. -- Ideally we'd do clipping on the GPU which would allow for arbitrary clipping geometry and better performance. That would need a complete rewrite of the UI renderer and might have compatibility issues. I think this is good enough as an improving step, it works reliably and the code is also simpler and easier to understand, in particular UV interpolation is much simpler now. ## Testing ``` cargo run --example overflow_transform ``` ``` cargo run --example overflow_transform_debug ``` --- ## Showcase

author: estetika101
body:
Closes #7.

Spec: [`docs/specs/race-end-detection.md`](https://github.com/Estetika101/pacefinderapp/blob/main/docs/specs/race-end-detection.md)

## Summary

Sessions previously closed only via the watchdog's 10s silence timeout — so the post-race UI signal lagged behind the actual finish-line crossing by up to 10 seconds. This PR detects the `is_race_on` 1→0 transition that Forza broadcasts and closes immediately.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `session/manager.py` | New state machine on `Session` (`_last_is_race_on`, `_race_off_streak`, `_should_close_for_race_end`, `closed_reason`). New `_update_race_end_state()` called from end of `ingest()`. |
| `session/protocol.py` | After ingest, check the flag and close the session inline (same state-update sequence as watchdog). |
| `session/watchdog.py` | Tag closes with `closed_reason='timeout'` or `'idle_timeout'` before calling `close()`. |
| `db/store.py` | Add `closed_reason TEXT` column via the existing idempotent migration; include in the INSERT. |
| `config.py` | New tunable: `RACE_END_DETECTION_PACKETS = 30` (≈ 0.5s at 60 Hz). |

## Decision rationale

Spec gave 1–2s as the responsiveness target. Sustained-0 threshold of 30 packets at Forza's 60 Hz UDP rate ≈ 500ms — fast enough, long enough to filter brief blips. The "≥1 completed lap" guard means a session that crashes/disconnects before any lap completes still falls back to the watchdog timeout (correct behavior).

## Pause behavior — flagged as open question

The spec marked it open whether `is_race_on` flips to 0 on **pause** as well as race end. I can't test this empirically without a live Forza session.

Mitigations in place:
- The "≥1 completed lap" guard means in-race pause (where you've already completed laps) could still trigger early close — that's the worst case.
- The 0.5s sustained threshold filters momentary blips.

If pausing during a multi-lap race turns out to flip `is_race_on=0` for extended periods, increase `RACE_END_DETECTION_PACKETS` (e.g., to 120 ≈ 2s) or add a secondary signal check (e.g. `current_race_time` resetting). Both are config tweaks, no rearchitect.

## Verification

- `python3 listener.py` starts cleanly, only Forza port bound
- DB schema migrated: `closed_reason TEXT` column present
- Inline state-machine assertion script (in commit notes) passes:
  - Won't close before racing
  - Won't close without completed laps
  - WILL close on 1→0 sustained 30 packets with completed laps
  - Streak resets when `is_race_on` goes back to 1

## What's NOT in this PR

The actual auto-show post-race modal UI. The current edit modal still requires a manual `Edit` click. The fields the modal will need (#2 weather, #3 tyre compound, expanded #4 track dropdown) come in subsequent PRs in this batch. Once those land, the frontend can poll `/status` for `state.status === "race_ended"` and auto-open the modal.

## 🥞 Stacked PR
Use this [link](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6726/files/6969bb1654212a1831653c58cd90585d3aa9f59a..ef1bab7f557f74801b5f48fd5c904f2d4f912509) to review incremental changes.
- [stack/dsv2-cdf-schema-bypass-message](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6724) [[Files changed](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6724/files)]
  - [stack/dsv2-value-aware-streaming-options](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6725) [[Files changed](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6725/files/52c0d4bd462441ce06d4b20a35490270a154d1c4..6969bb1654212a1831653c58cd90585d3aa9f59a)]
    - [**stack/dsv2-streaming-file-metadata**](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6726) [[Files changed](https://github.com/delta-io/delta/pull/6726/files/6969bb1654212a1831653c58cd90585d3aa9f59a..ef1bab7f557f74801b5f48fd5c904f2d4f912509)]

---------

#### Which Delta project/connector is this regarding?

Spark / V2 streaming reads for Unity Catalog managed Delta tables.

## Description

### CUJ

A user wants the source file path for each row in a streaming query:

```java
spark.readStream()
    .format("delta")
    .table("unity.default.t")
    .selectExpr("id", "_metadata.file_path AS file_path")
    .writeStream()
    .trigger(Trigger.AvailableNow())
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
    .foreachBatch(...)
    .start();
```

A user may also want Delta row tracking metadata:

```java
spark.readStream()
    .format("delta")
    .table("unity.default.t")
    .selectExpr("id", "_metadata.row_id AS row_id")
    .writeStream()
    .trigger(Trigger.AvailableNow())
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
    .foreachBatch(...)
    .start();
```

This is a valid CUJ because `_metadata.file_path` is standard Spark file metadata, and `_metadata.row_id` is Delta row-tracking metadata.

### Problem

For Unity Catalog managed Delta tables, streaming uses the V2 read path.

Before this PR, `_metadata.file_path` failed during analysis:

```text
No such struct field `file_path` in `row_id`, `row_commit_version`
```

The connector only declared Delta row-tracking fields in `_metadata`. It did not declare Spark file metadata fields.

Also, `_metadata.row_id` could resolve, but streaming execution could crash because the streaming read schema did not carry `_metadata` down to the reader.

### Solution

This PR fixes the catalog-managed row-tracking V2 streaming path.

It does three things:

1. Declares Spark file metadata fields in `_metadata` for catalog-managed row-tracking tables.
2. Adds `_metadata` back to the streaming read schema when Spark does not push it down.
3. Populates the metadata struct in the existing row-tracking read function.

This keeps the existing non-managed row-tracking metadata behavior unchanged.

## How was this patch tested?

Verified with:

```text
build/sbt 'sparkUnityCatalog/testOnly io.sparkuctest.UCDeltaTableDataFrameStreamingTest'
build/sbt 'sparkV2/testOnly io.delta.spark.internal.v2.V2RowTrackingReadTest'
```

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing changes?

Yes. V2 streaming reads on Unity Catalog managed Delta tables can now project `_metadata.file_path` and `_metadata.row_id`.

author: kelvinst
body:
## Summary

Expanded the pitch for handling ID allocation conflicts in parallel team workflows. The document now includes a concrete, implementable solution with clear tradeoffs and validation criteria.

## Key Changes

- **Problem statement:** Clarified the root cause — the 3-way merge silently accepts identical `next-id` increments from parallel branches, allowing duplicate IDs to land on `main` without conflict detection. Added a real example from the repo (`id: 19` collision).

- **Solution approach:** Defined a two-layer defense strategy:
  - CI dup-check script that fails on duplicate IDs and enforces branch protection rules
  - `kix dedupe` skill that detects and repairs collisions by renumbering branch artifacts while keeping `main` immutable

- **Design rationale:** Expanded alternatives section covering five different ID schemes (random, namespaced, PR-based, issue-based, date-slug) with explicit tradeoffs. Chose integer IDs + detect-and-repair to preserve memorability while making collisions self-healing.

- **Tiebreaker rule:** Established "main always wins" — when renumbering is needed, the branch's in-flight artifact loses its ID, never `main`'s, since external references (commits, PRs, chat) may already point to IDs on `main`.

- **Rabbit holes & no-gos:** Documented reference rewriting complexity, external reference staleness, and explicit constraints (no ID changes on `main`, no long-form IDs, no network-dependent allocation).

- **Delivery & validation:** Scoped as a small change with concrete test scenarios and a breakdown of implementation tasks.

## Notable Details

- The solution preserves the simple integer ID UX while making the allocator robust through detection and repair rather than prevention
- Branch protection configuration is critical to the correctness of the approach
- The `kix dedupe` skill must handle multiple types of internal references (filename, frontmatter, linked_to, requests array)

body:
## Summary

\`BuildHomeDashboardService#determine_state\` で **Android UA 判定を step_records 判定より先行** させていたため、Capacitor アプリで Health Connect 同期成功してもデモデータが永久表示される設計バグを修正。Issue #158 (= デモ表記のまま) + Issue #159 (= 設定画面導線残る) を 1 PR で同時 close。

## 検証経緯と原因確定

実機スクショの「+294 kcal」が **DemoDataService の今日値と完全一致**:

\`\`\`ruby
# DemoDataService RECENT_7_PATTERN[0] (= 今日)
{ steps: 7_200, distance_meters: 5_400, flights_climbed: 12 }
# estimated_kcal = 7200 * 0.04 + 12 * 0.5 = 294
\`\`\`

→ 「実データが反映されていない」ではなく **「Capacitor アプリではデモデータが強制表示される設計バグ」** と判明。

旧 \`determine_state\`:
\`\`\`ruby
return :guest unless user
platform = PlatformDetectorService.from_request(request)
return :android if platform == :android  # ← データあっても無視
return :iphone_with_data if user.step_records.exists?
:empty
\`\`\`

Capacitor アプリは overrideUserAgent に Android を含むため、**データの有無を見ずに :android 状態が確定** → DemoData 表示。

## 修正

\`app/services/build_home_dashboard_service.rb\`: 1 行順序変更

\`\`\`ruby
return :guest unless user
return :iphone_with_data if user.step_records.exists?  # ← platform 判定より前に
platform = PlatformDetectorService.from_request(request)
return :android if platform == :android
:empty
\`\`\`

## 修正後の優先順位

| ユーザー状態 | state | 表示 |
|---|---|---|
| 未ログイン | \`:guest\` | guest バナー + デモデータ |
| ログイン + step_records あり (= 全 platform 共通) | \`:iphone_with_data\` | バナーなし、**実データ** |
| ログイン + step_records なし + Android UA | \`:android\` | Capacitor 連携誘導バナー + デモ |
| ログイン + step_records なし + iOS/Web UA | \`:empty\` | iOS Shortcut 誘導バナー + デモ |

## v1.1 候補

state 名 \`:iphone_with_data\` は誤称 (= Android user も到達)。リネーム別 PR (= \`:user_with_data\` 等) で対応予定。

## Test plan

- [x] \`bundle exec rspec\`: 519 examples, 0 failures (= 新規 spec 4 件追加)
- [x] \`bundle exec rubocop\`: clean
- [x] 新規回帰防止 spec:
  - 「Android UA + step_records あり → :iphone_with_data」
  - 「records に DB StepRecord 含む (= デモではない)」
  - 「today_record が自分のデータ」
  - 「calorie_savings.this_month が実データ計算 (= 360 kcal)」
- [ ] マージ → Render auto-deploy
- [ ] 実機 (Torque G6) で再ログイン後ホーム画面確認:
  - 「サンプルデータです」表記が消える
  - 「Android アプリ版で連携できます」+「設定を見る」バナーが消える
  - 実データの歩数 / 消費カロリー / グラフが反映

Closes #158
Closes #159

author: miaodx
body:
## What

Adds `crates/robowbc-transport/` — a new wire-level DDS transport crate intended to sit beneath `robowbc-comm`'s higher-level `RobotTransport` API and provide the raw publish / subscribe surface for `unitree_hg` IDL messages over CycloneDDS.

Surface:

- **`Transport`** trait with typed `publish::<T>(topic, msg)` / `subscribe::<T>(topic) -> Subscription<T>`
- **`DdsMessage`** trait wrapping the `unitree-hg-idl` CDR encode/decode + a stable IDL type tag, with impls for `LowCmd`, `LowState`, `MotorCmd`, `MotorState`, `ImuState`, `BmsCmd`, `BmsState`, `HandCmd`, `HandState`
- **`InMemoryTransport`** loopback with per-topic type-tag enforcement, used by tests / examples / FSM mocks
- **`CyclorsTransport`** behind `cyclors-backend` cargo feature: owns a CycloneDDS domain participant via `dds_create_participant`. The publish/subscribe wiring (sertype / topic-descriptor registration for unitree_hg types) is documented in the module header and stubbed to return `TransportError::Native` — three implementation paths (codegen, custom sertype, hand-rolled descriptor) are spelled out for the follow-up
- `crc32_core` re-exported from `unitree-hg-idl`
- Example `pubsub_g1` exercising the `LowState` / `LowCmd` round-trip and CRC32

## Why

Closes #122 (partially — see Acceptance criteria status). This is the foundational issue for Path A: until a Rust-native transport lands, robowbc cannot talk to either `unitree_mujoco` or the real G1 without going through PyO3 + `unitree_sdk2_python`. Even the partial form of the trait + in-memory backend unblocks #126 (FSM) and #129 (CI) for unit-level integration; the cyclors wire-level work is the logical next shift.

## Acceptance criteria status

- [x] `robowbc-transport` crate exposes a `Transport` trait with `subscribe::<T>(topic)` / `publish::<T>(topic, msg)` methods
- [ ] `CyclorsTransport` impl that vendors cyclors via cargo, no system `libcyclonedds` required — **partial**: cyclors is wired in, the participant lifecycle works, but `publish` / `subscribe` for the unitree_hg types is stubbed pending sertype/topic-descriptor registration. See `crates/robowbc-transport/src/cyclors_backend.rs` module docs for the three approaches and concrete TODO.
- [ ] Bench: 500 Hz publish/subscribe loop on `lo` with `domain_id=1` sustains <1ms p99 jitter — **deferred**: cannot run meaningful 500 Hz numbers until the cyclors wire path is complete.
- [ ] Example `cargo run --example pubsub_g1` connects to `unitree_mujoco` — **partial**: example exists and runs end-to-end against the in-memory transport (demonstrates the trait API and CRC32 round-trip); the real `unitree_mujoco` connection waits on the cyclors wire path.
- [ ] CRC32 implementation matches `g1::publisher::LowCmd::Crc32Core` byte-for-byte (validated by sending a known frame and observing motors react) — **partial**: the CRC32 is the one already shipped in `unitree-hg-idl` (#137), unit-tested for shape, but the on-motor validation needs a real / sim G1.
- [x] Cross-compile target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu — verified with default features (`cargo build -p robowbc-transport --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`). The `cyclors-backend` feature additionally requires an aarch64 cmake/cc sysroot, which I did not have available locally.

## Validation performed

All commands run in the sandbox on this branch:

- `cargo build -p robowbc-transport` — pass
- `cargo build -p robowbc-transport --features cyclors-backend` — pass (cyclors vendors CycloneDDS 0.10.x via cmake + cc, ~30s clean build)
- `cargo test -p robowbc-transport --features cyclors-backend` — **12 tests pass**, including a live `dds_create_participant` round trip
- `cargo clippy -p robowbc-transport --all-targets --features cyclors-backend -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt -- --check` — clean (whole repo)
- `cargo build -p robowbc-transport --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` — pass (default features)
- `cargo run -p robowbc-transport --example pubsub_g1` — prints the expected round-trip output

## Notes

- **Pre-existing CI failure on `rust` job**: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on `crates/robowbc-core/src/validator.rs:295` with `clippy::needless_raw_string_hashes`, introduced by #138 (PolicyValidator) and unrelated to this PR. PR #138 was merged with the same `rust` check failing. This PR does **not** include a fix for that issue per the routine's "no bundling" rule — it deserves its own one-line cleanup PR.
- **Crate placement**: I introduced `robowbc-transport` as a new crate per the issue's literal spec, rather than extending the existing `robowbc-comm`. The two operate at different abstraction levels — `robowbc-comm` provides the high-level `JointState` / `JointPositionTargets` / control-loop runner; `robowbc-transport` is the wire-level pub/sub for `unitree_hg` IDL messages. `robowbc-comm` will eventually be refactored to sit on top of `robowbc-transport`, but that's out of scope here.
- **`CyclorsTransport` deferred wiring**: the three implementation paths are documented in `cyclors_backend.rs` module docs. Custom-sertype is the most likely choice (matches `zenoh-bridge-dds`, no extra build deps) but is ~500 LOC of careful unsafe.
- **Foundation-issue / Gate G5 status**: per the auto-PR routine, this is a foundation issue (transport blocks #126, #129, #131, #133, #134) and I cannot run a real integration test against `unitree_mujoco` from the sandbox. **Per the routine, this PR is `[deferred]` and should not auto-merge** — it's drafted for human review, with the in-memory + skeleton portions providing a useful foundation for the next shift.

author: otheruser325
body:
### Motivation
- Centralize scene key strings for safer scene management and reduce duplication across scenes.
- Add class progression so dice stats and skills scale with Class UP levels and surface alternate/transform forms in the UI.
- Make several skill/runtime metadata and damage behaviours explicit (meteor, ice active, sniper/iron/skull adjustments) so class scaling and runtime effects behave consistently.
- Rework Transcendence beam and Death transform flows to consume attacks correctly and apply wide-area beam damage/visuals.

### Description
- Introduced `src/scenes/sceneKeys.ts` and replaced hard-coded scene string keys across scenes (`BootScene`, `MenuScene`, `ArenaScene`, `CasinoScene`, `DiceScene`, `ShopScene`, `SettingsScene`, `AchievementsScene`).
- Added class progression system (`src/systems/ClassProgression.ts`) with multiplicative stat scaling, per-class skill tweaks (Skull revive chance, Sniper distance rate, Iron current HP bonus), and exposed `applyClassProgression` used in `ArenaScene` and `DiceScene` to present scaled stats/skills.
- Refactored runtime definition handling in `ArenaScene`: store per-instance class-scaled overrides (`instanceDefinitionOverrides`) and use `getDefinitionForInstance`/`getDefinitionsForCombat` so both stats and skills resolve at the die's class level; removed the old `instanceBaseAttack` approach.
- Implemented Transcendence beam mechanics and visuals: transformations tracked via `transcendenceTransformed`, beam execution via `executeTranscendenceBeam` (consumes 6 attacks, damages row/column including primary target), exhaustion checks, beam animation `animateTranscendenceBeam`, and adjusted combat loop to treat beam vs regular attacks separately.
- Extended skill metadata and types (`src/systems/DiceSkills.ts`, `src/types/game.ts`) to support new fields (`activeDamage`, `meteorDamage`, `lavaDamage`, `beamDamage`, `targetCurrentHpBonusRate`, `distanceDamageBonusRatePerTile`, etc.) and updated damage resolution to include current-HP-based bonuses and distance-rate bonuses.
- Made skill-driven active effects configurable via metadata (Ice active damage, Meteor strike & lava damage), updated the meteor/lava and ice behaviors in `ArenaScene` to use metadata values.
- UI/UX updates: Dice modal can toggle alternate forms for `Death` and `Transcendence`, DiceScene shows class-scaled stats/skill descriptions, status labels/colors support transformed Transcendence, small text/label tweaks in Casino and Menu themes.
- Bug fix in `src/systems/BattleState.ts` to restore revived target's `attacksRemaining` and `hasFinishedAttacking` to the pre-destruction values when revive triggers.
- Updated several JSON dice definitions (`public/gamedata/DiceDefinitions/*.dice`) to include the new modifier fields and more explicit notes for runtime parsing.

### Testing
- Performed a TypeScript type-check (`tsc --noEmit`) and a development build (`npm run build`) against the changed codebase; both completed successfully.
- Ran a quick automated dev build smoke test that compiles client assets and starts the dev server; build/start succeeded (no automated unit tests were added in this change).

### Context

This is a slimmed resubmit of #103717 — itself a takeover of @Avogar's stalled #102890 — per @alexey-milovidov's directive on #103717 (`the diff is too large. Keep only the relevant changes.`).

While preparing this resubmit, I noticed that the actual `.cpp` fix from #102890 is no longer needed: the **duplicate-fractional-separator** bug in `parseDateTimeBestEffort` was fixed on master by @yariks5s's #103773 (merged 2026-04-30 by @alexey-milovidov). Both fixes use the same approach (a boolean `has_fractional*` flag that errors on the second `.` after the fractional part has been opened).

The only remaining "relevant change" from #102890 is the **expanded test coverage**: 3 inputs × 3 function variants (strict / OrNull / OrZero) versus the single-case test on master (`tests/queries/0_stateless/04143_ub_parsing_datetime.sql`). So this PR adds **only** those tests.

### Tests added

`tests/queries/0_stateless/04101_parseDateTime64BestEffort_double_dot_fractional.{sql,reference}`:

- `'12:34:56..123'` (double dot directly)
- `'12:34:56.123.456'` (extra dot after fractional)
- `'12:34:56.123456789012345678.987654321'` (long fractional + dot)

Each validated against `parseDateTime64BestEffort` (strict), `parseDateTime64BestEffortOrNull`, and `parseDateTime64BestEffortOrZero`. All three currently pass on `master` HEAD `bc39c42c123e` against the locally-built debug binary (errors throw `CANNOT_PARSE_DATETIME` on strict, `\N` / `1970-01-01 00:00:00.000` on OrNull / OrZero).

Tests originally authored by @Avogar in #102890. The takeover workflow follows @alexey-milovidov's directive on #102890 (2026-04-29). Test files imported as-is; commit carries `Co-authored-by:` for @Avogar and @nihalzp (who reviewed the wording on the now-redundant `.cpp` fix).

author: nwparker
body:
## Problem

When ProjectV2 calls fail with `scope_missing`, Orca tells the user to run:

```
gh auth refresh -s project -s read:org -s repo
```

But that command **silently no-ops** when `GITHUB_TOKEN` (or `GH_TOKEN`) is exported in the user's shell — `gh` prefers env tokens and refuses to refresh them, exiting 0 with only a warning. Users follow the canned remediation, see no error, retry, and stay stuck.

Reproduced locally:

```
$ gh auth refresh -s project -s read:org -s repo
The value of the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable is being used for authentication.
To refresh credentials stored in GitHub CLI, first clear the value from the environment.
$ echo $?
0
```

## Fix

New `gh:diagnoseAuth` IPC that probes `gh auth status` and the Electron process env, then a tailored remediation UI for each detected cause:

- **Env-shadowed token** (the case that triggered this report): Tells the user `gh auth refresh` cannot modify env-supplied tokens, gives platform-specific commands to find where `GITHUB_TOKEN` is exported and how to unset it, and notes whether their keyring already has a fallback login.
- **gh CLI not installed**: Link to cli.github.com.
- **Plain missing scope** on a keyring login: Original refresh advice (which actually works in this case).
- **Scopes look fine but still denied**: SAML SSO authorization guidance.

Replaces the single canned "Copy command" button with one button per remediation step.

### Cross-platform

Per AGENTS.md, the env-var commands branch on `navigator.userAgent`:

- macOS/Linux: `grep -RIn ...`, `unset GITHUB_TOKEN`
- Windows: `Get-ChildItem Env:GITHUB_TOKEN`, `Remove-Item Env:GITHUB_TOKEN; [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('GITHUB_TOKEN', $null, 'User')`

Docs button uses `window.api.shell.openUrl` (matching SidebarToolbar) instead of `window.open`.

## Files

- `src/main/github/auth-diagnose.ts` — `gh auth status` parser + diagnosis
- `src/main/github/auth-diagnose.test.ts` — 6 tests including real env-shadow output, multi-host (github.com + GHES), and missing-header recovery
- `src/shared/github-auth-types.ts` — typed result
- `src/main/ipc/github.ts`, `src/preload/index.ts`, `src/preload/api-types.ts` — IPC wiring
- `src/renderer/src/components/github-project/GhAuthErrorHelp.tsx` — new error UI component (block + banner variants)
- `ProjectViewWrapper.tsx`, `ProjectPicker.tsx` — use it

## Test plan

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx vitest run src/main/github/`: 77 tests pass (10 files).
- `npx oxlint` on touched files: 0 errors.
- Manually verified `parseAuthStatus` against the real `gh auth status` output that surfaced the bug (env-shadowed GITHUB_TOKEN + keyring fallback).

author: rymu219
body:
## Summary

Railway watcher build was failing on every push to master since #11/#12 with:

> Set a start command to tell Railway how to run this Python application. Railpack detected Python and uv but could not auto-detect a start command because the project does not use a recognized framework (FastAPI, Flask, Django, FastHTML) and has no main.py or app.py in the project root.

Stale prior build kept serving while new ones failed.

## Why it broke

- Repo root `pyproject.toml` has the runner deps (acme/pandas/databento/signalrcore) — but **not** fastapi/uvicorn, so Railpack scanning the root didn't detect FastAPI.
- The watcher's actual deps + Procfile live in `web/` (slim: just fastapi, uvicorn, supabase, python-dotenv).
- The Railway service's "Root Directory" setting was `null`, so Railpack scanned the repo root instead of `web/`.

## Fix

`railpack.json` at the repo root that:
- `pip install -r web/requirements.txt` (slim, just the watcher deps)
- Starts `uvicorn app:app --app-dir web --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`

This keeps the watcher image small (no pandas / acme / databento) and doesn't depend on the dashboard "Root Directory" setting, which apparently can be reset.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → Railway auto-deploys
- [ ] Build succeeds (no "No start command detected")
- [ ] `/health` returns `{"ok": true}`
- [ ] `/?token=...` shows the v3 fleet overview from PR #12 (5 panels + paginated trades)

author: copilot
body:
`slytrans.com` (bare domain) points to Vercel, which only serves `/api/*` functions — not static HTML. Any non-API path hit Vercel with no matching route and returned 404. The actual frontend lives on GitHub Pages at `www.slytrans.com`.

## Change

- **`vercel.json`** — prepend a host-conditional catch-all 301 before all other rules:

```json
{
  "source": "/(.*)",
  "has": [{ "type": "host", "value": "slytrans.com" }],
  "destination": "https://www.slytrans.com/$1",
  "permanent": true
}
```

Covers all paths (not just the one that surfaced the issue), preserving the full path on redirect so bookmarks and deep links continue to work.

body:
### Motivation
- Saving `searchKeySets` used an IMT-prefilter instead of the final intersection of all active additional-access rule groups, causing mismatches between UI "Доступні карточки" and saved backend payload size.
- Diagnostics/toasts displayed intermediate prefilter counts (e.g. IMT) rather than actual payload users, misleading debugging output.
- The `imt` virtual field must not be written into `searchKeySets` while still participating in filtering logic.

### Description
- Added helper utilities in `src/utils/newUsersFilterSetsIndex.js`: `collectUniqueUserIds`, `countBuckets`, `countRecords`, `intersectUserIdSets`, `collectSearchKeyUserIdsForBuckets`, and `buildFilteredSearchKeySet` to compute final payloads and metrics from the `searchKey` file.
- Reworked `buildRuleBucketWrites` to compute `rawBucketMap`, collect per-field allowed user-id sets, compute `finalAllowedUserIds` as the intersection of prefilter, per-field sets and IMT-derived users, and produce `filteredSearchKeySet` from `finalAllowedUserIds` instead of using `imtAllowedUserIds` alone.
- Build Firebase `writes` from `filteredSearchKeySet` (skipping `imt` buckets), keep remove-then-set write ordering, and compute `aggregatedUserIds` from the actual `set` payloads.
- Added pre-save validation that compares `collectUniqueUserIds(filteredSearchKeySet).size` to `finalAllowedCount` and throws a `SEARCH_KEY_SET_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` error on mismatch to avoid saving inconsistent payloads.
- Extended debug metadata (`debugInfo` / `debug.lastSetDebug`) with `finalAllowedCount`, `imtAllowedCount`, `ageAllowedCount`, `payloadUsers`, `payloadBuckets`, and `payloadRecords` so diagnostics reflect the actual saved payload.
- Updated UI diagnostics in `src/components/ProfileForm.jsx` to use the new debug fields and show `finalAllowed`, `payloadUsers`, `payloadRecords` and to display the mismatch error message when it occurs.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test -- --watchAll=false` and all test suites passed (`16` suites, `73` tests total, all passing).
- Ran `npm run lint:js` and the linter completed successfully (reported browserslist update notice but no lint errors).

body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL

💡 **Vulnerability:**
The application stored master PINs for all user roles (`cashier`, `chef`, `admin`, `service`) in plaintext within the `js/app.js` file.

🎯 **Impact:**
Any user or attacker with access to the frontend could easily discover these credentials using Browser Developer Tools (F12) or by viewing the source code. This allowed full unauthorized access to sensitive POS features, including revenue reports, order history, and database administration.

🔧 **Fix:**
- Implemented a secure hashing mechanism using the **Web Crypto API** (`crypto.subtle.digest` with SHA-256).
- Replaced the plaintext `CREDENTIALS` object with a secured `app._AUTH_HASHES` property containing pre-calculated hashes.
- Converted the `login` function to `async` to handle cryptographic operations.
- Added a runtime check for `window.crypto.subtle` to ensure the security features only operate in secure contexts (HTTPS/Localhost).

✅ **Verification:**
- **Automated Testing:** Ran a Playwright test suite that mocked the Firebase SDK and verified that correct PINs successfully grant access while incorrect PINs are rejected with the appropriate security alert.
- **Security Audit:** Performed a recursive `grep` across the codebase to ensure no plaintext PINs ('1234', 'admin123', etc.) remain in the source.
- **Journaling:** Recorded critical security learnings in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: benitogf
body:
## Summary
Closes #53 by documenting the memory-layer aliasing contract instead of paying to defend against it at runtime.

## Why this changed shape mid-PR
The original commit cloned the object and its `Data` slice on `Set`, `Get`, and `GetList` so the store and caller buffers were fully independent. Benchmarks against realistic payload sizes showed the cost was steep on the hot read path:

| Operation | Payload | Before (main) | With clones | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Get` | 100 B | 37 ns | 104 ns | +180% |
| `Get` | 1 KB | 47 ns | 317 ns | +570% |
| `Get` | 10 KB | 39 ns | 2.7 µs | ~70× |
| `GetList(20)` | 10 KB | 1.1 µs | 43 µs | ~40× |

Direct callers of `Storage.Set` / `Get` / `GetList` are being phased out in favour of the typed `io.*` helpers, which sidestep aliasing by construction (`json.Marshal` / `json.Unmarshal` copy at the boundary, so the stored bytes never escape):

- `io.Set` / `io.Push` / `io.Patch`: marshal a typed value into a fresh buffer; nobody else holds those bytes.
- `io.Get` / `io.GetList`: unmarshal into a typed `T`; the returned `client.Meta[T]` carries the typed value, not raw `Data`.
- `io.Patch` additionally feeds the merge through `merge.MergeBytes`, which is non-mutating on its inputs.

For an internal-network deployment with controlled callers, paying ~70× on Get to defend a path with no current at-risk caller wasn't worth it.

## What this PR does instead
- Documents the aliasing contract on `MemoryLayer`, `MemoryLayer.Set`, `MemoryLayer.Get`, `MemoryLayer.GetList` so a future reader sees the constraint and the recommended path.
- Names the io.\* helpers as the preferred API for new callers.
- No behavior change; no perf change.

## Test plan
- [ ] Full test suite passes under `-race`.
- [ ] No new tests — there is no behavior change. The earlier isolation tests have been removed since they would assert a contract this PR explicitly declines to enforce.

## Summary Reps add notes after most calls. Until now that meant: open detail → click "Add Note" → modal opens → type → save → modal closes → list refreshes. Six steps for what should be two. Composes with Wave 11 (instant render via handoff) and Wave 14 (background revalidate) — **instant read + inline write = full read/write flow on the customer page without modals**. ## What ships **\`customer.html\`** - Replaced the panel header's "Add Note" button with an inline quick-add panel: persistent textarea + Send button + status indicator. Always visible, always ready. - **New \`window.quickAddNote()\`**: - Reads textarea, validates, locks the form during save. - **Optimistic prepend**: temp card appears at the top of the notes list with "Saving…" footer the moment the rep clicks Send. Real card replaces it after Firestore returns. - Same payload shape as \`window.saveNote\` (the modal's existing handler) — same collection, same fields, no schema drift. - On success: clears textarea, flashes "Saved ✓" for 1.8s, reloads notes from source, refreshes the Timeline panel. - On failure: removes the optimistic card, **restores the typed text** so the rep doesn't lose what they wrote, shows "Save failed — try again" inline + toast. - **Cmd/Ctrl+Enter** inside the textarea fires save (delegated \`keydown\` on document so it works even after re-renders). - The modal-based flow stays available via a small "Open larger editor" link in the panel header — useful for multi-paragraph notes. No behavioral change to \`saveNote()\` itself. - Updated empty-state copy: *"No notes yet — type one above and hit Send"* (was a button that opened the now-secondary modal). ## Test plan - [ ] Open a customer detail page → notes panel shows the inline textarea always visible. - [ ] Type a note + click Send → temp card appears immediately + textarea clears + "Saved ✓" flashes + real card replaces temp within ~500ms. - [ ] Cmd+Enter (Mac) / Ctrl+Enter (Win) submits the note. - [ ] Empty textarea + Send → input gets focus, no save attempt. - [ ] Network failure / Firestore error → temp card removes, typed text restored to textarea, error toast. - [ ] Multi-line note (Shift+Enter for newlines) → \n preserved as
in the saved card. - [ ] Click "Open larger editor" → modal still works for multi-paragraph entries. - [ ] Notes persist after page reload (same Firestore collection as before). - [ ] Timeline tab shows the new note after each save (same behavior as the modal flow).

author: takashiaihara
body:
## 概要 / Why

items は group 内の品目マスタ (stocks の親)。本 Issue では手動入力経路だけを実装する。バーコード経由の自動 find-or-create は `packages/jan-api` 完成後に別 Issue (UC-02) で扱う。

## 変更内容 / What

### `/v1/items` (5 endpoint)

- `POST /v1/items` body: `{ groupId, name, categoryId?, defaultUnit?, manufacturer?, memo?, barcode? }`
  - `productMasterId` は本 endpoint では指定不可（強制 null）
- `GET /v1/items?groupId=...&categoryId=...&barcode=...` 一覧（categoryId / barcode で絞り込み可、name 昇順）
- `GET /v1/items/:id`
- `PATCH /v1/items/:id` name / categoryId / defaultUnit / manufacturer / memo / barcode を更新可
- `DELETE /v1/items/:id` soft delete。active な子 stock 参照ありなら 422 `ITEM_IN_USE`

### 認可
- 一覧は `withGroupAccess` (query.groupId)
- 単件系・編集系は handler 内 `checkGroupAccess` (path.id 経由で resource.groupId 解決)
- 編集系 (POST / PATCH / DELETE) は EDITOR 以上必須

### バリデーション
- **barcode 重複チェック**: 同じ `(groupId, barcode)` の active item が既に存在したら 422 `ITEM_BARCODE_DUPLICATE`。DB 側に `(group_id, barcode) WHERE product_master_id IS NULL AND barcode IS NOT NULL` の uniqueIndex があるが、明示的に事前 check してわかりやすいエラーを返す
- **cross-group categoryId**: `categoryId` 指定時は同 group の category かを `assertCategoryInGroup` で検証、不整合なら 422 `CATEGORY_GROUP_MISMATCH`

### スキーマ
- `routes/schemas.ts` に `itemDtoSchema` + create/update body schema 追加
- ISO string + plain UUID で API 境界統一 (branded type は内部のみ)

### E2E (`items.test.ts` 11 case)
- CRUD ハッピーパス + 認可エラー (非 member / VIEWER) + barcode duplicate + cross-group categoryId + active stock cascade block + soft-deleted 取得 404

## 設計判断

- **手動 items は productMasterId なし** で固定。バーコード経路を別 Issue で導入する際、productMasterId を後付けする余地を残す
- **DELETE cascade ルールは locations / categories / items すべて統一**: active な子参照ありなら 422 で blocked
- **categoryId 変更は許可**（品目の分類変更は運用でよくある）
- **PATCH の barcode 重複チェック** は productMasterId が null の item のみが uniqueIndex のスコープ内なので、`existing.productMasterId == null` の条件で限定

## スコープ外 / Out of scope

- バーコード経由の find-or-create 作成（UC-02 / `packages/jan-api` 連動で別 Issue）
- 商品マスタ (`productMasters`) との連結ロジック
- 画像アップロード

## 検証 / Test plan

- [x] `bun --filter @prep-hamster/api typecheck`
- [x] `bun --filter @prep-hamster/api test:e2e` → 47 pass / 0 fail (うち 11 が #71)
- [x] `bun x oxlint apps/core/api/src apps/core/api/e2e` → 0 errors
- [x] `bun x oxfmt --check apps/core/api/src apps/core/api/e2e` → ok

## 関連 Issue / Links

- Closes #71
- Base: #81 (#70 locations/categories CRUD)
- Depends on: #67 (#79), #69 (#80), #70 (#81)

## チェックリスト

- [x] PR タイトルが Conventional Commits に従っている
- [x] 関連 Issue を `Closes #N` でリンクしている
- [x] CI（Typecheck / Test）が通っている
- [x] スコープ外の変更を含めていない

author: cozmogeek
body: - add the ability to create a prioritized list of satellites and transmitters to monitor. - drag and drop or click up and down arrows to change priority. - add a satellite to the monitored list by right clicking in the satellite list. This will add the currently selected sat and the selected transmitter to the monitored list. - checkboxes to record audio or I/Q files for the monitored passes (or you can just let an external program process the audio going through your virtual audio cable. - check the Auto box in the monitored satellites panel to enable auto tuning. - big yellow box in the menu bar warning you that auto tuning is turned on. - skyroof will automatically change to the previously selected transmitter during a pass. If a higher priority satellite begins a pass while one is in progress it will change to the higher priority satellite. The elevation slider determines how high a pass on a higher priority sat needs to be in order to change from an in progress pass. So it won't change from a good pass to a low one just because the new sat is higher priority. - audio files saved in the recordings directory with filenames like "2026-05-06_03_56_04Z_AO-7_14deg.wav" so that's the UTC timestamp, satellite name, and the max elevation of the recorded pass. This does not support rotators yet. Rotator tracking gets turned off when the current satellite is changed. I will have a rotator very soon and can make an implementation for that too. Currently it is supposed to park the rotator between passes. Feel free to clean it up or tweak it however necessary. Maybe up and down arrows and a trash icon instead of text buttons.

author: copilot
body:
MPCP runtime had drift across multiple layers: valid states were inconsistently defined in each module, `CAUSE→ACTION→RESULT` chain was broken on halt paths, trace entries carried no context snapshot, and ROT's fail condition check was a no-op.

## Changes

### `kernel/contract.py`
- Replaced hardcoded `["SUCCESS", "WAIT", "STOP"]` with `VALID_STATES` frozenset covering all 10 spec states: `idle ready run wait done warn block fail STOP SUCCESS`
- Removed duplicate `SYSTEM_NAME` — now imported from `system.py`
- `validate_output()` rejects `fail` state without `error` field

### `kernel/rot.py`
- `validate_fail_condition()` was a no-op; now enforces that halt states (`STOP`, `fail`, `block`) must carry an `error` field for ROT traceability

### `runtime/executor.py`
- All `mpcp_trace()` calls now pass `env=data` so every trace entry carries a context snapshot
- `to_mpcp_output()` extended to map all 10 states to color/sym (was: only 3 states, everything else collapsed to Red/STOP)
- `MODEW_NOT_FOUND` and fail-safe results now include `cause` (the task name)
- `data = {}` pre-init documented: guarantees `cause` is capturable even when `parse_mpcp()` itself raises

### `modew/base_modew.py`
- `run()` captures `cause = context.get("TASK")` and includes it in both `SUCCESS` and `STOP` results — completes the `CAUSE→ACTION→RESULT` chain at the Modew level

### `orchestrator/manager.py`
- Replaced local `["SUCCESS", "WAIT", "STOP"]` check with `VALID_STATES` from contract (single source of truth)
- Defined explicit flow-control groups:
  - **continue**: `SUCCESS`, `done`
  - **pause**: `WAIT`, `wait`
  - **warn+continue**: `warn`
  - **halt**: `STOP`, `fail`, `block`
  - **unexpected lifecycle state** (`idle`, `ready`, `run` as final result) → `_stop()` with traceable error
- `_stop()` and `_response()` now include `cause` for flow-level trace linkage

### `runtime_sanity_sweep.py` *(new)*
75-check sweep covering all audit categories: VALID_STATES coverage, ROT halt enforcement, executor cause traceability, fail-safe structure, BaseModew CAUSE→ACTION→RESULT, `to_mpcp_output` color map completeness, and Modew boundary (invalid state rejected by contract).

```python
# Before: warn/done/fail/block silently rejected by contract
MPCPContract.validate_output({"state": "warn"})  # raised ValueError

# Before: STOP result had no cause
run("TASK:unknown")  # → {"state": "STOP", "error": "MODEW_NOT_FOUND:unknown"}

# After
run("TASK:unknown")  # → {"state": "STOP", "cause": "unknown", "error": "MODEW_NOT_FOUND:unknown"}
```

author: copilot
body:
All comparison results (total cap, resistance, coupling cap) now flow exclusively through `PlotData` for both CLI and GUI, eliminating a parallel set of C++ structs/functions and Python dataclasses that had accumulated as unused "recommendations."

## C++ removals (`spef_core.h` / `spef_core.cpp` / `wrapper.cpp`)
- **Removed structs**: `ResistanceResult`, `CorrelationResult`, `CapComparisonData`, `ResComparisonData`, `CouplingCapComparison`, `ComparisonResult`, `ComparisonChunk`
- **Removed from `NetData`**: `node_prefix_map`, `pin_to_node_cache`, `pin_map_built`
- **Removed functions**: `compare_spef_full`, `summarize_comparison`, `compare_coupling_caps`, `compare_spef_chunk`, `compare_spef_streaming`, `build_pin_to_node_map`, `compute_batch_driver_sink_resistances`
- **`compute_pearson_correlation`**: simplified to return `double`, made `static` (internal linkage)
- **Coupling-cap comparison merged into `export_plot_data`** — `PlotData` now populates `ccap_*` fields in the same pass as cap/res

## Python removals (`spef_rc_correlation.py`)
- **Removed dataclasses**: `CapComparison`, `ResComparison`, `CouplingCapComparison`, `NetRC`
- **Removed wrapper functions**: `compare_spef_cpp`, `compare_spef_with_coupling_cpp`, `compare_coupling_caps_cpp`, `compare_spef_cpp_objs`, `parse_net_*_data`, `write_*_csv`
- **GUI**: dropped `_data_caps`, `_data_ress`, `_data_coupling_caps` — all plot/filter logic reads directly from `_cpp_result` (`PlotData`)
- **CLI**: both SPEF-pair mode and data-file mode now call `export_plot_data` / `create_plot_data_from_files` directly; no Python-side conversion loop

## Before / After

**Before** — three separate code paths:
```python
caps, ress, coupling_caps, top10_cap, top10_res = compare_spef_with_coupling_cpp(s1, s2)
# ... convert each to Python dataclass lists, write separately
```

**After** — single call, single object:
```python
plot_data = spef_core.export_plot_data(s1._cpp_spef, s2._cpp_spef, threads, res_method)
# plot_data.cap_*, plot_data.res_*, plot_data.ccap_* all populated
```

author: chelojimenez
body:
## Summary
Brings local Inspector (CLI / `--ui`) onto the same Convex-backed authorization path hosted uses, so server configs (STDIO + env included) and OAuth credentials live in Convex instead of being trusted from the client / localStorage.

**Server (`/api/mcp/*`)**
- New `server/utils/local-server-resolver.ts` — calls Convex `/web/authorize-batch-local` with the user's bearer, maps the response to an `MCPServerConfig` (with OAuth header injection), threads the server-side log context.
- `/api/mcp/connect` and `/api/mcp/servers/reconnect` accept the new `{projectId, serverId}` shape and resolve config server-side. Legacy `{serverConfig, serverId}` body is retained as a fallback during the client migration.

**Client**
- Drop `HOSTED_MODE` short-circuits in `shouldRetryHostedAuth401`, `hasHostedGuestAccess`, `getHostedAuthorizationHeader`, `authFetch`'s 401 retry, and `use-hosted-api-context`. Bearer / 401 retry / form-save are now mode-agnostic.
- Add `tryResolveProjectServer` — opt into the new request shape when the API context has both `projectId` and a Convex `serverId`, fall back to legacy otherwise.
- Unify the form-save Convex sync branch so both modes `await` the sync; OAuth in either mode now requires a Convex `serverId`.
- `testConnection` / `reconnectServer` accept optional `{projectId, serverName}` and emit the new body shape when present.
- Include `env` in `serializeServersForSharing`.

**Migration**
- One-time localStorage → Convex migration for legacy local installs: reads `mcp-inspector-projects` / `mcp-inspector-workspaces` / `mcp-inspector-state`, pushes each project + servers to Convex via `projects:createProject`, clears legacy keys + per-server OAuth keys. OAuth tokens are **not** migrated — users re-auth on first connect post-migration. Gated by `mcp-inspector-migrated-to-convex` flag; skipped in `HOSTED_MODE`.

Pairs with mcpjam-backend PR #215 which adds `/web/authorize-batch-local`. **Do not merge before that PR is deployed.**

## Test plan
- [ ] `bun test` passes (`mcpjam-inspector/server/routes/mcp/__tests__/{connect,servers}.test.ts` and `mcpjam-inspector/client/src/lib/__tests__/local-state-migration.test.ts` updated)
- [ ] `bun run typecheck`
- [ ] Local CLI (`bun run dev` + `--ui`):
  - [ ] Sign in with WorkOS, create an HTTP MCP server, connect — works end-to-end
  - [ ] Create a STDIO server with `env` vars, connect — env vars reach the spawned process
  - [ ] Create an OAuth-required HTTP server, complete the OAuth dance, reconnect — token comes from Convex, not localStorage
  - [ ] Sign out, run as guest — guest path still works (same `/web/guest-session` flow)
- [ ] Hosted (`HOSTED_MODE`):
  - [ ] Existing hosted flows unchanged (HTTP-only, HTTPS-required, share/chatbox tokens still work)
  - [ ] Confirm hosted does **not** call `/web/authorize-batch-local`
- [ ] Migration:
  - [ ] Fresh install with no legacy localStorage — migration is a no-op, flag gets set
  - [ ] Install with legacy `mcp-inspector-projects` populated — projects + servers appear in Convex, legacy keys cleared, OAuth keys cleared, OAuth servers prompt for re-auth on first connect

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core auth/token-handling and the `/api/mcp/*` connection flow to resolve server configs via Convex, plus adds a one-time localStorage→Convex migration; mistakes could break connectivity or leak/withhold credentials. Also tightens when/where the Convex bearer is attached, so regressions could cause unexpected 401/403s or failed OAuth flows.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Unifies local and hosted Inspector connection/auth flows around Convex-resolved server config.** Local `/api/mcp/connect` and `/api/mcp/servers/reconnect` now accept a new `{projectId, serverId, serverName}` request shape and resolve full server config (including STDIO and OAuth bearer injection) server-side via a new `local-server-resolver`, while keeping the legacy `{serverConfig, serverId}` body as a transitional fallback.
> 
> **Makes bearer/session handling mode-agnostic and safer.** `getHostedAuthorizationHeader`/401-retry logic is no longer gated by `HOSTED_MODE`, `authFetch` only attaches the Convex bearer to an allowlisted set of paths and trusted origins (incl. `*.convex.site`), and 401 retries are skipped when responses are flagged `X-MCP-Auth-Required: oauth`.
> 
> **Adds a one-time migration from legacy localStorage state to Convex.** A new `useLocalStateMigration` hook runs on app boot (non-hosted only) to push legacy projects/servers into Convex, with cross-tab lease + bounded retries, progress tracking for partial failures, and updated serialization that preserves secrets for persistence while still redacting them for sharing.
>

### Motivation

- Allow the SDK to detect and react to server-side API error codes returned in HTTP responses so listeners can stop futile retry loops.
- Surface the last API-level error from an HTTP request via the HTTP client so callers can make policy decisions.

### Description

- Add API error string constants `PORTILLIA_API_ERROR_*` to `include/portillia/types/types.h` for known server error codes.
- Add a `last_error_code` field to `struct portillia_http_client` and expose `portillia_http_client_last_error_code()` in `include/portillia/sdk/api_client.h`.
- Parse the response envelope in `http_json()` and store the `error.code` string into `client->last_error_code`, clearing it before each request and freeing it on destroy.
- Update the listener main loop in `src/sdk/listener.c` to consult `portillia_http_client_last_error_code()` and break out of the registration retry loop when the error is `EPROTO` or one of the fatal API errors (`feature_unavailable`, `transport_mismatch`, `hostname_conflict`, `ip_banned`).

author: kxlahsimx09
body:
## Summary

- `createWorktree` (`src/commands/shared/wake-session.ts`) now passes an explicit starting-point to `git worktree add`, resolved as `origin/HEAD` (typically `origin/main`) with a best-effort `git fetch origin --quiet` first.
- Falls back to the prior behavior (no starting-point = primary worktree's HEAD) if `origin/HEAD` isn't configured.

## Why

When the primary worktree is parked on a stale feature branch from a prior session — the common case after any agent finishes a W1 pass without someone manually `git checkout main` — every `maw wake` spawned a new worktree branched from that stale tip.

Observed in `mb-next-payment-gateway`:

```
primary  → a526082 [architect/w1-refine-adr-4c-deposit-auto-expire-2026-04-29]   ← week-old
main     → c60703f (post §ADR-4d amendment merge)
origin/main → c60703f
```

Architects opening W1 on a freshly-spawned worktree saw week-old commits and had to recreate the branch from main before doing useful work. Repeats every wake.

## Behavior

| Repo state | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/HEAD` set, online | branch from primary HEAD (often stale) | branch from fetched `origin/<default>` |
| `origin/HEAD` set, offline | branch from primary HEAD | branch from local `origin/<default>` (best available) |
| `origin/HEAD` not set | branch from primary HEAD | branch from primary HEAD (unchanged) |
| No `origin` remote | branch from primary HEAD | branch from primary HEAD (unchanged) |

Cost per wake: +1 `symbolic-ref` (ms) + 1 `fetch origin --quiet` (1-3 sec, network-bound, non-fatal).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/wake.test.ts` — 6/6 pass
- [x] `bun build src/cli.ts --target=bun` — clean
- [ ] Manual: in a repo with stale primary HEAD, `maw wake` and verify new worktree starts on `origin/main` tip
- [ ] Manual: offline run still completes (uses local `origin/<default>` if known, falls back to HEAD otherwise)
- [ ] Manual: repo without `origin/HEAD` configured still works (regression check)

`createWorktree` isn't covered by an isolated unit test today; new behavior is observable end-to-end via `maw wake`. If you want I can add a fixture-based test in a follow-up.
