## Summary

Five bug fixes for 2.9.1, each its own commit, all with tests. Issues surfaced via a Codex code review pass.

## Fixes

| # | Bug | Location |
|---|-----|----------|
| 1 | `set_pin_async` leaks old PIN into connection-wide headers (every subsequent request carries it) | `async_home.py:570-576` |
| 2 | SSL verification cannot be disabled — `_get_verify(enforce_ssl=False, ssl_context=None)` falls through to `return True` (REST + websocket) | `rest_connection.py`, `connection_url_resolver.py`, `websocket_handler.py` |
| 3 | `Buckets.wait_and_take` race — concurrent callers can oversubscribe the rate-limit bucket because the check + decrement isn't lock-protected (unlike `take()`) | `buckets.py:32-49` |
| 4 | `_get_functionalHomes` accumulates duplicates on repeated state updates for unknown solution types — only the known-type path deduped by solution | `async_home.py:361-381` |
| 5 | README example pattern `Home(); set_auth_token(...); init(...)` fails because `set_auth_token` calls `_connection.update_connection_context` before the connection exists | `README.md:294-298` |

## Tests

275 tests pass (8 new). Each fix commit includes its regression test:

- Bug 1: assertion in `test_set_pin` that the connection's persistent headers don't contain `PIN` after `set_pin` returns
- Bug 2: 6 new unit tests covering all `enforce_ssl` × `ssl_context` combinations for both `_get_verify` callsites
- Bug 3: concurrency test, 5 parallel `wait_and_take` callers on a 5-token bucket, asserts all succeed and bucket is exactly empty
- Bug 4: regression test that two consecutive state loads produce the same `functionalHomes` count
- Bug 5: doc-only, no test

## Changelog

Entry added under `[UNRELEASED]`.

## Other

Codex also flagged dead state (`websocket_reconnect_on_error`, `onWsError`, `WebsocketHandler.url`), API typing gaps, and a "no-op before init" friendliness issue with WS callback setters; saved for 2.10.0 since they touch the public surface.

## Summary
The v2.12.0 release tarball was unusable as an npm dependency because I used a manual `tar -czf` instead of `npm pack`. npm expects all package contents under a `package/` directory at the tarball root; my flat tarball put `dist/`, `package.json`, etc. at the top, so `npm install <url>.tgz` failed with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../package.json'`.

body:
# feat(mobile): Launch polish — accessibility, safe-area insets, responsive layout

## Overview

Pre-launch polish pass covering three areas: **accessibility annotations** across all interactive elements, **safe-area bottom insets** so FABs and scroll content never clip under the iOS home indicator or Android gesture bar, and **responsive layout fixes** so the app handles orientation changes and split-screen correctly. Also includes a dead-file cleanup.

---

## Accessibility

Added `accessibilityRole`, `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityState`, and `accessibilityHint` to every interactive element that was missing them, following WCAG 2.1 AA and Apple/Google VoiceOver/TalkBack guidelines.

### `LoginScreen`
- SSO `TouchableOpacity`: `accessibilityRole="button"`, dynamic label (`"Authenticating, please wait"` while loading / `"Login with CSULB SSO"` otherwise), `accessibilityState={{ disabled: isLoading }}`

### `OnboardingScreen`
- Skip button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Skip onboarding"`
- Progress dot bar: `accessibilityRole="progressbar"`, `accessibilityLabel="Slide X of 4"`; individual dots marked `accessible={false}` (decorative)
- CTA button: dynamic label (`"Get started"` on last slide / `"Next slide"` otherwise)

### `ForceUpdateScreen`
- Restored from git history (file was accidentally emptied — 0 bytes)
- Logo `Image`: `accessibilityRole="image"`, `accessibilityLabel="SharkPark logo"`
- Title `Text`: `accessibilityRole="header"`
- Update button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, platform-aware label (`"Update on the App Store"` / `"Update on Google Play"`), `accessibilityHint="Opens the store listing to download the latest version"`

### `PermissionGateScreen`
- Allow Notifications button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityHint="Grants permission to receive parking alerts"`
- Not Now button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Not now, skip notifications"`

### `ProfileScreen`
- **4 notification toggles** (`favorites_filling`, `favorites_clearing`, `surge_alerts`, `event_alerts`): `accessibilityRole="switch"`, descriptive `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityHint`, `accessibilityState={{ checked: !!notifPrefs.X, disabled: ... }}`
- **3 theme radio buttons** (System / Light / Dark): `accessibilityRole="radio"`, `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityState={{ checked: themeMode === X }}`; selected-indicator `View` marked `accessible={false}`
- Logout button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Logout"`; icon `accessible={false}`
- Delete Account button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Delete account"`, `accessibilityHint="Permanently deletes your SharkPark account and all data"`; icon `accessible={false}`
- Grant Location button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Grant location access"`, `accessibilityHint="Opens location permission settings"`

### `SubHeader`
- Back button: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Go back"`
- Title `Text`: `accessibilityRole="header"`

### `ShuttleModal`
- Overlay tap-to-close `TouchableOpacity`: `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Close shuttle details"`

---

## Safe-Area Bottom Insets

The `Header` component already applied `insets.top` internally. The gap was the **bottom** — FABs and scroll content were clipping under the iOS home indicator (34 pt) and Android gesture bar on devices without a hardware nav bar.

All four affected screens now import `useSafeAreaInsets` from `react-native-safe-area-context` and offset bottom-anchored elements by `insets.bottom`.

### `ShortTermForecastScreen`
- `ScrollView` `contentContainerStyle`: `paddingBottom: 80 + insets.bottom`
- Report FAB `bottom`: `SPACING.xxl + insets.bottom`
- Navigate FAB `bottom`: `SPACING.xxl + insets.bottom`

### `LongTermForecastScreen`
- Main `ScrollView` `contentContainerStyle`: `paddingBottom: insets.bottom + SPACING.xxl`

### `MapScreen`
- Filter FAB `bottom` (inline override): `SPACING.xxl + insets.bottom`
- Favorites FAB container `bottom` (inline override): `SPACING.xxl + insets.bottom`

### `LoginScreen`
- `KeyboardAvoidingView` container style: `paddingBottom: insets.bottom`

---

## Responsive Layout

Module-level `Dimensions.get('window')` returns a snapshot at import time and never updates when the user rotates the device or enters split-screen. Replaced with the `useWindowDimensions()` hook, which re-renders on change.

### `OnboardingScreen`
- Removed `import { Dimensions }` and top-level `const SCREEN_WIDTH`
- Added `const { width: screenWidth } = useWindowDimensions()` inside the component
- Slide `View` uses `style={[styles.slide, { width: screenWidth }]}` (inline, not in `StyleSheet.create`)
- `getItemLayout` references `screenWidth` from closure
- `renderSlide` `useCallback` deps include `screenWidth`

### `LockedForecastCard`
- Removed `Dimensions` import and static `SCREEN_WIDTH` constant
- Added `const { width: screenWidth } = useWindowDimensions()` inside the component
- `barWidth` `useMemo` dep array updated to `[screenWidth]`

---

## Housekeeping

### Deleted `GeofencingProvider.tsx`
- File was empty (0 bytes) with no imports referencing it anywhere in the codebase — all references point to `EnhancedGeofencingProvider`
- Removed to avoid confusion

### `console.log` audit
- Audited `locationService.ts`, `leaveDetectionService.ts`, `useTransitData.ts`, `EnhancedGeofencingProvider.tsx`, `AzureAuth.tsx`
- All calls were already inside `if (__DEV__)` blocks — no changes needed

---

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/screens/LoginScreen.tsx` | SSO button a11y + bottom safe-area inset |
| `src/screens/OnboardingScreen.tsx` | Skip/CTA/progress a11y + `useWindowDimensions` responsive |
| `src/screens/ForceUpdateScreen.tsx` | Restored from git + logo/title/button a11y |
| `src/screens/PermissionGateScreen.tsx` | Button a11y |
| `src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx` | Notification switches, theme radios, logout, delete, grant-location a11y |
| `src/screens/ShortTermForecastScreen.tsx` | Bottom safe-area insets on FABs + scroll |
| `src/screens/LongTermForecastScreen.tsx` | Bottom safe-area inset on scroll |
| `src/screens/MapScreen.tsx` | Bottom safe-area insets on FABs |
| `src/components/Header/SubHeader.tsx` | Back button + title a11y |
| `src/components/Modals/ShuttleModal.tsx` | Overlay close button a11y |
| `src/components/LockedForecastCard.tsx` | `useWindowDimensions` responsive |
| `src/context/GeofencingProvider.tsx` | **Deleted** (dead empty file) |

---

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter mobile typecheck` — 0 errors
- `pnpm --filter mobile lint` — 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in `coverage/` artifact, unrelated)

- Before: `<Button size="icon"><Menu /></Button>`
- After: `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Toggle sidebar"><Menu /></Button>`

author: bensepanski
body:
#### Context

BEN-56 ("Code quality") asks for DRY / style cleanups. While reviewing
`src/web/`, the `StatusBadge` helper had two consumer paths: most files
imported from `./shared.js`, but `RunDetail.tsx` and `Search.tsx` imported it
from `./Dashboard.js`, which existed only because `Dashboard.tsx` re-exported
it. Two paths for one helper is a DRY hazard.

#### TL;DR

Drop the `StatusBadge` re-export from `Dashboard.tsx`, point all consumers at
`./shared.js`, and replace its 7-deep nested ternary with a lookup map.

#### Summary

- `src/web/Dashboard.tsx`: remove `export { StatusBadge } from "./shared.js"` re-export.
- `src/web/RunDetail.tsx` + `src/web/Search.tsx`: import `StatusBadge` from `./shared.js` directly (matches `MetricsPanel.tsx`, `Dashboard.tsx`).
- `src/web/shared.tsx`: replace the nested ternary in `StatusBadge` with a `STATUS_BADGE_COLORS: Record<string, string>` lookup + named default — same rendering, easier to extend with new run statuses.
- No behaviour change. Class names, ARIA, and the `running` pulse indicator are unchanged.

#### Demo

n/a — internal refactor, no user-visible surface.

#### Alternatives

- Leave the re-export and just delete the duplicate by adding a lint rule
  that bans re-exporting from feature files. Rejected: the rule would have
  exactly one trigger today; a one-line refactor is cheaper.
- Keep the nested ternary. Rejected: the structure encodes status → color
  mapping, which is data, and the ternary form makes adding `cancelled`
  vs. `rate_limited` non-obvious — see how `cancelled` and the unknown
  fallback shared the same arm.
- Move `StatusBadge` color tokens into a Tailwind plugin / theme file.
  Deferred: the codebase doesn't have one and this PR isn't the place to
  add framework infrastructure for one helper.

#### Test Plan

- [x] `pnpm all` — typecheck + fmt:check + lint + test (151) + eval (5)
- [ ] `pnpm build:web` — not run; touched no bundling, no new deps
- [x] Manual: `grep -rn "from \"./Dashboard" src/web/` — only `App.tsx` (which imports `Dashboard` itself) remains.

## 🧾 Descrição

Implementa duas melhorias principais:

1. **Externalização dos easter eggs** (issue #53):
   - Cria o serviço `EasterEggService` que carrega mensagens especiais de um arquivo `easter-eggs.json` (classpath ou volume).
   - Permite adicionar/editar easter eggs sem recompilar a imagem (basta editar o JSON e reiniciar o container).
   - Tratamento robusto para arquivo ausente ou malformatado (o bot não quebra).
   - Configuração via `application.properties` com fallback para `classpath:easter-eggs.json`.

2. **Informação do diretor na resposta do filme**:
   - Busca o diretor principal na crew do TMDB.
   - Exibe o nome do diretor com emoji 🎬, em uma linha separada (com espaço antes do elenco).
   - Sem link para evitar complexidade (deixado para issue futura).

**Testes:** todos os testes foram ajustados e passam localmente.

- Closes #53
- Relacionado a #56 (apenas prepara estrutura)

- [x] Nova feature
- [x] Refatoração
- [x] Documentação

## 🧪 Como testar

### 1. Estrutura do arquivo JSON
- Localmente: `src/main/resources/easter-eggs.json` (já incluído no repositório).
- Em produção: montar o arquivo via volume (`config/easter-eggs.json` no diretório do projeto).

Exemplo de conteúdo:
```json
{
    "280": "🤖 *Review do T-1000:* \"Eu já vi esse filme, e não gostei muito do final\"",
    "1124": "🤖 *Review do T-1000:* \"De acordo com o pessoal desse canal, é a obra-prima do Nolan, eu ||particularmente discordo||.\""
}
```

### 2. Teste do easter egg
- Busque `t1000 buscar terminator 2` → deve aparecer a frase do T-1000 após o "Onde assistir".
- Busque `t1000 buscar the prestige` → deve aparecer o easter egg para o ID 1124 (se configurado).

### 3. Teste do diretor
- Qualquer filme: deve mostrar a linha "🎬 Diretor: Nome" logo após a nota. Exemplo:
  ```
  ⭐ Nota: 8,2/10

  🎬 Diretor: Christopher Nolan

  👥 Elenco: ...
  ```

## 📸 Evidências

*Log de inicialização bem‑sucedido:*
```
INFO ... ✅ Carregados 2 easter eggs de classpath:easter-eggs.json
```

*Resposta do filme (The Prestige) com espaçamento correto e easter egg:*

🎬 O GRANDE TRUQUE
📅 Ano: 2006 🇺🇸🇬🇧
⭐ Nota: 8,2/10

🎬 Diretor: Christopher Nolan

👥 Elenco: ...

```

Assim que o PR for aprovado e mergeado na `develop`, você pode seguir para o próximo passo: **merge da `develop` para a `main`** (quando a versão estiver pronta para lançamento).

Antes de fazer o deploy da versão que contém essa feature, **certifique-se de que o arquivo `config/easter-eggs.json` exista no servidor** (com pelo menos o easter egg do Terminator 2). Caso contrário, o bot iniciará sem easter eggs (mas não quebrará).

body:
## Summary

End-to-end follow-through on three QA-team skill executions plus collateral cleanup. 19 commits, all pushed; tree clean apart from local `.claude/` state.

Tests green at every step:
- Unit 142/142
- Integration 251/251 (whole suite, no skips)
- E2E 100/100 (changed-area scope; full suite gated in CI by the new e2e-tests job)
- Lint: `npx eslint .` reports 0 problems (was broken on the parent commit; surfaced 42 errors + 6 warnings of debt that are now cleared)

## Changes by area

### Test methodology — strict assertions, deterministic timing, isolation
- 4 strict-assertion violations fixed (`Is.True.Or.False`, `.Or.EqualTo(Conflict)`, two `Task.Delay` in route mocks)
- Four more `Task.Delay` calls replaced with `TaskCompletionSource` so loading-state assertions can never race the route handler
- 3 disjunctive `Does.Contain(...).Or.Contain(...)` tightened to single-outcome (Health body, nginx upstream, /health probe)
- Two conditional-body specs (`RefreshButtonReloadsActivity`, `SearchInputFiltersEnvironments`) had `if (await x.IsVisibleAsync())` guards that silently passed when the element was absent — replaced with `Expect(...).ToBeVisibleAsync()`
- `CompleteWorkflowTests` now has an `OnTearDown` safety net that deletes any tracked schemas; the existing inline cleanups stay for the happy path
- Added 10 new auth E2E specs (single-field submit, error recovery, a11y banner, persistence)

### Accessibility
- 5 critical (4 `select-name` + 1 `label`) and 3 serious contrast violations fixed; added `aria-label` to selects/checkbox in Schemas / Settings / CreateSchema; `text-slate-500 → text-slate-400` for Mocks tab eyebrows. Pre-emptive flatten of 11 more Mocks eyebrows that sit on gradients (axe-incomplete) so they stay safe if the gradients ever flatten.

### Security
- Live admin JWT under `e2e/.auth/user.json` was protected via `.gitignore` before any other work, then the directory was deleted entirely
- Dev secrets (Mongo, RabbitMQ, JWT signing key) moved to compose `${VAR:-default}` env substitution. Default values stay backward-compatible (`password123` / `guest`) so existing dev volumes keep authenticating without intervention. JWT default is now an obvious placeholder (`dev-only-do-not-use-in-prod-...`)
- Migration tooling: `infrastructure/rotate-mongo-password.sh` rotates the Mongo admin credential in-place via `db.changeUserPassword`. Verified end-to-end against the live dev stack

### Dependencies
- axios `^1.7.9 → ^1.8.2` (GHSA-jr5f-v2jv-69x6)
- vite `^5.4.11 → ^5.4.14` (GHSA-x574-m823-4x7w + GHSA-vg6x-rcgg-rjx6)
- ESLint 8 (EOL) → 9; the existing `eslint.config.js` was already v9-shaped but missing 5 plugin packages from `devDependencies`, so `npm run lint` had been broken with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Lint now runs clean

### Lint debt cleanup (after the v9 migration exposed it)
- 42 `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` errors fixed:
  - Catch handlers: `catch (err: any)` → `catch (err: unknown)` paired with `getErrorMessage` / new `getErrorStatus` helpers
  - Dialogs: `schema: any` / `field: any` → `Schema` / `SchemaField`
  - State: `Record<string, any>` → `Record<string, unknown>` (matches canonical `Entity.fields`)
  - `useSignalR<T = any>` → `<T = unknown>`
- 4 `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings fixed via `useCallback` (Mocks load functions, Layout bell callback)
- 2 intentional disables with rationale (Mocks initial-environment one-shot effect; EntityList load-on-route)
- 3 `react-refresh/only-export-components` disables for context+hook colocation (AuthContext, ToastContext, NotificationBell) with cross-referenced rationale

### CI
- New `e2e-tests` job: builds TestService.E2E in Release, installs the chromium Playwright browser, spins up the dev compose stack with `--build --wait`, runs against `:3000`/`:5000`, captures stack logs on failure, uploads results, tears down in `always()`
- Coverage thresholds: TestService.Unit gated at 80% (was un-gated); TestService.Tests bumped 70% → 80%
- New NuGet vulnerability scan: `dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive` after restore, fails the job on any Severity-tagged finding (currently clean)

### Operational
- `infrastructure/VERSION 1.0.5 → 1.0.8`, k8s images bumped to 1.0.8, API replicas 1 → 2 (separate concern from the QA work; came from a prior session's QA2 sync)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit, integration, E2E all green locally
- [x] `npx eslint .` reports 0 problems
- [x] `npx vite build` succeeds
- [x] Mongo password rotation script verified against live dev stack
- [ ] CI green on the e2e-tests job in this PR
- [ ] CI green on the NuGet vuln scan in this PR

## Migration notes for reviewers

- Dev environments need no action. Existing Mongo and RabbitMQ volumes keep authenticating.
- To rotate the dev Mongo password without losing data: `bash infrastructure/rotate-mongo-password.sh <old> <new>` and then update `infrastructure/.env`.

author: kirklandgee
body:
## Summary
- Replaces the per-user `GSC_CREDENTIALS_PATH` `.env` field with a single fixed convention: `./credentials.json` at the repo root
- `.gitignore` gets a prominent entry for `credentials.json` (and `credentials.*.json`) right next to the existing public-repo / artifacts warning so it's impossible to miss
- `start.sh` computes the credentials path from the repo root automatically — no env var to misconfigure
- `setup.sh` drops the JSON-path prompt and instead prints a hint at the end about dropping `credentials.json` if it isn't there yet
- Stale registration handling: `CLAUDE.md` documents `claude mcp remove gsc` + re-run `start.sh` to fix paths from older setups

## Why
The previous setup asked each team member to set an absolute path in `.env`, which meant:
- N different valid path conventions across team Macs
- Easy to typo (especially `~/Documents/...` which shells expand differently in different contexts)
- Easy to forget when migrating to a new Mac

A fixed `./credentials.json` convention removes all of that. The onboarding message becomes one line: "drop the JSON from 1Password at the repo root."

## Onboarding (after this merges)
For a new team member:
1. `git pull`
2. Save the GSC service-account JSON from 1Password as `./credentials.json` in the repo
3. `bash start.sh` — registers the MCP automatically
4. Quit + reopen Claude Code

For someone who set up GSC under the old path-in-`.env` convention (i.e. just me):
1. `git pull`
2. Move/copy your existing JSON to `./credentials.json` in the repo
3. `claude mcp remove gsc` (clears the stale registration)
4. `bash start.sh` (re-registers against the new path)

## Test plan
- [x] Verified `git check-ignore credentials.json` reports the `.gitignore` rule on line 12 — file cannot be accidentally committed
- [x] Verified `bash -n start.sh` and `bash -n setup.sh` syntax-check clean
- [x] Migrated my own setup to `./credentials.json`, removed stale MCP, re-registered via the same command `start.sh` would issue
- [x] Confirmed `mcp__gsc__list_properties` still returns the Navi property correctly with the new credentials path

## Reviewer notes
- The `.gitignore` rule is intentionally placed near the top of the file (right after the artifacts warning) and includes both `credentials.json` and `credentials.*.json` so renamed copies stay covered.
- `start.sh` does **not** auto-fix stale registrations — it only registers when no `gsc` MCP exists. If the registered MCP points at an old absolute path from a previous setup, the user has to `claude mcp remove gsc` once. Documented in CLAUDE.md troubleshooting.

## Summary
- Added release data-preservation preflight documentation for database/media/env safety before alpha deploys and later SN-1 sync work.
- Added a read-only public data snapshot helper for safe GET-only backend comparisons.
- Added an SN-1 sync data safety note that keeps any future sync on a non-default branch first.
- Linked the data-preservation steps from the existing alpha release and deployment/media preflight docs.
- Added static docs coverage for the new data-safety docs and helper.

## Exact files changed
- `DATA_PRESERVATION_PREFLIGHT.md`
- `SN1_SYNC_DATA_SAFETY_NOTE.md`
- `scripts/public_data_snapshot.py`
- `ALPHA_RELEASE_READINESS.md`
- `DEPLOYMENT_MEDIA_PREFLIGHT.md`
- `super-nova-2177/backend/tests/test_alpha_readiness_docs.py`

## Data-preservation rules added
- Never run DB reset/seed/drop/truncate/migration-reset/destructive cleanup against production.
- Never point release deploys at a fresh empty DB by accident.
- Preserve `DATABASE_URL`, `UPLOADS_DIR` or durable media storage, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.
- Treat uploads/images as runtime state, not git state.
- Old missing upload bytes cannot be reconstructed without source files, backups, or durable storage.
- Take DB and upload/media backups before deploy promotion or SN-1 branch-sync preview.
- Record `/proposals?filter=latest&limit=30` before and after deploy.

## Destructive-operation audit findings
- Searched for `drop_all`, `create_all`, `seed`, `reset`, `delete database`, upload removal, sqlite deletion, migration reset, and direct file/database deletion patterns.
- Active `backend/app.py` has additive SQLAlchemy `create_all` schema initialization in standalone fallback mode; no drop/reset path found there.
- `backend/supernova_runtime.py` preserves existing `DATABASE_URL` and only falls back to local SQLite when no env URL is set.
- Upload routes create upload directories and save new files; no active upload wipe path was found.
- Backend tests use `create_all` against isolated temporary databases.
- `drop_all` matches were confined to legacy/protected-core tests or stubs, not active release startup.
- No confirmed active production destructive reset path was found, so no runtime code was changed.

## Snapshot helper result
- Added `scripts/public_data_snapshot.py`.
- The helper accepts a backend URL and performs only unauthenticated GET requests to `/health`, `/supernova-status`, and `/proposals?filter=latest&limit=30`.
- It outputs timestamp, backend URL, endpoint statuses, proposal count, proposal IDs/titles/authors, and sampled media URLs.
- Ran against a temporary local backend at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`: all three endpoints returned 200, proposal sample count was 30, and media URLs were captured where present.
- Temporary backend process was stopped after the snapshot check.

## SN-1 sync safety note
- Added `SN1_SYNC_DATA_SAFETY_NOTE.md`.
- It says not to merge SN-2 into SN-1 `master` directly first.
- It directs a future sync to push SN-2 to SN-1 as a non-default branch, preview/stage first, compare public snapshots, and roll back code first, then uploads, then DB only if data changed.
- It reiterates that git does not carry DB rows or upload bytes.

## No uploads/DB/env/local remnants staged
- Confirmed only the six intended docs/test/helper files were staged.
- No uploads, DB files, env files, `.next`, `node_modules`, or deleted-frontend remnants were staged.
- The pre-existing local `super-nova-2177/frontend-social-six/.env.example` remains untracked only.

## Intentionally not changed
- No protected core files.
- No `frontend-vite-basic` changes.
- No backend route/helper semantics.
- No AI publishing/safety behavior.
- No schema, production env files, uploads/DB files, rate-limit thresholds, Docker Compose behavior, deleted legacy frontend folders, SN-1 remotes, or SN-1 branches.
- FE7 source was not touched, so FE7 lint/build/E2E were not rerun for this docs/helper-only patch.

author: chfeng-cs
body:
## Purpose

Close #41830 — change HMA from opt-in to opt-out for KV transfer connectors.

Previously, `--kv-transfer-config` unconditionally disabled the Hybrid KV Cache Manager (HMA), requiring users to explicitly pass `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` to enable it. Since HMA is now mature enough, this PR reverses the default: HMA stays enabled when the effective connector configuration supports it, and is only auto-disabled for connectors that do not.

For hybrid-attention models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Mixtral, Mamba hybrids), this fixes startup OOM caused by `unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs` collapsing sliding-window/chunked-local specs into `FullAttentionSpec` and ballooning KV memory allocation.

## Changes

Add `KVConnectorFactory.supports_hma_config()` that resolves effective HMA support from the transfer config:
- Plain connectors: checks `SupportsHMA` on the class.
- MultiConnector: recurses into all configured children — returns True only if every child supports HMA. Empty/missing children → False.

Both the config auto-disable path and the factory runtime check now use this single helper, keeping them consistent. Non-HMA connectors retain the existing auto-disable + warning behavior.

## Related

- [[#29805](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29805)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29805) introduced the unconditional auto-disable
- [[#39269](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39269)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39269) addresses the analogous issue in the `kv_events_config` path; this PR only changes the `kv_transfer_config` path

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py -v
```

5 unit tests covering:
- HMA-capable connector (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) → not auto-disabled
- Non-HMA connector (`ExampleConnector`) → auto-disabled
- Explicit `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` + non-HMA connector → factory raises `ValueError`
- MultiConnector with all HMA children → not auto-disabled
- MultiConnector with mixed HMA/non-HMA children → auto-disabled

Regression coverage across affected test files:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py \
    -q \
    -k "not multi_example_connector_consistency and not mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache"
```

The two deselected tests require a real distributed environment and are not runnable in a single-process CPU setup.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py -q
.....                                                                    [100%]
5 passed in 2.51s

$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hma_auto_config.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py \
    -q \
    -k "not multi_example_connector_consistency and not mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache"
34 passed, 2 deselected
```

Two tests deselected require hardware or environment not available in this setup.

author: mdheller
body:
## Summary

Adds ADR-035 and the first portable contracts for transparent fault attribution and embedded-engine accountability.

This follows the existing platform contract authority rather than creating a new repo or burying the work in product repos. ADR-033 already establishes canonical receipts and event envelopes in `prophet-platform`; this PR extends that model for crash/guard/sandbox/engine/rollout/diagnostic-redaction surfaces.

## Added

- `adr/ADR-035-transparent-fault-attribution-and-embedded-engine-policy.md`
- `contracts/FaultEnvelope.v0.1.json`
- `contracts/EngineManifest.v0.1.json`
- `contracts/BoundaryTransition.v0.1.json`
- `contracts/RolloutReceipt.v0.1.json`
- `contracts/DiagnosticRedactionPolicy.v0.1.json`
- `tests/fixtures/fault-envelope-script-editor-synthetic.json`

## Design intent

The motivating case is a first-party Script Editor/WebKitLegacy guard-fault report. The finding is intentionally bounded: the artifact is not evidence of external tampering by itself. It is evidence that dense platform diagnostics can still fail to explain hidden subsystem causality to the operator.

The contracts support:

- typed fault semantics instead of ambiguous “crash” buckets;
- explicit engine manifests for renderers, terminal bridges, AI workers, automation bridges, media decoders, diagnostics, and network profilers;
- boundary-transition records that answer “why is this engine running?”;
- human-readable rollout receipts instead of mystery rollout IDs;
- diagnostic redaction tiers separating local-private forensic bundles from shareable/public reports.

## Validation

Not run in this connector turn. This PR is schema/ADR/fixture-only and should next add JSON Schema validation wiring if the repo does not already include a generic contract validator for new `contracts/*.json` files.

## Follow-up product homes

- BearBrowser: component inspector and renderer/automation manifests.
- TurtleTerm: system-action transcript and PTY/automation boundary transitions.
- SourceOS Shell: document/PDF/browser/terminal degraded-mode diagnostics.
- Sociosphere: schema distribution/registration and repo-governance rollup.
- Ontogenesis: ontology terms and SHACL shapes for fault, engine, boundary, rollout, and redaction classes.

author: ybyesilyurt
body:
## Summary

Adds support for templates that require a mix of **1 video + 1 photo** as user input, with everything else (text, font, size, position, music, timing) coming from a curated reference TikTok. Ships the first such template: **Impressing Myself** (template id `936e9558-248f-49be-b857-2b9a193522c6`), modeled tıpa tıp on https://www.tiktok.com/@bassy.e91/video/7622071463956303126.

## Backend

- `media_type` per recipe slot (`"video"` | `"photo"`), default `"video"` for backward compat
- `POST /uploads/template-photo` — multipart image (JPEG/PNG/WEBP/HEIC) → server-side conversion to looping mp4 in GCS via Pillow + pillow-heif + FFmpeg
- Mixed-media path in template orchestrator: positional clip→slot binding, photo slots skip Gemini analysis (synthetic ClipMeta)
- `validate_clip_count` enforces exact slot count for mixed-media templates
- HDR/SDR color-space handling: `zscale + tonemap` for HLG/PQ inputs (iPhone HDR), `setparams` for SDR — fixes FFmpeg 7.x crash on `arib-std-b67`
- Beat-snap buffer: photo mp4 generated at `target + 1s` so beat-snap can extend without exhausting clip duration
- Public `/templates` exposes per-slot `media_type` + `target_duration_s`

## Text overlay improvements

- Word-wrap in `_draw_text_png` (long captions wrap to multiple lines instead of overflowing the canvas)
- `MAX_OVERLAY_TEXT_LEN` raised 40 → 300 (was truncating 60-char captions to "...")
- `stroke_width` field on overlay (TikTok-style black outline around white text)
- `emoji_prefix` field — Twemoji PNG composited to the left of the first line, centered as one unit with the text
- HDR transfer aware

## Frontend

- `SlotBoundUpload` — per-slot widget (photo vs video MIME picker, HEIC accepted), drives the user-facing flow on `/template`
- Same component injected into the admin Test tab so admins can render with mixed media without a frontend round-trip
- Admin slot editor: `Media` select (video / photo)

## Fonts added

- `Inter-Bold.ttf`
- `InterTight-Bold.ttf` (closest open-source match to TikTok's caption font)
- Twemoji `1f5e3.png` (🗣️ speaking head) under `assets/emoji/`

## Tests

- `tests/services/test_image_to_video.py` — 9:16 normalize + e2e mp4 generation (ffprobe-asserted duration + resolution)
- `tests/tasks/test_mixed_media.py` — `_is_mixed_media`, positional binding skips Gemini for photo slots, matcher closest-duration selection
- `test_admin_extended.test_validate_clip_count_mixed_media_requires_exact_slot_count`

## Migrations

Cherry-picked 0010 + 0011 from upstream branches that were deployed but never merged (prod DB was at revision 0011 ahead of `main`). Functional code from those branches not pulled in — only the migration files needed for `alembic upgrade head` to walk the chain.

## Test plan

- [x] iPhone HDR video + JPEG photo upload → render succeeds
- [x] Long caption wraps to 2 lines, no truncation
- [x] Emoji 🗣️ renders fully on-canvas, centered with line 1
- [x] Inter Tight Bold matches reference TikTok caption font weight
- [x] Slot 2 text appears AT photo start (start_s=0.0), not 1s late
- [ ] Side-by-side review of latest render vs reference (eyeball check by Emir)
- [ ] Eng review of pipeline changes (`_assemble_clips`, photo-slot beat-snap)

## Notes for review

- Recipe is mutable JSONB — admin can tune any text overlay field (font, size, color, stroke, emoji, position) without code changes
- `assets/emoji/` is the new "drop a Twemoji PNG named `<codepoint>.png` to support a new emoji" extension point
- Pillow has no color-emoji rendering without raqm/HarfBuzz, hence the static-asset PNG composite approach

body:
## Summary

Первый из четырёх PR-ов **Спринта 2.5 — расширенный админ-интерфейс в боте** (ГДД §18.6, `development_plan.md` §5 / задачи 2.5.1-2.5.10). Этот PR — **только каркас**: новые таблицы, middleware и use-case-ы для TOTP-подтверждения. Реальные admin-команды (`/ban`, `/grant_*`, `/balance_set`, `/announce`, `/audit`, `/clan_*`) появятся в следующих PR-ах серии (2.5-B → 2.5-D), они будут переиспользовать всё, что заложено здесь.

Изменения разбиты на **3 атомарных коммита**:

### 1. `046ad62` — 2.5-A.1: `admin_audit_log` table + порт `IAdminAuditLogger`

Отдельная таблица для админских мутаций (отличается от общего `audit_log` тем, что `admin_id` обязателен, добавлены `tg_chat_id` / `ip` / `source ENUM('bot','web')` для будущей команды `/audit <admin>`).

- Миграция `0016_admin_audit_log` (descends from `0015_referrals`).
- ORM `AdminAuditLogORM` с тремя индексами `(admin_id, occurred_at)`, `(target_kind, target_id)`, `(action)` + `CHECK source IN ('bot','web')`.
- Domain port `IAdminAuditLogger` + VO `AdminAuditEntry` + enum-ы `AdminAuditAction` / `AdminAuditSource`.
- `SqlAlchemyAdminAuditLogger` + `FakeAdminAuditLogger`.
- 6 integration-тестов + 4 unit-теста + расширение `test_migrations`.

### 2. `43186c3` — 2.5-A.2: `AdminGuard` aiogram outer-middleware

«Тихий» enrichment-middleware: читает `data["auth_data"]` (от `AuthMiddleware`), ищет `Admin` через `IAdminRepository.get_by_tg_id`, кладёт `data["admin"] = Admin | None`. Деактивированные админы → `None` (соответствует ГДД §18.6 revoke-семантике).

- `bot/middlewares/admin_guard.py`.
- DI-композиция в `build_dispatcher()` (между `AuthMiddleware` и `LocaleMiddleware`).
- 7 unit-тестов + апдейт `test_composition_root`.

### 3. `0bc3fdc` — 2.5-A.3: TOTP-confirm scaffold

Однократный `token` + 6-значный TOTP — для опасных команд в 2.5-B/C/D. Токен **сжигается до проверки** (atomic `pop` из store-а) — защита от brute-force.

- Миграция `0017_admins_totp_secret` (новая колонка `admins.totp_secret BASE32`, `NULL` = 2FA не настроено).
- Domain: `AdminConfirmRequest` / `AdminConfirmEntry` + ошибки (`Confirm{TokenNotFound,TokenExpired,CodeInvalid,AdminMismatch}Error`, `TotpNotConfiguredError`) + порты `IAdminConfirmStore` / `ITotpVerifier`.
- Application: `RequestAdminConfirm` (генерит token + пишет `ADMIN_CONFIRM_REQUESTED` в audit) + `VerifyAdminConfirm` (`pop` → проверка → `ADMIN_CONFIRM_VERIFIED`/`FAILED` в audit).
- Infrastructure: `InMemoryAdminConfirmStore` (TTL 60c, `cleanup_expired`) + `PyOtpTotpVerifier` (RFC 6238, `valid_window=1` для дрейфа часов).
- Локали: `admin-confirm-*` строки в `ru.ftl` + `en.ftl`.
- `pyotp>=2.9,<3` добавлен в runtime-зависимости + `mypy` override (нет stub-ов).
- 35 новых unit-тестов + 2 integration-теста на totp_secret-roundtrip.

**DI в `Container` намеренно НЕ делаем** — handler-ы появятся в 2.5-B/C/D, тогда и подключим.

### CI

- `make ci` зелёный локально: **2901 passed / 1 skipped, coverage 96.20%**.
- `ruff` / `mypy --strict` / `import-linter` (3 контракта) — все ✅.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

Риск **жёлтый**: новый код, но он не активирован — handler-ы появятся в следующих PR-ах. Главный риск — миграции и контракты портов.

- [ ] **Миграция `0017_admins_totp_secret`** — убедиться, что `alembic upgrade head` на чистой БД проходит и таблица `admins` получает колонку `totp_secret VARCHAR(64) NULL`. У существующих админов значение остаётся `NULL` (после миграции опасные команды для них вернут `TotpNotConfiguredError` — это ожидаемо, в 2.5-D будет `/admin_setup_totp`).
- [ ] **Хранение TOTP-секрета в plain-text** — мотивация в шапке миграции `0017`. Если ты считаешь, что обязательно нужно шифрование (KMS / app-level encryption) — давай обсудим до PR 2.5-D, чтобы не переделывать и схему, и use-case.
- [ ] **`AdminGuard` placement** — middleware кладёт `data["admin"]` для всех update-ов (не только админских). Это намеренно (для будущего `/audit` и rate-limit-decisions), но если хочешь ограничить — могу добавить filter-by-router.
- [ ] **Token format** — сейчас токен генерируется в композиционном корне через `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)` (128 бит); use-case это не знает, принимает `TokenFactory: () -> str`. В 2.5-B при подключении к Container надо будет аккуратно прокинуть фабрику.
- [ ] **Локали** — `admin-confirm-*` ключи добавлены в `ru.ftl`/`en.ftl`, но handler-ов, которые их зачитывают, ещё нет. CI это не ловит — формальный smoke-тест появится в 2.5-B.

**Test plan для smoke-проверки after-merge:**
1. `git checkout main && git pull && alembic upgrade head` — на свежей dev-БД миграция проходит, схема `admins` содержит `totp_secret`.
2. Запустить бота, написать `/start` от не-админа → нет регрессии (AdminGuard кладёт `admin=None`).
3. Зайти как существующий админ (из `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_IDS`) → `/balance_reload` (старая команда) продолжает работать без TOTP (она не из «опасных», её reauth добавим в 2.5-C).
4. (Опционально) В REPL вручную создать `RequestAdminConfirm` + `VerifyAdminConfirm`, прогнать happy-path с реальным authenticator-приложением.

### Notes

- Снимок состояния обновлён в `docs/current_tasks.md` (последний коммит `0bc3fdc`, CI 2901/1, 96.20%).
- `history.md` обновлю **после мерджа** этого PR (как обычно по протоколу из `CONTRIBUTING.md`) — там же зафиксирую, что 2.5-B следующий.
- `current_tasks.md` после мерджа надо будет пересинкать под 2.5-B.

author: sydneyrenee
body:
This pull request updates translation discipline and documentation for the Rust-to-Kotlin port, clarifies naming conventions, and refines translation recipes for trait default methods with `where` clauses. It also updates the `bulkPush` implementation in `Append.kt` for consistency with the new root type and improves documentation and provenance tracking. The most important changes are:

**Translation Discipline and Documentation:**
* Added a comprehensive "Translator's mindset" section to `CLAUDE.md`, outlining strict translation discipline, file mapping, comment handling, and porting workflow. This section emphasizes a faithful, non-optimizing, and non-architectural translation process.
* Clarified and expanded the rules for translating Rust doc comments and identifiers to Kotlin, especially regarding the prohibition of Rust syntax in Kotlin docs and the correct mapping of naming conventions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L22-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L114-R135) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7L56-R153)
* Updated provenance tracking instructions to require `port-lint` headers to point to paths relative to `tmp/rust-stdlib-collections-btree/`, and clarified how these headers are used for audit and cheat detection. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7L36-R129) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1c455d3323f97415d13986dd25facec043345bcedcb8d5646ec52084b84fb939L3-R9) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7L131-R229)

**Trait Default Methods and API Mapping:**
* Added a detailed recipe (in both `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`) for translating Rust trait default methods with `where` clauses to Kotlin extension functions with appropriately constrained type parameters, including rationale and canonical examples. This section also documents the dual-overload pattern for comparator-based APIs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9R244-R402) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7R248-R269)

**Naming Conventions:**
* Strengthened and clarified naming conventions to prevent "Rustifying" Kotlin source: file names use `PascalCase.kt`, types use `PascalCase`, functions/locals use `camelCase`, and packages are lowercase. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54ff182c7e8acf56acfd6e4b9c3ff41e2c41a31c9b211b2deb9df75d9a478f9L114-R135) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7L56-R153)

**Codebase Update:**
* Changed the signature of `bulkPush` in `Append.kt` to operate on `Root<K, V>` instead of `NodeRef<Marker.Owned, K, V, Marker.LeafOrInternal>`, aligning with the new abstraction. Also replaced a `for` loop with `repeat()` for clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-70adedc3640958928e76de18a150082f8c3fd2fd4a8a675c799ce797e617f7c6L11-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-70adedc3640958928e76de18a150082f8c3fd2fd4a8a675c799ce797e617f7c6L52-R49)

These updates collectively enforce stricter translation discipline, improve documentation clarity, and ensure the Kotlin port remains idiomatic and maintainable.

author: smitbarmase
body:
Git's `-d` flag deletes a branch only if it's fully merged into its upstream or HEAD - this is what we were using before, which caused the "not fully merged" error. The `-D` flag force deletes a branch even with unmerged changes (equivalent to `--delete --force`).

### Before

Deleting an unmerged branch failed with a "not fully merged" error toast.

### After

- Deleting an unmerged branch prompts for confirmation to force delete
- Delete button tooltip shows "Hold alt to force delete" hint
- Holding **alt** turns the delete icon red and tooltip changes to "Force Delete Branch"
- Force delete keybinding: `cmd-alt-shift-backspace`

Release Notes:

- Added confirmation prompt when deleting unmerged git branches, with option to force delete.
- Added alt+click on delete button to force delete a branch immediately.

body:
## What

Same treatment as #6 for the remaining Jira-pipeline workflows: pull every \`prompt: |\` block out into reusable commands; consolidate per-attempt variants where they existed.

## Numbers

| File | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| task-tests.yaml | 1,098 | 431 | **−61%** |
| epic-decompose.yaml | 355 | 286 | −19% (partial) |

6 new commands totalling ~750 lines of prompt content.

## Synthesized prompt

### \`archon-review-generated-tests\` (replaces review-generated-tests-1 and -2)

Old shape: \`-1\` was a fresh comprehensive review, \`-2\` was a tighter re-review after the repair pass. Synthesized into one prompt that always reads any prior \`test-review-latest.json\` — if present, verifies each prior \`required_repairs[]\` was actually fixed; if absent, runs as a fresh review. Phase 1.5 selector sanity check applies to both runs uniformly. Always overwrites \`test-review-latest.json\` (no more \`test-review-1.json\` / \`test-review-2.json\` archive).

## Mechanical extractions

- \`archon-generate-tests\` ← generate-tests
- \`archon-repair-tests-from-review\` ← repair-tests-from-review (input ref updated to \`test-review-latest.json\`)
- \`archon-repair-generated-tests-quality\` ← repair-generated-tests (handles lint/typecheck rot, distinct concern from review repairs)
- \`archon-build-decomposition-plan\` ← build-decomposition-plan-json

## Not extracted

\`process-tasks\` in epic-decompose uses an inline \`loop.prompt\` (loop iteration body). The engine's loop schema requires \`loop.prompt\`, not \`loop.command\`. Left inline; \`loop.command\` support would be a separate engine PR.

\`jira-router\` and \`task-done\` have zero inline prompts — nothing to extract.

## YAML bash changes

- \`parse-test-review-1\` reads \`test-review-latest.json\` (was \`test-review-1.json\`).
- \`parse-test-review-final\` snapshots \`test-review-latest.json\` to \`test-review.json\` instead of fallback-chaining \`test-review-2.json\` then \`test-review-1.json\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bun run cli validate workflows\` — 38/39 valid (the 1 invalid is \`archon-smart-pr-review\` missing local MCP config, pre-existing on main, unrelated)
- [x] \`bun run check:bundled\` — clean (50 commands, 25 workflows)
- [x] \`bun run type-check\` — clean (10 packages)
- [x] \`bun run lint\` — clean (\`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192\`)
- [ ] **Live shake-out:** next ticket through task-tests should converge identically. The synthesized review prompt is a superset of the old per-attempt variants — first review now runs the prior-repair-verification check (no-op when no prior exists).

## Behavior changes

- First review run now runs the full "verify prior repairs" check uniformly (no-op when no prior review exists). Same logic that was already running on the second pass.
- No attempt-numbered review files anywhere. Every consumer reads \`test-review-latest.json\`.

body:
## Summary
- New `?action=capture&title=…&url=…&tags=…` query handler in the matrix shell that materializes a task in the **Eliminate** quadrant. Designed to be triggered by a browser bookmarklet (cross-origin same-origin policy prevents direct IndexedDB writes from a bookmarklet, so the URL-param round-trip is the privacy-first path).
- Pure parser at `lib/share-capture.ts` with 9 unit tests — handles 80-char title truncation, hostname fallback when the page has no title, comma-separated tag dedup (capped at 20), and rejection of non-http(s) URLs.
- Icon-rail hover-expand now waits 500ms before expanding (vs. instant) so accidental cursor drift no longer triggers expand/collapse churn. Keyboard `focus-within` remains instant.
- Version bump 9.0.2 → 9.1.0 plus matching SW cache key bump (returning users need a fresh cache to pick up the new URL handler).

## Bookmarklet for users
```
javascript:(function(){var u=encodeURIComponent(location.href);var t=encodeURIComponent(document.title||location.hostname);window.open('https://gsd.vinny.dev/?action=capture&title='+t+'&url='+u+'&tags=readme,todo','_blank');void 0;})();
```

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run test` — 1825/1825 pass (9 new tests in `tests/data/share-capture.test.ts`)
- [x] `bun typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun lint` — no new warnings
- [x] Drag the bookmarklet to the bookmarks bar, click it from a third-party site (e.g. Hacker News), confirm a task appears in the Eliminate quadrant with title = page title, description = URL, tags = `readme`, `todo`
- [ ] Refresh the GSD tab after capture — verify the task does **not** double-add (params should be stripped via `replaceState`)
- [ ] Hover the icon-rail briefly (< 500ms) — should stay collapsed
- [ ] Hover and rest ≥ 500ms — should expand
- [ ] Tab into a rail button via keyboard — should expand instantly

author: rtkartista
body:
Closes #3860 (partial — search module benchmark)

### What
Adds the first benchmark to the `search` module: `benchmarks/search/bench_kdtree.cpp`

Benchmarks `pcl::search::KdTree` (FLANN) vs `pcl::search::KdTreeNanoflann`
across three axes:
- **Tree construction**: 10k / 100k / 500k points
- **kNN query**: k = 1, 5, 20, 50
- **Radius search**: r = 5, 10, 20 m

### Results
Hardware: 12 threads / Ubuntu 24.04 / GCC 13 / `-O3 -mavx2`  
Cloud: `table_scene_mug_stereo_textured.pcd` (307,200 pts) for query benchmarks;
synthetic uniform random for build benchmarks  
Repetitions: 3 — mean reported  

> absolute timings may vary slightly

#### Tree construction (ms, lower is better)

| Points | FLANN (ms) | nanoflann (ms) | Speedup |
|--------|-----------|----------------|---------|
| 10k    | 1.15      | 0.979          | 1.17×   |
| 100k   | 16.2      | 13.1           | 1.24×   |
| 500k   | 129       | 94.4           | **1.37×** |

#### kNN query (µs, lower is better)

| k  | FLANN (µs) | nanoflann (µs) | Speedup |
|----|-----------|----------------|---------|
| 1  | 0.831     | 0.244          | **3.41×** |
| 5  | 1.43      | 0.466          | **3.07×** |
| 20 | 2.18      | 0.912          | **2.39×** |
| 50 | 5.10      | 2.97           | **1.72×** |

#### Radius search (µs, lower is better)

| radius (m) | FLANN (µs) | nanoflann (µs) | Speedup |
|------------|-----------|----------------|---------|
| 5          | 12,735    | 1,521          | **8.37×** |
| 10         | 12,991    | 1,536          | **8.46×** |
| 20         | 13,244    | 1,539          | **8.60×** |

**nanoflann is 1.2–1.4× faster to build, 1.7–3.4× faster on kNN, and
8.4× faster on radius search** — making it the clear default for
localization and mapping pipelines that call `radiusSearch` in tight loops
(normal estimation, ICP, GICP, NDT).

### Notes
- Accepts optional PCD path as `argv[1]`; falls back to synthetic 100k-pt cloud
- nanoflann benchmarks compiled in automatically when `PCL_HAS_NANOFLANN` is defined
- Ready to extend with `registration` / `features` benchmarks in follow-up PRs

author: copilot
body:
Several UI/UX issues across the app: report dialog text was invisible (white-on-white inheritance), products without subcategories showed a noisy "no subcategory" placeholder, the checkout page was cramped with unnecessary trust-account copy, email notifications had no HTML template and leaked email addresses as sender names, and the navbar greeting used a static icon regardless of time of day.

## Changes

### Report popup (`sellers/[id]/page.tsx`)
- Explicitly set `bg-white text-slate-900` on the dialog body to prevent color inheritance from the red header
- Changed cancel button to `variant="outline"` for clear visual contrast
- Darkened submit button hover state (`hover:bg-red-700`)

### Subcategory section (`HeroAnimation.tsx`)
- Entire subtype section (label + input group) is now conditionally rendered — hidden when `getSubTypesForProduct()` returns `[]` (ספר תורה, תפילין)
- Removed the "אין תת-סוג נוסף לקטגוריה זו" placeholder

### Checkout page (`checkout/[id]/page.tsx`)
- Removed the "trust account" ShieldAlert explanation block and the small shield note in the summary card
- Changed grid from `md:grid-cols-3` (2+1) to `md:grid-cols-5` (3+2) for better horizontal balance

### Email HTML template (`send-email.ts`, `api/send-email/route.ts`)
- `SendEmailOptions` now accepts optional `html` field passed through to Resend
- API route accepts `senderName`, `message`, and `link`; builds a styled black/white HTML email when present:

```ts
// POST /api/send-email
{ to, subject, text, senderName, message, link }
```

### Sender name in chat notifications (`chat/[id]/page.tsx`)
- Added `myProfile` state: fetches `first_name`/`last_name` from sellers/customers tables in parallel on mount
- Email notification now uses actual full name instead of email address prefix

### Greeting icon (`Navbar.tsx`)
- Replaced static `Sparkles` with time-appropriate icons:
  - 05:00–11:59 → `Sunrise`
  - 12:00–17:59 → `Sun`
  - 18:00–21:59 → `Sunset`
  - 22:00–04:59 → `Moon`

author: dexonapi-alt
body:
## Summary

Pulls model + folder + chat + user + awareness badge + chunk pulse into a sticky `<Header>` at the top of the App. **The user always sees current state without scrolling up.**

```
  sys v0.1  my-project · openrouter-auto · my-chat · joy · ✔ 92 · ▸ 3
  /model /mode /permissions ...
```

Awareness/chunk cells appear only after the matching event arrives, so a fresh terminal shows just the identity row.

### Event bus extension

Two new event types in `cli-client/src/agent/events.ts`:
- `awareness_update { state, confidence, lastSignal? }` — emitted whenever the server response carries a fresh `awarenessSnapshot`
- `chunk_plan { chunkIndex, nextAction, fileCount? }` — emitted once per chunk planner brief

### Reducer extension

- New `AwarenessSnapshot` + `ChunkPulseState` types in `AgentEventState`
- `awareness_update` overwrites the snapshot (most recent wins). `clear` wipes back to null.
- `chunk_plan` increments a `pulseKey` monotonically per event so the Header's `<Pulse>` re-fires even when `chunkIndex` appears to repeat (defensive against duplicate emissions).

### New `<Header>` component

Single-row layout: `sys · folder · model · chat · user · [awareness badge] · [chunk pulse]`.

**Awareness badge** uses `awarenessGlyph(state)` for the glyph + `confidenceGradient(confidenceToGradientT(score))` for the colour. The mapping is slightly exponential (`Math.pow((100 - confidence) / 100, 0.85)`) so a 90 still feels solidly green, not "near yellow" which a linear mapping would imply. The glyph carries state for `--no-motion` mode where the colour interpolation collapses to a single stop.

**Chunk pulse** renders `▸ N` through `<Pulse>` keyed on `pulseKey` so a new chunk re-fires the ping; the index reads as a monotonic counter.

### Agent emissions (`cli-client/src/agent/agent.ts`)

Two callsites: the initial-turn chunk plan (in user-message arrival) and the per-turn chunk plan (in handleNeedsTool). Both emit `awareness_update` + `chunk_plan` via `emitAgent` when the matching response field is present and `isInkActive()` returns true.

**Awareness emission is independent of chunk_plan presence** — a tool-only turn can still drop confidence and the Header should reflect it.

### App.tsx restructure

- Top StatusLine replaced with `<Header />` (same data props). The trailing two cells light up via the events bus.
- `StatusLine.tsx` deleted (only consumer was App.tsx).
- Layout unchanged otherwise: Header on top, AgentStream middle, ChatInput, LiveStatusBar bottom.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean both sides
- [x] CLI `npm test`: **202/202** (was 190 → +12)
  - 8 reducer cases: awareness set/overwrite/null-fallback, chunk set/default-fileCount/pulseKey monotonicity/duplicate-index defensive/clear-wipe
  - 4 `awarenessGlyph` mapping cases (each state's glyph, no two collide)
- [x] Server `npm test`: **268/268** unchanged (cli-only stage)
- [x] **Backwards-compat verified**: with `SYS_INK` unset, `isInkActive()` returns false, `emitAgent` calls for awareness/chunk are skipped, legacy console rendering unchanged. The Header component is a pure render swap of the previous StatusLine — same data props, no API change for the consumer (App.tsx).

## What's coming in Stage 6

- `<Typewriter>` applied to AI message content in `<AgentStream>` (long-form completions, summaries)
- `<Reasoning>` component replaces the legacy reasoning display: animates in via `<Fade>`, auto-collapses to a one-liner after 8s, expands on Tab
- Chunk-progress "▸ next action" gains a `<Pulse>` on transition between chunks (single-shot, cubic-out)

**Visible win at Stage 6**: AI output reads like writing, not loading.

author: jeanmainguy
body:
This PR introduces a match score for every predicted toxin–antitoxin pair, along with a second output file and several usability improvements.

### Scoring

Each pair is scored by comparing three structural features — toxin size, antitoxin size, and intergenic distance — against reference statistics derived from known TADB3 systems. Robust Z-scores (median + MAD) are used to handle the non-normal size distributions common in TA families. A compatibility term is added when the toxin–antitoxin family combination has not been observed in TADB3. All terms are combined into a single score in `(0, 1]`:

```
score = exp(−mean(|z_i|))
```

Family-specific statistics are used when available; a global fallback is applied for unrecognised or rare families.

### Changes

- **New output file** `tatouscan_results_pairs.tsv`: one row per predicted pair, with gene annotations, protein lengths, intergenic distance, and the pair score.

author: nahv
body:
## Summary
Bug: el admin devolvía 422 \"Signups not allowed for this instance\" al pedir magic link, incluso con un email autorizado.

Causa: el código en \`admin/js/auth.js\` llamaba \`supabase.auth.signInWithOtp\` con \`shouldCreateUser: true\` (default). Con signups deshabilitados a nivel del proyecto Supabase (lo que recomendamos en el README como capa extra de seguridad), Supabase rechaza intentos de signup con 422 — incluso para emails que después se podrían loguear.

## Fix

\`shouldCreateUser: false\` en \`signInWithOtp\`. Con esto:
- Magic link se manda solo a users que ya existen en Supabase Auth.
- Los users del admin se crean **manualmente una vez** en Dashboard → Authentication → Users.
- Si alguien intenta loguearse con un email no registrado, devuelve error claro: \"No encontramos una cuenta con ese email. Pediles a un admin que te agregue manualmente en Supabase Auth.\"

## Compatibilidad con la security model

Esta combinación da defensa en profundidad:

| Capa | Qué bloquea |
|---|---|
| Frontend allowlist (\`config.js\`) | UX — rechaza emails no allowlisted antes de hablar con Supabase |
| Supabase \"Disable signups\" | Bloquea creación de users desde cualquier API |
| Manual user creation | Solo emails que un admin agregó pueden loguearse |
| \`shouldCreateUser: false\` | El cliente no intenta signup |
| Edge Function ADMIN_ALLOWLIST | Backend rechaza JWTs de emails fuera de la lista |

Cualquiera de las 5 que se rompa, las otras 4 protegen.

## Test plan

- [ ] Mergear → deploy a main → cache limpia → ir a \`iudex.com.ar/admin/\`.
- [ ] Login con \`nahuel@iudex.com.ar\` (asumiendo está pre-creado en Supabase Auth Users) → recibir magic link → click → autenticado.
- [ ] Login con un email no autorizado (\`test@gmail.com\`) → frontend rechaza inmediatamente sin tocar Supabase.
- [ ] Login con un email autorizado pero NO pre-creado en Supabase Users → mensaje claro \"No encontramos una cuenta...\".

## Para el reviewer
Antes de testear, verificar en Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Users que existan:
- \`nahuel@iudex.com.ar\`
- \`mbury@iudex.com.ar\`

Si no están, agregarlos con \"Add user\" → Email (sin password). Es one-time setup.

author: rrhester
body:
## Two bugs from the Today's Plan attendance approvals

### 1. Confirm threw enum-cast error
```
column "status" is of type public.shift_status but expression is of type text
```

Migration `0071_attendance_decide.sql` declared `v_status text` and assigned it into `shifts.status` (the `public.shift_status` enum). Postgres is strict about enum assignment.

**Migration `0075_attendance_decide_status_cast.sql`** re-creates the function with an explicit cast:
```sql
update public.shifts
   set status = v_status::public.shift_status
 where id = p_shift_id;
```
Logic otherwise identical. Safe to re-apply.

### 2. Decline left the row on screen
JS just faded `opacity:.55` and stopped. Operators expected the queue to shrink as they processed approvals.

Fixed: 600ms after the inline "Approved/Declined" pill renders, the row fades + slides + collapses out (.35s transition) and removes itself from the DOM. Then `_refreshTodayPlanData()` refreshes the wave KPIs so the Checked-In / Not-In counts reflect the new shift status.

## You need to apply migration 0075 in Supabase

Open `supabase/migrations/0075_attendance_decide_status_cast.sql`, paste into Supabase SQL Editor, run. The `notify pgrst, 'reload schema'` is at the bottom so PostgREST picks up the new function definition immediately.

Cache buster: `live.js?v=20260507o`.

author: luke-bradford
body:
Refs #974. Closes #976. Second foundational PR for the credential-health-as-scheduling-precondition umbrella.

## What

- **`app/services/credential_health_cache.py`** — thread-safe per-process cache. Pre-init reads return MISSING (fail-safe — consumers don't run creds-using work until the listener confirms state). Includes `scan_all_operators(pool)` for full-table aggregate scan.
- **`app/jobs/credential_health_listener.py`** — listener thread:
  - Initial full-scan with retry-with-backoff (1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, 30s cap) until success.
  - LISTEN on `ebull_credential_health` channel.
  - 1s notify-block + drain loop.
  - 5s poll fallback that re-scans the full table to recover any dropped notify.
- **`app/main.py`** + **`app/jobs/__main__.py`** — each process owns its own cache + listener thread daemon, joined with 5s timeout on shutdown.
- Production NOTIFY payloads now include `environment` for forward-compat with multi-environment.
- Malformed payloads logged by exception type only — never payload contents.

## Why

Subsequent children (#977/D/E) need a fast in-process view of operator credential health to make scheduling/connection decisions. Going to the DB on every gate check would 10x the connection load. The cache is process-local because notifies are wake-ups and the DB is the source of truth — no shared state needed.

## Test plan

- [x] 16 new tests at `tests/test_credential_health_listener.py`:
  - Pre-init fail-safe: every read returns MISSING.
  - Cache: post-init unknown operator MISSING; known operator returns seeded value; upsert + replace semantics.
  - scan_all_operators: aggregate per (operator, env); excludes revoked-only operators.
  - Listener startup: initial scan populates cache + flips initialized.
  - Listener startup retry: failing scan backs off and retries until success.
  - Constants pinned: backoff sequence, poll interval, notify-block < poll interval.
  - Notify path: NOTIFY triggers re-read + cache update.
  - Poll fallback: dropped notify recovered within POLL_INTERVAL_S.
  - **Security**: malformed payload contents never reach logs (PREVENTION test for Codex r1.4).
- [x] All 42 #975 tests still pass; 58 in the combined suite.
- [x] Smoke (lifespan boots clean) passes.
- [x] ruff + format + pyright clean.
- [x] **Codex pre-push review**: 4 findings + 1 coverage gap raised, all fixed before push (Python 2 except syntax, missing environment in payload, payload contents in log, malformed-payload test).

## Spec

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-credential-health-precondition-design.md` sections "NOTIFY contract" + "Subscribers MUST do a full DB scan on startup" + Codex r1.10/11/12 + r2.8.

author: sebmendo1
body:
## Summary

Sprint 6 (M6 part A) — AutoDSM detects local Claude credentials, streams
agent turns into the renderer's chat panel, and lays down the
`ChannelTransport` contract for the manager↔preview bridge that Sprint 7
will activate end-to-end. Stacked on Sprint 5 (PR #5).

## Auth (`code/lib/autodsm-agent/src/auth/detect.ts`)

Full classification matrix: `subscription` | `api-key` | `oauth-token` |
`bedrock` | `vertex` | `none`. Probes the local `claude` CLI via
`claude --version` + `claude auth status` (subscription wins) and falls
back through `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`. **Never** reads
`~/.claude/.credentials.json` or the macOS Keychain — Anthropic TOS
prohibits OAuth-token extraction by third-party apps.

Test injection points (`env`, `skipClaudeProbe`) drive a 7-test suite
covering the full env-var matrix.

## Stream parser (`runtime/stream-parser.ts`)

`StreamJsonParser` buffers partial chunks across stdout reads and emits
one `StreamEvent` per complete line. Recognizes `message_start/stop`,
`text`, `content_block_delta` (→ text), `tool_use`, `tool_result`,
`error`. 7 unit tests covering complete lines, partial buffering,
content_block_delta, tool_use, parse errors, end() flush, blank-line
skipping.

## Subprocess runtime (`runtime/subprocess.ts`)

`spawnClaude()` forks `claude -p --output-format stream-json
--input-format stream-json [--model] [--allowed-tools]`, pipes the user
prompt through stdin, exposes an `AsyncIterable<StreamEvent>` the main
process drains into IPC, and a graceful `abort()` that escalates
SIGTERM → SIGKILL.

## API fallback (`runtime/api-fallback.ts`)

Contract + stub for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` users. Emits an actionable error
event for now; wiring `@anthropic-ai/sdk` is deferred until production
needs it.

## Sessions (`sessions.ts`)

JSONL persistence under `<repoRoot>/.autodsm/sessions/<id>.jsonl` with
`appendEntry` / `readSession` / `listSessions` / `newSessionId`.
Tolerates corrupt lines so a bad write doesn't lock the user out. 4
unit tests.

## IPC + Electron host

- `shared/ipc`: `AGENT_AUTH_STATUS`, `AGENT_QUERY`, `AGENT_ABORT`,
  `AGENT_DONE` channels and payload types.
- `electron/main`: handles `AGENT_AUTH_STATUS` → `detectAuth`,
  `AGENT_QUERY` → spawn claude, streams turns to renderer, persists to
  JSONL, `AGENT_ABORT` → kills active subprocess. When auth is
  none/api-key, returns an actionable error turn instead of failing
  silently.
- `electron/preload manager`: exposes `getAuthStatus` / `agentQuery` /
  `agentAbort` / `onAgentTurn` / `onAgentDone` on `window.autodsm`.

## Channels (`autodsm-channels`)

- `createRendererTransport(bridge)`: real `ChannelTransport`
  implementation for `createBrowserChannel({ extraTransports: [...] })`.
- `createMainBridge(bridge)` + `MainBridge` type: documents the
  main-side IPC contract Sprint 7 will hook up.

## Renderer

- "Auth: …" billing badge: green for `subscription` / `oauth-token`,
  purple for `bedrock` / `vertex` / `api-key`, red for `none`.
- Agent transcript: chat-style turns (user / assistant / tool / error)
  with appropriate accent colors. Input disabled when auth is `none`.

## Test plan

- [x] All 8 AutoDSM packages pass `check-package.ts`.
- [x] `yarn vitest run code/lib/autodsm-agent` → 18/18 passing across
      auth, stream-parser, sessions.
- [x] Earlier sprint suites still green: detect (27), indexer (9),
      csf-writer (22) → total **76/76**.
- [ ] **Manual**: open the AutoDSM Electron app on a machine with
      `claude` CLI authenticated → badge shows
      `Claude Code · subscription`; type a prompt → response streams in.
- [x] Audit: `grep -r '\.credentials\.json\|Keychain' code/lib/autodsm-*
      code/apps/autodsm-electron` returns nothing.

## Sprint 6 DoD

- [x] Auth detection identifies all 6 kinds across an env-var matrix.
- [x] Stream-JSON parser handles partial chunks, tool_use, errors.
- [x] No subscription OAuth tokens are ever read.
- [ ] Channel events flow end-to-end IPC: contract is in place; the
      preview-side preload bridge wires up in Sprint 7 alongside the
      manager-api integration.

## What's next

Sprint 7 — repair tools, ChangeSet UI, onboarding polish, and the
preview-side IPC bridge that closes the manager↔preview channel.

author: davidwkeith
body:
## Summary

Anglesite's local HTTPS preview (mkcert + hosts file + pfctl) requires sudo/admin access. In Claude Cowork and other web-based or sandboxed environments, sudo isn't available, which currently causes confusing prompts or hangs during `npm run ai-setup`.

This PR detects the environment and skips HTTPS setup entirely when admin access isn't available. The dev server falls back to `http://localhost:4321`.

## Changes

- **`template/scripts/setup.ts`** — New `canRunPrivileged()` helper checks for root, sudo binary, cached/NOPASSWD sudo, and TTY availability. The HTTPS-related steps (`installMkcert`, `trustLocalCA`, `generateCert`, `configureSystemHttps`) are gated behind it. Persists `HTTPS_AVAILABLE=true|false` to `.site-config` so other code can adapt.
- **`template/scripts/cleanup.ts`** — Same detection; falls back to printing manual cleanup instructions instead of attempting sudo.
- **`template/scripts/check-prereqs.ts`** — Reports `https=available` or `https=unavailable (no admin/sudo — preview at http://localhost:4321)` based on `.site-config` and live environment check.
- **`skills/start/SKILL.md`** — Adds Claude Cowork wizard summary and post-setup messaging based on `HTTPS_AVAILABLE`.
- **`template/CLAUDE.md`** — Webmaster guide explains how to choose the right preview URL (`https://DEV_HOSTNAME` vs `http://localhost:4321`) based on `HTTPS_AVAILABLE`.
- **`template/docs/local-https.md`** — Documents the no-admin fallback and `HTTPS_AVAILABLE` flag.

## Detection logic

```ts
async function canRunPrivileged(): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!isWindows && process.getuid?.() === 0) return true;   // root
  if (isWindows) return true;                                // GUI elevation
  if (sudo binary missing) return false;                     // Cowork-like env
  if (sudo -n true succeeds) return true;                    // cached/NOPASSWD
  return process.stdin.isTTY === true;                       // can prompt
}
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `npm test` (passes — 2184 tests)
- [ ] Run `npm run ai-setup` in a sudo-less environment (e.g., container without sudo binary) and confirm HTTPS steps are skipped, `HTTPS_AVAILABLE=false` is written, dev server starts on `http://localhost:4321`
- [ ] Run `npm run ai-setup` on macOS with sudo and confirm existing flow still works, `HTTPS_AVAILABLE=true` is written
- [ ] Run `npm run ai-check` in both environments and confirm `https=available|unavailable` is reported correctly
- [ ] Verify the `start` skill picks the correct post-setup message based on `HTTPS_AVAILABLE`

---
`crank` run, then:

## Entry

If current folder is not a git repo, warn the user files might be edited.

Open url/app/cli-login where url is braintrust.dev by default and can be changed with BRAINTRUST_APP_URL (done by creating a session via POST /api/cli/wizard-signin/create)

The web ui will return an api key, org name and id, project name and id

Now the web ui setup is done, the user is back in the terminal.

choose model provider and paste the api key ; sdk integration and agents framework are not relevant here. The list of available models is in the braintrust monorepo.

- don't ask the api key for custom llm providers (for example self-hosted llm). The option custom should exist and flip a boolean, and instrumentation does not happen if the llm provider is a custom one

If in a git repo, store it in .env.braintrust and add .env.braintrust to .gitignore if there isn't already a pattern that covers it (like .env\*)

We now have a project selected, an AI provider API key and a BRAINTRUST_API_KEY.

## Instrumentation

Ask the user whether to run our custom coding agent harness:

- yes:
  - if `bt` is not on path, install it with `curl -fsSL https://bt.dev/cli/install.sh | bash` if on Mac/Linux. [Windows support will come later.]
  - run the custom harness with our prompt (so we use a coding agent) and BRAINTRUST_API_KEY in the env
- no: write the prompt to /tmp/ and tell the user the prompt is in said temp file
  End of coding agent use

## Cleanup

Tell the user:

- if instrumentation was run, command to copy-paste to resume the instrumentation chat with the agent
- for production, they need the BRAINTRUST_API_KEY env variable
- where the docs are (https://www.braintrust.dev/docs).
  If a trace was emitted, include the permalink to it. Explanation about how to get the permalink is in [point to the correct skill]

## Prompt

Use the same prompt as `bt setup`:

- Like for `bt setup`, detect the language used by the current repo (look for dependency file in the current folder and if none are found, in the subfolder, depth 1 maximum).
- these parts must not be copied to `crank` since they will be done deterministically by the code:
  - Verify API Key (Install Precondition)
  - Verify in Braintrust (CRITICAL)
  - Post-Success Verification and Next Steps

## Custom Harness

Use pi and extend it.
If the output of the agent (not user input, not thinking, only an answer of the agent to the user) contains 'summary' (case-insensitive), end the conversation 1s after the agent has stopped thinking/typing and is waiting for user input, and go to the next step: Cleanup.

The only tools allowed should be:

- write/edit files (includes grep, git grep, ripgrep) in the current folder and its subfolders, `.env.braintrust` at the root of the current git folder
- curl (mainly to read braintrust.dev/docs). GET and HEAD only, no POST request.
- bt
- package managers, formatters, linters and test helpers of the target language and an interpreter when relevant (python, node...). If no language has been programmatically detected, allow all package managers
- git
- env
- the agent must be able to ask the user to temporarily add a tool to the list of allowed tools. `sudo` must not be in the command the agent tries to run (if it is then denied).
  Notably, bash and python are not allowed.
  The harness runs in yolo mode since it can not do dangerous things.

#### Python

conda, hatch, mamba, pdm, pip, pipenv, pipx, poetry, rye, uv
formatters: autopep8, black, isort, ruff, yapf
linters: flake8, mypy, pylint, pyright, ruff
test: coverage, nose2, pytest, tox, unittest

#### JavaScript / TypeScript

bun, deno, ni, npm, pnpm, yarn
formatters: biome, dprint, prettier
linters: biome, eslint, oxlint
test: ava, jasmine, jest, mocha, node:test, vitest

#### Go

dep, glide, go modules
formatters: gofmt, gofumpt, goimports
linters: go vet, golangci-lint, revive, staticcheck
test: ginkgo, go test, gomock, testify

#### C#

Chocolatey, NuGet, Paket
formatters: csharpier, dotnet format
linters: roslyn analyzers, sonaranalyzer, stylecop
test: FluentAssertions, MSTest, NUnit, Shouldly, xUnit

#### Java

Bazel, Gradle, Ivy, Maven, Mill, SBT
formatters: checkstyle, google-java-format, spotless
linters: checkstyle, error prone, pmd, spotbugs
test: AssertJ, JUnit, Mockito, Spock, TestNG

#### Ruby

Bundler, RubyGems, asdf, rbenv, rvm
formatters: rubocop, rufo, standardrb
linters: brakeman, reek, rubocop, standardrb
test: cucumber, minitest, rspec, test-unit

# Important notes:

All cli choices must have the same choices/behavior as choice done in the web ui
`crank` is a rehaul of `bt setup`. However some behavior has changed. Ask if anything is unclear, even if `bt setup` has an implementation.

## Web ui signup workflow

- choose email/password
- email verification
- choose org name and US/EU data plan
- welcome page that says the user should go back to the terminal

## Login

`bt setup` open a local callback server and the web flow redirects with a token. This is not the desired behavior for crank.
`crank` call POST /api/cli/wizard-signin/create, which returns api key, name and id of project and org.

## Options of `crank`

Same behavior as `bt`:
--api-url <URL> Override API URL [env: BRAINTRUST_API_URL]
--app-url <URL> Override app URL [env: BRAINTRUST_APP_URL]
--ca-cert <PATH> Path to PEM CA bundle [env: BRAINTRUST_CA_CERT; overrides SSL_CERT_FILE]

# Telemetry

## Braintrust monorepo

Listen on braintrust.dev/app/cli-telemetry for json payload.
TBD: backend implementation detail
Append only
No authentication.

## Crank

If the CRANK_ENABLE_TELEMETRY env variable is FALSE (case-insensitive), do not start any of the telemetry. This should be said in the help.
Otherwise:
When crank starts, start a very lightweight process (crank-telemetry).
crank-telemetry stores (in RAM, nothing stored on disk):

- launch time (when crank-telemetry starts), seconds from epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00)
- stop time (when crank stops)
- if crank stopped because of ^C sending SIGINT to crank, or just because it finished (SIGINT/finished JSON payload). To do this, crank must inform crank-telemetry that everything is done after it finishes cleanly. If crank stops and crank-telemetry hasn't received this information, the reason is SIGINT.
- which language is instrumented: typescript, python, go, ruby, java, csharp, unknown
- which llm provider was used: openai, anthropic, gemini, mistral, togetherai, fireworks, perplexity, xai, groq, lepton, cerebras, replicate, baseten, custom
  After crank has stopped or 15 minutes has passed (whichever is first), send the telemetry (POST with Content-Type: application/json, User-Agent: crank/<version>) to braintrust.dev/app/cli-telemetry. Stop crank-telemetry after the telemetry has been sent.
  The language and provider fields are optional, because crank can be stopped at any time, including before those choices are made.
  In case of network failure, try a second time. If it still fails, stop crank-telemetry.
  If the HTTP request takes longer than 5s to go through, cancel it and stop crank-telemetry.
  The user should never be slowed by crank-telemetry.
  Example:

```json
{
  "start": 1778276067,
  "end": 1778276545,
  "stop-reason": "SIGINT",
  "language": "python",
  "provider": "custom"
}
```

## Summary

The admin **Enable notification emails** toggle was only checked when *queuing* new emails (`Consumer::receive()` / `bulkReceive()`). The `MailQueueHandler::sendEmails()` background job that actually delivers emails had no knowledge of the toggle and would send all queued entries regardless.

This means: if emails were already sitting in `oc_activity_mq` when an admin disabled the toggle, they would still be sent on the next background job run.

The fix adds an early-return guard at the top of `sendEmails()`, consistent with the checks already in `UserSettings::getUserSetting()` and `filterUsersBySetting()`. The queue is intentionally left intact — if the admin re-enables emails, pending notifications can still be delivered.

Related to #2562 (which fixed the same missing check in `bulkReceive()`).
