author: natejsimonsen
body:
## Summary

Remove SBOM digests from the `docker buildx imagetools create` calls in `publish-gadget-images-manifest` and `publish-ig-images-manifest`. The image index now contains only platform images and their attestation manifests.

## Problem

The `oras attach` step creates SBOM artifacts with platform `linux` and an **empty architecture string**. When these digests are passed to `imagetools create`, the resulting OCI image index contains entries like:

```json
{
  "platform": { "architecture": "", "os": "linux" },
  "config": { "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json" }
}
```

Some container registries -- notably AWS ECR pull-through cache -- fail to resolve architecture-specific images when these malformed `linux/""` platform entries are present, breaking image pulls on arm64 nodes.

For comparison, the `unknown/unknown` attestation manifests (created by buildx, with `vnd.docker.reference.type: attestation-manifest` annotations) are handled correctly by ECR and containerd. The `linux/""` SBOM entries are the problem.

### Current v0.51.0 index (6 entries)

| platform | type |
|----------|------|
| linux/amd64 | platform image |
| linux/arm64 | platform image |
| unknown/unknown | attestation (amd64) -- harmless |
| unknown/unknown | attestation (arm64) -- harmless |
| linux/"" | SBOM (amd64) -- **breaks ECR** |
| linux/"" | SBOM (arm64) -- **breaks ECR** |

### After this change (4 entries)

| platform | type |
|----------|------|
| linux/amd64 | platform image |
| linux/arm64 | platform image |
| unknown/unknown | attestation (amd64) |
| unknown/unknown | attestation (arm64) |

This matches the index shape of other multi-arch images (e.g. `vectordotdev/vector`) that work correctly through ECR pull-through cache.

## Why this is safe

SBOMs are already attached to each per-platform image via `oras attach` (steps `gadget-container-images-attach-sbom` and `ig-container-images-attach-sbom`). They remain discoverable through the [OCI referrers API](https://github.com/opencontainers/distribution-spec/blob/main/spec.md#listing-referrers) and tools like `oras discover`. Including them in the image index was redundant.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on this branch
- [ ] After merge: verify `docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/inspektor-gadget/inspektor-gadget:<next-tag>` shows only linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and unknown/unknown attestation entries (no linux/"" entries)
- [ ] After merge: verify `oras discover ghcr.io/inspektor-gadget/inspektor-gadget:<next-tag>` still shows SBOM artifacts attached to per-platform images

body:
## Summary

Adds four features inspired by [SyncDisBoi](https://github.com/SilentVoid13/SyncDisBoi) (the closest competitor) without diluting this project's analysis-first focus. Bumps version `0.6.0` → `0.7.0`.

## What's new

### 1. `sync-likes` command (menu `[10]`)

Mirrors YT Music **Liked Songs** to Spotify's **Liked Songs** library (`/me/tracks`).

- Reuses Spotify URIs already discovered in `playlist_enriched.csv` so a track in both places is matched only once.
- Separate snapshot under `data/snapshots/likes/` — likes diff state never collides with playlist diff state.
- Separate output files: `data/likes_enriched.csv`, `data/likes_unmatched.csv`.
- Supports `--dry-run`.

**Heads-up:** the OAuth scope expanded to include `user-library-read` and `user-library-modify`. First 0.7.0 launch triggers a one-time re-authorization in the browser; spotipy refreshes the cached token automatically.

### 2. `export` command (menu `[11]`)

Writes the enriched CSV as portable JSON.

```bash
python playlist_sync.py export                       # data/playlist_enriched.json
python playlist_sync.py export -o /tmp/data.json     # custom path
```

Structure: `{ exported_at, track_count, tracks: [{...}, ...] }` with all 49 enrichment fields per track. Easier to feed `jq`, dashboards, or other tools than the 49-column CSV.

### 3. Per-run debug stats JSON

Every `sync` writes `data/debug/run_<timestamp>.json` (and a rolling `latest.json`):

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-07T12:34:56",
  "totals": {"current": 3202, "already_matched": 3113, "newly_matched": 0, "unmatched": 89, "skipped": 12},
  "diff": {"added": 28, "removed": 7, "unchanged": 3089},
  "match": {"rate_pct": 97.22, "methods": {"title_artist": 25, "relaxed": 1}, "avg_confidence": 0.95},
  "skip_reasons": {"no_album": 12},
  "unmatched_examples": [{"title": "...", "artist": "..."}, ...],
  "skipped_examples": [{"title": "...", "artist": "...", "reason": "no_album"}, ...]
}
```

Useful for graphing sync quality over time or feeding a monitoring dashboard.

### 4. Skip-no-album filter (`skip_reason` column + `data/skipped.csv`)

YT Music tracks lacking album metadata (typically YouTube uploads, fan edits, mixes) are now filtered out **before** Spotify search and written to `data/skipped.csv` with `skip_reason="no_album"`.

Effects:
- Saves ~1.5 s × N tracks of Spotify API time per sync.
- Keeps `unmatched.csv` focused on tracks that genuinely should match but didn't.
- Per-track audit trail of *why* each was skipped (extensible — future skip reasons can use the same column).

Tracks whose album metadata later gets filled (user edits in YT Music) are re-evaluated naturally on the next sync.

body:
## Summary

Closes EDO-10. Sub-task of EDO-8 (Strapi audit). All config-only, no feature changes.

### M2 — Strapi config hardening

- **Split `strapi/config/middlewares.ts`** into a base file plus per-env overrides under `strapi/config/env/{development,production}/middlewares.ts`. Strapi merges them at runtime via lodash so the active CORS origin list depends on `NODE_ENV`.
  - Base: empty `origin` list (safe default for unknown envs / `test`).
  - Development: `http://localhost:{3000,1337,5173}` only.
  - Production: `https://e-do.studio`, `https://www.e-do.studio`, `https://cms.e-do.studio` only — no localhost.
- **Tightened CSP `connect-src`**: dropped the global `https:` allowance. Production now lists `'self'`, the prod API URL, and the R2 bucket explicitly. Development keeps `'self'`, the local API, ws://localhost:1337 (HMR), and the R2 bucket.
- **`config/server.ts`**: added `proxy: env.bool('IS_PROXIED', false)` so behind a reverse proxy / CDN, `ctx.request.ip` and `ctx.request.protocol` are correct and admin cookies become `secure`.
- **`config/admin.ts`**: flipped `FLAG_NPS` and `FLAG_PROMOTE_EE` defaults from `true` to `false`. The NPS survey and EE promo banner no longer appear in prod without an explicit opt-in.

### M4 — `.env.example`

- Added `NODE_ENV`, `PUBLIC_URL`, `IS_PROXIED`, the full database block (sqlite default, postgres/mysql commented), Cloudflare R2 upload provider keys (`CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CF_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `CF_ACCESS_SECRET`, `CF_BUCKET_NAME`, `CF_PUBLIC_URL` — names match `config/plugins.ts`), and the admin feature flags. Each block is preceded by a one-line comment so a new dev can `cp .env.example .env`, fill in the blanks, and run `npm run develop`.

## Verification

- `npm run build` in `strapi/` passes (TS compile + admin panel build).
- Confirmed via a small lodash-merge probe against the compiled output that:
  - `NODE_ENV=production` → CORS origin = `[e-do.studio, www.e-do.studio, cms.e-do.studio]`, CSP `connect-src` does **not** contain `https:` global.
  - `NODE_ENV=development` → CORS origin = `[localhost:3000, localhost:1337, localhost:5173]`.
  - Base (any other env) → CORS origin = `[]`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this branch (`npm run build`).
- [ ] Deploy to prod (or run with `NODE_ENV=production` locally): `OPTIONS /api/site-setting` from `http://localhost:3000` is rejected, from `https://e-do.studio` it succeeds.
- [ ] Inspect a prod admin response: CSP header has no `connect-src https:` global.
- [ ] With `IS_PROXIED=true` behind a proxy (or simulating `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`), the admin no longer warns about non-secure cookies.
- [ ] Prod admin UI: no NPS banner, no EE promo banner.
- [ ] Fresh checkout: `cp .env.example .env`, set DB + R2 creds, `npm run develop` boots cleanly.

## Out of scope

- Frontend wiring (M1) and `site-setting` model (M3) — separate sub-tasks.
- Database/upload provider migration — backlog.

author: fenio
body:
## Summary
Closes #19. Two related fixes to the Install / Edit App form on the Apps page.

**1. The Internal port input was hard-disabled.**

Auto-detection from the image's `EXPOSE` works for many images but not all — private registries, no `EXPOSE` declared, registry unreachable, or simply images where the user wants a different internal port for some reason. The user reported this against `jellyfin/jellyfin` (which listens on 8096): even when they typed the right exposed port, the internal stayed stuck at the default 80.

Fix: drop `disabled` on the container_port input and wire `checkPortConflicts` to its `oninput` so editing it re-runs conflict detection like the host port does.

**2. `apps.inspect_image` failures were swallowed silently.**

The form started with a default `container_port: 80`, called inspect on `onblur` of the image field, and on any failure quietly fell back to that default. Users with a problematic image saw "80" appear and had no clue why auto-detection didn't fire.

Fix: track an `inspectMsg` state and surface it inline under the image input:
- `Image declares no exposed ports — set the internal port manually.` when inspect succeeded with an empty ports list
- `Could not inspect image (<error>) — set ports manually.` when the RPC itself failed

The message is amber (warning, not error) and clears as soon as the next inspect runs.

## Test plan
- [ ] Engine + WebUI CI green (svelte-check 0/0, vitest 60 tests still pass)
- [ ] On a real appliance: install a Jellyfin app, verify Internal port can be typed manually and Exposed maps onto it correctly
- [ ] Type a bogus image like `does-not-exist:latest` and confirm the amber inline message appears
- [ ] Type an image with no `EXPOSE` (e.g. some `alpine` tag) and confirm the "no exposed ports" message

## Summary
Completes the bidirectional follow relationship between members. PR #49 added `following[]` and the mutations — this PR adds the reverse `followers[]` side and makes both mutations keep both arrays in sync atomically.

## Changes

**Member model**
- Added `followers: [ObjectId]` array (refs `Member`) alongside existing `following`
- No migration needed — existing documents default to empty arrays

**GraphQL schema**
- Added `followers: [Member!]!` to `Member` type

**Mutations — now bidirectional**

`followMember(memberId)`:
- Validates target member exists before writing
- `$addToSet` on requester's `following` AND target's `followers` in `Promise.all`
- Self-follow guard still in place

`unfollowMember(memberId)`:
- `$pull` on requester's `following` AND target's `followers` in `Promise.all`

**Field resolvers**
- Added `followers` resolver that populates ObjectIds into full Member documents

## Querying
```graphql
query {
  currentMember {
    following { id firstName lastName }   # who I follow
    followers { id firstName lastName }   # who follows me
  }
}
```

body:
## Summary

Extends the body-existence-check exemption in `scripts/validate_docs.py` from a single `target_ref` to also cover a new optional `target_secondary_refs` frontmatter array on review artefacts.

**Why.** Review-PR branches are forked from `main` per `docs/prompts/reviewer.md` §A.15 / §B.15. Until now, the validator exempted only one off-main target artefact-id (the review's `target_ref` or `ticket_ref`). That works for single-target reviews (RV-SPEC-006..012) but fails for bundle-reviews where an ArchSpec extension brings multiple new ADRs and Tickets along — first usage is RV-SPEC-013 reviewing `ARCH-001@0.6.0` + `ADR-014..018` + `TKT-021..028` (13 secondary refs). Without this fix, body references to those secondary artefacts trigger `referenced artifact ADR-014 does not exist` etc. on the review-PR until the architecture PR merges first.

**What changes.** A reviewer can now declare additional off-main targets in frontmatter:

```yaml
target_ref: ARCH-001@0.6.0
target_secondary_refs:
  - ADR-014@0.1.0
  - TKT-021@0.1.0
  # ...
```

The validator extracts artefact-ids from this list (in addition to `target_ref` / `ticket_ref`) and exempts them from the body-existence check. All other references — and unpinned bare references regardless — must still resolve.

**Smoke-tested locally:**
- Validator on `main` with patch and no review using the new field: `86/0` (unchanged behaviour).
- RV-SPEC-013 review file with `target_secondary_refs:` populated: `87/0` (review file now passes).
- Negative case — bogus `ADR-999@0.1.0` injected in body, not in `target_secondary_refs`: still `[FAIL]` with `referenced artifact ADR-999 does not exist` (no blanket-exemption regression).

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Confirm the new code path is gated on `art.type_ == "reviews"` so non-review artefacts that happen to have the field are unaffected (current implementation does this).
- [ ] Sanity-check that `bare_re` (unpinned-reference detector below) is intentionally untouched — bundle-review targets must still be cited with full `@X.Y.Z` pins.

### Notes

This is a clerical Devin Orchestrator PR. RV-SPEC-013 (PR #143) does not strictly need the new frontmatter to land — once PR #142 merged, rebasing #143 onto post-#142 `main` makes its body references resolve naturally. This fix is forward-looking: future multi-artefact SPEC reviews can opt into the field directly without depending on merge-order plumbing.

author: origamihase
body:
## 🛡️ Sentinel Security Enhancement

### 🚨 Severity
MEDIUM — same Zero-Trust shape-guard pattern previously caught for `places/client.py`, the Baustellen fallback loader, and the provider modules. This iteration fixes the per-iteration variant in the VOR station-update path.

### 💡 Vulnerability / Gap
`scripts/update_vor_stations.py:fetch_vor_stops_from_api` already routed *decode* failures through a fallback branch:

```python
try:
    payload = response.json()
except ValueError:
    log.warning("VOR API returned invalid JSON for station %s", station_id)
    stop = fallback_map.get(station_id)
    if stop:
        stops.append(stop)
    continue

raw_stops = payload.get("StopLocation")   # ← AttributeError on list/null/scalar
```

A successfully-decoded but non-object body (list / `null` / scalar) — from a misbehaving upstream proxy or a contract change — would slip through the `except ValueError:` and crash on `payload.get(...)`. Because the call happens **inside** a `for station_id in ids:` loop, the resulting `AttributeError` propagates out of the loop entirely.

### 🎯 Impact
Per-iteration Zero-Trust failures are worse than per-call ones:

* A single bad station response terminates the *entire* batch — every station after the bad one is silently skipped.
* The per-station `fallback_map.get(station_id)` handler that exists for exactly this scenario is bypassed, because it is unreachable after the raise.
* `update_all_stations.py` (run by the `update-stations.yml` and `manual-full-refresh.yml` GitHub Actions workflows) calls this function as part of the periodic station-directory refresh, so a single malformed VOR response would leave the directory partially refreshed and require manual intervention.

### 🔧 Fix
Adds an `isinstance(payload, Mapping)` guard immediately after the decode, and routes shape failures through **the same** `log.warning(...)` → `fallback_map.get(station_id)` → `continue` branch as the existing decode-failure and HTTP-error branches. Loop continuity matches the already-documented failure-handling contract.

```python
if not isinstance(payload, Mapping):
    log.warning(
        "VOR API returned non-object JSON (%s) for station %s",
        type(payload).__name__,
        station_id,
    )
    stop = fallback_map.get(station_id)
    if stop:
        stops.append(stop)
    continue
```

### ✅ Verification
- `python -m pytest tests/test_update_vor_stations_api.py -v` → **7 passed** (3 existing + 4 new parametrised cases over `[]`, `None`, `42`, `"Service Unavailable"`)
- `python -m pytest tests/ -q --timeout=60` → **1634 passed, 3 skipped**
- `ruff check scripts/update_vor_stations.py tests/test_update_vor_stations_api.py` → **All checks passed**
- `mypy scripts/update_vor_stations.py` → **Success: no issues found**

The new test asserts not just that the malformed station's fallback is used, but that the fallback **with the correct vor_id and name** appears in the returned `stops` list — pinning down loop continuity, not just per-iteration recovery.

### 📓 Journal
New entry in `.jules/sentinel.md` records the loop-continuity nuance: a Zero-Trust shape guard added *inside* a loop must mirror the structure of the nearest existing failure branch verbatim, otherwise the existing per-iteration fallback handler is unreachable.

### Diff scope
- `scripts/update_vor_stations.py` (+17)
- `tests/test_update_vor_stations_api.py` (+88)
- `.jules/sentinel.md` (+5)

Total: 110 insertions — purely additive shape-validation, no behaviour change on the happy path.

author: jjackson
body:
## Product Description

AI agents using the labs MCP can now create or update solicitations as publicly listed (\`is_public=true\`) — the same behavior the form-based UI already offers. Previously the MCP rejected \`is_public=true\` with POLICY_VIOLATION, which forced agents to hand off to a human (or run the admin CLI command) any time they wanted a record to surface on the public **/solicitations/** marketplace. The broader policy still applies to funds and reviews.

## Technical Summary

The no-public-records-via-MCP policy on main was a security boundary against AI agents publishing records that could carry PII or pipeline-preview data. That concern is real for funds (financial allocations) and reviews (evaluator notes), but a solicitation's whole point is to be publicly discoverable — its content is title, scope of work, questions, and evaluation criteria. Blocking that meant every public-listing flip required either the form UI or the new \`fix_solicitation_public\` admin command, which is awkward when an agent is otherwise authorized to draft solicitations end-to-end.

Two changes, both narrowly scoped to \`commcare_connect/mcp/tools/solicitations.py\`:

- \`create_solicitation\` drops the POLICY_VIOLATION guard on \`is_public=true\` and forwards the value as \`public=\` to \`LabsRecordAPIClient.create_record\`. Default behavior (no \`is_public\` set) is unchanged — records are still private.
- \`update_solicitation\` captures \`is_public\` from \`update_data\` before stripping it from the merged \`data\` dict, then forwards it as \`public=\` to \`update_record\`. The strip remains so visibility lives exclusively on the LabsRecord envelope (no duplication inside JSON \`data\`).

Tool descriptions updated to spell out the relaxation and warn against putting PII or pipeline-derived data into a public solicitation. \`commcare_connect/mcp/tools/funds.py\` and \`commcare_connect/mcp/tools/reviews.py\` are untouched.

## Safety Assurance

### Safety story

The relaxation is a deliberate scope reduction of the security policy, not a removal: solicitations are exempted because their data shape is inherently public (no PII fields, no pipeline JSON). Funds and reviews remain blocked. The relaxation also matches what the form-based create flow already does — agents now have parity with the UI rather than a stricter sandbox.

The propagation logic on update is identical to the shape we landed earlier on PR #162 before realising the policy applied; it captures \`is_public\` before the strip, which is the only correct ordering. Updates that don't touch \`is_public\` still pass no \`public=\` kwarg, so the existing flag is preserved.

### Automated test coverage

\`commcare_connect/mcp/tests/test_solicitation_tools.py\`:

- \`test_create_solicitation_propagates_is_public_to_server\` — replaces the old POLICY_VIOLATION test; verifies \`public=True\` reaches \`create_record\` when \`data.is_public\` is true.
- \`test_update_solicitation_propagates_is_public_to_server_flag\` — verifies \`public=True\` reaches \`update_record\` AND that \`is_public\`/\`public\` are stripped from the merged data dict (no duplication).
- \`test_update_solicitation_omits_public_when_is_public_absent\` — verifies updates that don't touch \`is_public\` don't send a \`public=\` kwarg.

\`test_create_solicitation_happy_path\` (no \`is_public\` in data) still passes — confirms private-by-default behavior is unchanged.

Funds (\`test_fund_tools.py\`) and reviews (\`test_review_tools.py\`) suites pass unchanged — 54 total tests across the three.

### QA Plan

After deploy:

1. From a Claude Code session with the labs MCP, call \`create_solicitation(program_id=\"<id>\", data={\"title\": \"Test\", \"is_public\": true, ...})\` and confirm the response shows \`public: true\` and the record appears at \`https://labs.connect.dimagi.com/solicitations/\`.
2. Call \`update_solicitation(<id>, update_data={\"is_public\": false})\` and confirm the record disappears from the public listing.
3. Call \`create_fund(...)\` (or any fund tool) with \`is_public: true\` and confirm POLICY_VIOLATION is still raised — the broader policy is intact.

### Labels & Review

- [x] The set of people pinged as reviewers is appropriate for the level of risk of the change

author: usepowershell
body:
**🧪 Fry (Tester)**

Closes #194

## What got wired

- **ExecutorFactory** — builds ICommandExecutor per HostMode using the same construction path the production server uses (OutOfProcessCommandExecutor + OutOfProcessSubprocessPool), without the hosting/configuration/logging stack. Skips `SetupAsync` because built-in cmdlets are callable without environment customization — the harness measures executor cost, not module install.
- **HostMode [Params] axis** on every scenario (Single, Pool, ProcessPool) — one `dotnet run` produces one results table covering all three configurations.
- **All five scenarios** wired end-to-end: `ColdStartBenchmark`, `WarmInvokeThroughputBenchmark`, `PayloadSizeSerializationBenchmark`, `ProcessCrashRecoveryBenchmark`, `RunspaceCorruptionRecoveryBenchmark`.
- **Crash injection** lives in `ExecutorFactory` via reflection into private fields — keeps the bench-only hook out of production types. `InternalsVisibleTo` for `PoshMcp.Benchmarks` added to `PoshMcp.csproj` for the few internal types referenced through the public `ICommandExecutor` surface.
- **P99StatisticColumn** custom BDN column — the AC requires P99 and BenchmarkDotNet 0.14 only ships `StatisticColumn.P95`.
- **AI / spec-008 logging disabled** inside the bench process — `Program.cs` sets `ApplicationInsights__Enabled=false` and clears `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` before BDN starts.

## Output columns (per AC)

| Column         | Source |
|----------------|--------|
| Mode           | `HostMode` `[Params]` |
| Scenario       | one row per `[Benchmark]` method |
| Payload size   | `PayloadBytes` `[Params]` (256 KB / 1 MB rows on the size scenario) |
| Mean           | BDN built-in |
| P95            | `StatisticColumn.P95` |
| P99            | `P99StatisticColumn` (custom) |
| Crash-recovery | `Mean` column on `ProcessCrashRecoveryBenchmark` rows IS the per-mode recovery time |

## Invocation (full reproduction lives in PoshMcp.Benchmarks/README.md)

```powershell
# All scenarios, all modes
dotnet run --project PoshMcp.Benchmarks --configuration Release -- --filter *

# One scenario across all modes
dotnet run --project PoshMcp.Benchmarks --configuration Release -- --filter '*WarmInvoke*'

# Filter by mode
dotnet run --project PoshMcp.Benchmarks --configuration Release -- --filter '*Mode=ProcessPool*'

# Smoke test (near-zero iterations)
dotnet run --project PoshMcp.Benchmarks --configuration Release -- --filter '*ColdStart*' --job dry
```

Markdown output lands in `PoshMcp.Benchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/` — the `*-report-github.md` file is what #195 will consume.

## Smoke-test results

- **Build (Release):** 0 errors, no new warnings (2 pre-existing `NU1510` from `System.Security.Cryptography.Xml` in `PoshMcp.csproj`).
- **`--list flat`:** all 5 scenarios discovered.
- **`ColdStartBenchmark --job dry`:** PASS for `Single` (5.5 s), `Pool` (5.9 s), `ProcessPool` (6.0 s) — confirms the harness drives all three executors end-to-end.
- **`WarmInvokeThroughputBenchmark --job dry`:** PASS for `Pool` (265–318 ms / 10 calls). `Single` and `ProcessPool` throw `OOP error: An item with the same key has already been added. Key: Content` from `OutOfProcessHost.SendRequestAsync` when 10 concurrent invokes share a single host. **This is a real production bug in `OutOfProcessHost` that the harness exposes — not a bench-wiring defect.** Filed as a follow-up; does not block #194 (the harness wiring is correct, and the failure mode is exactly what a benchmark is supposed to surface).
- **Full regression suite (Debug):** 629 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped.

## Expected full-run duration

A complete run across all five scenarios × three modes × the payload-size axis is on the order of **30–60 minutes** on a modern dev box; allow longer when including the 1 MB payload row and accounting for repeated cold-start launches in `ProcessCrashRecoveryBenchmark`.

author: taddiemason
body:
## Summary

The bot started throwing `OperationalError: unable to open database file` mid-session — `!daily` succeeded, then `!portfolio` failed a minute later. `DB_PATH` defaults to the **relative** path `"hatebot.db"`, so SQLite resolves it against the process's current working directory. If `cwd` changed (or the parent dir of an env-var override didn't exist), SQLite couldn't find/create the file and every DB-touching command crashed.

## Fix

- Anchor `DB_PATH` to `database.py`'s directory by default — `cwd` changes can no longer break it
- Resolve to an absolute path even when set via env var
- `os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)` so a missing parent dir is created automatically

## Test plan

- [ ] Bot launches from any cwd and finds/creates `hatebot.db` next to `database.py`
- [ ] `DB_PATH` env var still works (now resolved to absolute)
- [ ] `!daily`, `!portfolio`, `!balance` and other DB-touching commands work after restart

body:
💡 What: Optimized distance calculations in `CanonBase.cs` by caching squared distance thresholds and utilizing pre-calculated `RaycastHit.distance` from physics queries.

🎯 Why: `Vector3.Distance` involves vector subtraction, three multiplications, and a square root operation. Since `RaycastHit` already stores the distance calculated by the physics engine, recalculating it is redundant. Additionally, calculating `fireRange * fireRange` every frame for multiple cannons adds unnecessary CPU overhead.

📊 Impact: Reduces CPU overhead per cannon instance in the `Update` loop. This is particularly effective during boss encounters with many active cannons.

🔬 Measurement: Verify that `Vector3.Distance` is no longer used in `UpdateLaserScale` and `HandleRotationAndFiring`. Ensure `fireRangeSqr` and `fireRangeSqrGate` are used for distance threshold checks.

author: charleneleong-ai
body:
## Summary

Every MACLA step's per-request log shows `"tokens": {"prompt": 0, "completion": 0, "total": 0}` despite the LLM clearly being called (we have responses). Two combined bugs:

1. **`safe_structured_invoke` discards usage.** It called `llm.with_structured_output(schema).invoke(messages)` and returned only the parsed Pydantic model — throwing away the AIMessage wrapper that carries `usage_metadata`.
2. **`_postprocess_log_extras` only handled cached tokens.** Even when a `usage` object was passed, prompt/completion/total never reached `log_extras`. The non-MACLA path surfaced them in `BaseOrakAgent.get_action` directly, but MACLA's override only calls `_postprocess_log_extras`, skipping that block.

Net effect: W&B token cost tracking, per-step cost dashboards, and the `tokens` field in `raw_requests.jsonl` were all silently zeroed.

## Fix

- `agents/macla/structured_output.py:safe_structured_invoke` now returns `(parsed_model, usage_dict | None)`. Uses `with_structured_output(..., include_raw=True)` so we get the AIMessage back and lift `usage_metadata` (LangChain canonical) or `response_metadata.token_usage` (legacy provider integrations) off it. Normalises both to `tokens_prompt` / `tokens_completion` / `tokens_total` keys.
- `agents/macla/unified.py:_base_fallback` unpacks the tuple and stashes usage on `self._last_llm_usage`. `_get_action` then injects it into `memory_stats["usage"]` so the existing `BaseMaclaAgent.get_action` plumbing (which already does `usage = memory_stats.get("usage")`) picks it up.
- `agents/base.py:_postprocess_log_extras` extracts prompt/completion/total tokens in addition to cached. Handles both the new dict shape and the legacy OpenAI usage object via `hasattr`.

Procedure-cache hits (no LLM invocation) leave usage at `None` and the record stays at zero — same as before, no false reporting.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_macla_token_logging.py` (10 tests, all passing):
  - `_extract_usage` lifts `usage_metadata` from AIMessage
  - `_extract_usage` falls back to `response_metadata.token_usage` for legacy provider integrations
  - `_extract_usage` synthesises `total_tokens` when only prompt+completion present
  - `_extract_usage` returns `None` cleanly when neither field is set
  - `safe_structured_invoke` returns a `(parsed, usage)` tuple — pinning the new contract
  - `safe_structured_invoke` degrades gracefully when a provider silently drops `include_raw=True`
  - `_postprocess_log_extras` extracts dict-shaped usage into canonical token keys
  - `_postprocess_log_extras` extracts OpenAI-shaped usage object via attribute access (backwards compat)
  - `_postprocess_log_extras` does not overwrite a `tokens_total` already populated by the BaseOrak direct path
  - `_postprocess_log_extras` handles `usage=None` without crashing (procedure-cache hits)
- [x] Pokemon + weave-entity test suites still pass — `tests/test_pokemon_milestones.py` (10/10), `tests/test_pokemon_warp_render.py` (8/8), `tests/test_weave_entity_prefix.py` (5/5)
- [ ] Verify on next pokemon run that `raw_requests.jsonl` shows non-zero token counts, and W&B run cost dashboard populates.

## Out-of-scope follow-ups

- The `_stats["total_input_tokens"]` aggregator in `BaseOrakAgent.act` (line 232-234) already reads `tokens_prompt` from `log_extras` — once this PR lands those W&B-side aggregates will start populating too. No additional code changes needed.
- The non-MACLA `BaseOrakAgent.get_action` path (line 465-471) still has its own inline token-extraction block. Could be consolidated into `_postprocess_log_extras` for full DRY, but leaving as-is — that path was already working, and consolidation would slightly change the order of the cache-stats vs token-counts lookup. Not worth a behaviour change in this PR.

## Commits

| SHA | Subject | Files |
|---|---|---|
| [`d62efe3`](https://github.com/charleneleong-ai/orak-2025-starter-kit/commit/d62efe3) | fix(macla): surface LLM token usage into raw_requests.jsonl | [`structured_output.py`](https://github.com/charleneleong-ai/orak-2025-starter-kit/blob/fix/macla-token-logging/agents/macla/structured_output.py) · [`unified.py`](https://github.com/charleneleong-ai/orak-2025-starter-kit/blob/fix/macla-token-logging/agents/macla/unified.py) · [`base.py`](https://github.com/charleneleong-ai/orak-2025-starter-kit/blob/fix/macla-token-logging/agents/base.py) · [`test_macla_token_logging.py`](https://github.com/charleneleong-ai/orak-2025-starter-kit/blob/fix/macla-token-logging/tests/test_macla_token_logging.py) |

author: bhavenst
body:
## Summary

Authenticator maps of `map_type=allow` could not recover `access_allowed` once it had been set to `False` by an earlier deny-all rule. The `create_claims()` function in `ansible_base/authentication/utils/claims.py` guarded the `allow` branch with `and not has_permission`, which silently dropped the case where a later allow-map fires affirmatively (`has_permission=True`). As a result, once `access_allowed=False` was set by the first map, no subsequent allow map — regardless of order — could ever restore access.

## Root Cause

At line 123 of `ansible_base/authentication/utils/claims.py`, the condition:

```python
if auth_map.map_type == 'allow' and not has_permission:
    access_allowed = False
    understood_map = True
```

only executed when `has_permission=False`. When a later allow-map evaluated to `ALLOW` (`has_permission=True`), the condition was `False`, control fell through to the `if not understood_map` catch-all, and the error `"Map type allow of rule ... does not know how to be processed"` was logged. The `access_allowed` variable was never reset to `True`.

## Changes

- **`ansible_base/authentication/utils/claims.py`** — Remove the `and not has_permission` guard and replace `access_allowed = False` with `access_allowed = has_permission`. This makes `access_allowed` always track the most recently evaluated allow-map result, letting later (higher-order) rules override earlier ones as the ordering mechanism is designed to support.
- **`test_app/tests/authentication/utils/test_claims.py`** — Add one parametrized case (`allow` + `always` trigger) to the existing `test_create_claims_single_map_acl` suite, and three new standalone regression tests:
  - `test_create_claims_deny_all_then_allow_override` — deny at order=1, allow-always at order=2 → access granted
  - `test_create_claims_deny_all_not_overridden_without_match` — deny at order=1, allow-group at order=2, user NOT in group → access denied
  - `test_create_claims_deny_all_overridden_with_group_match` — deny at order=1, allow-group at order=2, user IS in group → access granted

## Risk Assessment

- **Confidence:** HIGH (95%)
- **Risk:** Low — the change only affects `map_type == 'allow'` maps. The deny path (`has_permission=False`) produces the same result as before (`access_allowed = False`). The only behavior change is that the grant path (`has_permission=True`) now sets `access_allowed = True` instead of being silently dropped.
- **Scope:** 2 files changed

## Testing

- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] Regression tests added (4 new test cases covering the fixed code path)
- [ ] Lint checks pass

## JIRA

- Ticket: [AAP-45394](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AAP-45394)

## See Also

See also: https://github.com/ansible/django-ansible-base/pull/959 — an open PR with an identical fix (also covering AAP-45047 and AAP-45394). Reviewers may choose to close this PR in favor of #959 or merge whichever is reviewed first.

---
*Debuggernaut autonomous fix -- review carefully before merging.*

  * Authentication rule evaluation updated so later allow rules can override earlier denials, ensuring rule ordering is respected.

* **Tests**
  * Added regression tests covering rule override scenarios: deny-then-allow, non-matching allow, group-based matches, allow-then-deny precedence, revoke-deny overridden, and multi-rule "last writer wins" behavior.

## Summary

This PR introduces a non-destructive **preview mode** to the Open Library Import API endpoints (`/api/import` and `/api/import/ia`) and refactors the import pipeline's public surface for clarity. When callers pass `?preview=true`, the full import pipeline runs end-to-end with **zero persistence and zero external side effects**, returning simulated keys (`/works/__new__{UUID}`, `/books/__new__{UUID}`, `/authors/__new__{UUID}`) and an `edits` list mirroring the records that would have been written.

## Changes (6 files, +320/-79 lines, 6 commits)

### Renames (backward-incompatible by design — old names removed)
- `import_author` → `author_import_record_to_author(author_import_record, eastern=False)` in `load_book.py`
- `build_query` → `import_record_to_edition(rec)` in `load_book.py`
- `build_author_reply` → `load_author_import_records(authors_in, edits, source, save=True)` in `__init__.py`

### New Public Function
- `check_cover_url_host(cover_url, allowed_cover_hosts) -> bool` — case-insensitive host allow-listing, used by `process_cover_url` and exposed for tests/observability.

### Preview-Mode Plumbing
- `save: bool = True` parameter added to `load`, `load_data`, `new_work`, `load_author_import_records`, and `update_edition_with_rec_data`. Default `True` preserves backward compatibility.
- When `save=False`: `web.ctx.site.save_many`, `add_cover`, and `update_ia_metadata_for_ol_edition` are all skipped. Simulated UUID keys replace `web.ctx.site.new_key`. Response payload includes `preview: True` and an `edits` list.

### HTTP Endpoint Wiring
- `importapi.POST` and `ia_importapi.POST` parse `preview = i.get('preview') == 'true'` from `web.input()` and forward `save=not preview` through every downstream call (including `ia_importapi.ia_import`, `ia_importapi.load_book`, and the bulk-MARC branch). The `ia_importapi` class docstring is updated to document the new field.

### Test Coverage
- All 15 existing call sites in `test_load_book.py` updated to use the renamed functions (34 tests).
- `test_add_book.py` adds 11 new tests: 6 parametrized `test_check_cover_url_host` cases and a `TestPreviewMode` class with 5 methods asserting persistence/cover/IA-writeback skipping and UUID-based key allocation (99 total tests).

## Validation Results

- **Tests**: 2361 passed, 9 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failures (`pytest . --ignore=infogami --ignore=vendor --ignore=node_modules --ignore=venv`)
- **Linting**: ruff and black pass for all 6 modified files; mypy reports no new errors
- **Backward compatibility**: All existing callers (`openlibrary/core/vendors.py`, `openlibrary/core/batch_imports.py`, `openlibrary/plugins/admin/code.py`) preserved — `save` defaults to `True` everywhere.
- **Zero residual references** to `import_author`, `build_query`, or `build_author_reply` anywhere in the codebase.

90% complete. All AAP-scoped autonomous work is implemented, tested, and validated. The remaining 4 hours cover path-to-production activities (maintainer code review, staging QA of the new `?preview=true` parameter, production smoke test).

author: sudhakarsingh27
body:
# Design

## Problem

8×H100, `test_essential=True`, 38 runnable CP attention configs:

- ~554 s wall when each config runs in its own `torchrun`.
- Of that, only ~216 s is the test work itself (CP fwd/bwd + assertions, ~5.7 s/config).
- The remaining ~338 s is per-spawn overhead — Python imports + NCCL global init/teardown — paid 38 times at ~8.9 s each.

We need that overhead amortised, without changing how tests are written or how skips report.

## Approach

A session-scoped fixture (`_cp_batch_results`) does two passes:

1. **Collect (dry-run, in-process).** Walk pytest's collected items. For each item that requests `_cp_batch_results`, call its test function directly with a stubbed `request`. The body executes its inline `pytest.skip(...)` checks normally; if any fires, the item is dropped from the batch. Otherwise the body's final call to `_run_or_fetch(...)` records its kwargs in a module-level dict instead of launching a subprocess.
2. **Batch + execute.** Group recorded kwargs by `num_gpus_per_node`, chunk into batches of `CP_TEST_BATCH_SIZE` (default 16), launch one `torchrun` per chunk. Worker (`run_attention_with_cp.py`) inits NCCL once, loops over configs, atomically flushes per-config results to `<batch>.results.json`. When pytest later runs each test for real, the body re-evaluates skips and `_run_or_fetch` looks up the recorded result.

## How dry-run works

```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def _cp_batch_results(request):
    items = [it for it in request.session.items
             if "_cp_batch_results" in getattr(it, "fixturenames", ())]
    _COLLECT_MODE = True
    for item in items:
        if _item_static_skip(item):
            continue
        try:
            _dry_run_item(item)
        except pytest.skip.Exception:
            pass
        except BaseException:
            pass  # surfaces in execute mode as a normal pytest error
    _COLLECT_MODE = False
    # group _COLLECTED_KWARGS by num_gpus, chunk, run torchrun batches
```

`_dry_run_item` calls the underlying function with the same parametrize values pytest would have passed:

```python
def _dry_run_item(item):
    func = item.function
    params = dict(item.callspec.params)
    func(_DummyRequest(item.nodeid), {}, **params)
```

This bypasses pytest's runner entirely — no fixture setup hooks, no plugin reporters, no captured-stdout machinery.

`_run_or_fetch` checks a module-level `_COLLECT_MODE` flag:

```python
def _run_or_fetch(request, batch_results, *, num_gpus_per_node, **worker_kwargs):
    if _COLLECT_MODE:
        _COLLECTED_KWARGS[request.node.nodeid] = dict(num_gpus=num_gpus_per_node, **worker_kwargs)
        return  # never reaches the lookup; never asserts
    entry = batch_results.get(request.node.nodeid)
    ...
```

In collect mode it's a recorder, in execute mode it's a result-fetcher. The test body doesn't know which mode it's in — it just calls one helper at the end.

### Stubs and skip handling

| Param | Stub | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `_DummyRequest(nodeid)` — only `request.node.nodeid` | `_run_or_fetch` only reads `nodeid`; test body never touches `request`. |
| `_cp_batch_results` | `{}` (empty dict) | `_run_or_fetch` returns early in collect mode, never inspects `batch_results`. |

Inline `pytest.skip("reason")` raises `pytest.skip.Exception`. The dry-run loop catches per-item, drops the item from the batch, and moves on. In execute mode the same line raises again; pytest reports SKIPPED with the same reason.

`@pytest.mark.skip` and `@pytest.mark.skipif(<bool_condition>)` markers don't fire when calling `item.function(...)` directly. `_item_static_skip(item)` walks `item.iter_markers("skip"|"skipif")` and reads `marker.args[0]` (the condition) before the dry-run, dropping items the markers would otherwise skip.

### Cost of running the body twice

For each item the body runs once during dry-run and once during execute. Skip checks are pure Python; the only non-trivial work is `get_available_attention_backends`, cached per nodeid via `_BACKEND_CACHE` so the second call is a dict hit. Measured on full `test_essential=True` (10272 collected items, 38 runnable): 530 cache lookups, 0.03 s total.

End-to-end pytest overhead (dry-run + collection, with `torchrun` stubbed): ~14 s wall, of which ~6.6 s is module-import startup, ~3.2 s is pytest per-item setup, 0.2 s is the batching infra itself. Negligible vs the GPU work it dispatches.

## Performance

8×H100, `test_essential=True` (38 runnable configs: 34 × 2-GPU + 4 × 4-GPU). In **unbatched** mode each config is its own `torchrun`. In **batched** mode, configs sharing the same `num_gpus_per_node` are grouped into one `torchrun` of up to `CP_TEST_BATCH_SIZE` configs.

| Run        | Torchrun spawns                | Wall   | Speedup |
|------------|--------------------------------|--------|---------|
| Unbatched  | 38 (one per config)            | ~554 s | 1.0×    |
| `B=16`     | 4 (16+16+2 @ 2GPU; 4 @ 4GPU)   | 274 s  | 2.0×    |
| `B=32`     | 3 (32+2 @ 2GPU; 4 @ 4GPU)      | 248 s  | 2.2×    |
| `B=50`     | 2 (34 @ 2GPU; 4 @ 4GPU)        | 237 s  | 2.3×    |

### Where the 2× comes from

1. **34 fewer `torchrun` spawns.** Each saved spawn cuts ~12 s of startup (Python imports + NCCL global init/teardown) — measured directly from the wall-time delta `B=50 → B=16` (37 s saved across 2 fewer spawns).
2. **~1.2 s lower per-config work** (~46 s total). Sharing NCCL global state across configs in a batch drops per-config wall from 5.7 s to 4.5 s; only the per-config CP comm-group create/destroy remains.

The spawn savings dominate.

### Picking `CP_TEST_BATCH_SIZE`

For these 38 configs (34 × 2-GPU + 4 × 4-GPU):

- `B=16 → B=32`: −27 s (one fewer 2-GPU spawn).
- `B=32 → B=50`: −11 s (one more, but the merged batch is now large enough that bookkeeping eats into the savings).

`16` and `32` are ballparks for *this* matrix — once `B` exceeds the largest GPU-group size (here, 34), all configs in that group already share a `torchrun` and further increases do nothing. With a larger config matrix (e.g. full `test_essential=False` ≈ 348 runnable), the same logic implies `B` should scale up too: pick it so the largest GPU-group has only a small number of `torchrun` spawns, but not so large that a single batch becomes long enough that a worker crash loses too much progress.

## Knobs

| Env var | Effect |
|---|---|
| `CP_TEST_BATCH_SIZE=N` | Configs per `torchrun`. Default 16. Set 1 to bisect. |
| `CP_TEST_BATCH_RETRY=0` | Disable singleton retry for unattributed crashes. |

## Adding a batched test

1. Write the test the way you would any CP test: `@pytest.mark.parametrize` stack + inline `pytest.skip(...)` checks.
2. Add `request, _cp_batch_results` to the function signature.
3. Replace the trailing `run_distributed(get_bash_arguments(...))` with `_run_or_fetch(request, _cp_batch_results, num_gpus_per_node=N, ...)` (kwargs become the worker's `run_dpa_with_cp(**kwargs)` arguments).

That's the entire wiring.

## Failure semantics

| Outcome | What pytest sees |
|---|---|
| Inline `pytest.skip(...)` fires | Standard SKIP (re-evaluated in execute mode and short-circuits before `_run_or_fetch`). |
| `@pytest.mark.skip(if)` marker fires | Standard SKIP via pytest's normal path (not queued for `torchrun`). |
| Config ran, assertion failed | FAIL with worker's traceback. |
| Assertion fired on rank > 0 only | FAIL via cross-rank `dist.all_reduce(ok, op=MIN)`. |
| Worker subprocess crashed before flush | Each affected config retried as a singleton; real result wins, residual crashes surface as FAIL with attribution. |
| Dry-run itself raised | Caught and ignored in the fixture; same exception fires in execute mode and pytest reports it as a normal test ERROR. |

author: kirpodolak
body: ## Problem `digital-signage.service` used `Requires=dsign-mpv.service`. When Settings or IPC recovery runs `sudo systemctl restart dsign-mpv.service`, systemd briefly deactivates mpv; **Requires** propagates that into stopping `digital-signage`, killing Flask and in-flight `sudo` children (journal shows SIGKILL on `sudo` / `systemctl`). ## Fix Replace **Requires** with **Wants** for `dsign-mpv.service`. `After=dsign-mpv.service` is unchanged so boot ordering stays sane; restarting mpv no longer tears down the controller. ## Deploy After merge: copy updated unit (or `git pull` + install script), then: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart digital-signage.service`

body:
## Summary

- Adds a subtraction quiz that mirrors the addition flow: visual dots (with the trailing N "taken away" — ghosted and struck through), the equation `A − B = ?`, and four tap-to-answer buttons. Numbers are constrained so the answer stays in `0..10` (no negatives for early learners).
- Adds a parent-controlled **Settings** screen (modal, opened from a gear button on Home) with a Switch to opt in to subtraction. Persisted via `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` so the choice survives restarts. Includes a "More levels coming soon" card to set expectations for future content.
- When subtraction is enabled, Home shows two CTAs side by side ("Add!" and "Take away!"). Otherwise it stays the single "Let's Play!" button.

## Notable changes

- `lib/problems.ts`: `generateProblem(op, rng?)` now supports `'add' | 'sub'`. Distractor logic is unchanged.
- `lib/settings.ts`: new `SettingsProvider` / `useSettings` backed by AsyncStorage. v1 schema is just `{ subtractionEnabled: boolean }`, default `false`.
- `components/dot-group.tsx`: new `removed?: number` prop fades and strikes through the trailing dots so subtraction reads as "start with A, take away B".
- `app/_layout.tsx`: wraps the tree in `SettingsProvider` and registers a modal `/settings` route.
- `app/play.tsx`: reads `?op=add|sub`, resets the streak when the mode changes, switches the visual + glyph + header label accordingly.
- `app/index.tsx`: gear button → `/settings`; conditional dual CTAs based on the persisted setting.
- `app/settings.tsx`: new screen with the toggle + coming-soon card.

- [ ] `npx expo lint` passes (verified locally)

author: leoquent
body:
### 💡 What
Refactored `AnimatedNumber` component to use `motion/react`'s native `animate` function instead of a `setInterval` with React state updates.

### 🎯 Why
The previous implementation used `setInterval` firing every 16ms to update React state (`setDisplay`), which caused the entire component to re-render ~125 times over the 2-second duration. Since multiple animated numbers run simultaneously on the page, this resulted in hundreds of unnecessary render cycles.

### 📊 Impact
Eliminates ~125 re-renders per animated number instance by directly mutating the DOM node's `textContent` outside of React's render cycle. 

### 🔬 Measurement
Start the dev server (`npm run dev`) and observe the animated statistics on the homepage (e.g., "130+ Jahre Erfahrung"). Use React Developer Tools Profiler to verify that the `AnimatedNumber` component no longer re-renders constantly during the count-up sequence. Visual fidelity and timing (2s linear) remain perfectly intact.

body:
### Motivation

- Improve perceived load time by restoring previously rendered page fragments from `sessionStorage` while the live data request runs. 
- Persist small view snapshots so users see meaningful content immediately on navigation and during transient network errors. 
- Fail gracefully on storage errors so the cache is best-effort and does not break page rendering.

### Description

- Introduces `DASHBOARD_VIEW_CACHE_KEY` and `STANDINGS_VIEW_CACHE_KEY` and helper functions `readDashboardViewCache`, `writeDashboardViewCache`, `readStandingsCache`, and `writeStandingsCache` to manage JSON blobs in `sessionStorage` with a `cachedAt` timestamp. 
- Adds `restoreDashboardViewFromCache` and `restoreStandingsCache` which rehydrate DOM fragments (e.g. `driver-podium`, `team-podium`, `side-kpis`, `hero-next-race`, `hero-storyline`, `drivers-standings-body`, `teams-standings-body`) and a few textual elements (e.g. `status-season`, `status-next-event`, `.page-subtitle`) when present. 
- Writes cached HTML and text content after successful render paths in `loadDashboard()` and `loadStandingsPage()` so subsequent visits can show the last view immediately; storage write failures are ignored to avoid breaking the app. 
- Restores cached dashboard and standings content on `DOMContentLoaded` before triggering the live load functions, and keeps existing error handling and rendering flows intact.

### Testing

- Ran linting with `npm run lint` and the existing automated frontend test suite with `npm test`, both completed with zero errors. 
- No new automated tests were added for cache behavior; existing tests passed after the changes.

author: adriandomc
body:
## Resumen

**M4 — AdditiveSynth.** Sustituye el sine generator por un sintetizador aditivo polifónico real. Es el primer instrumento "de verdad" del MVP. Teclado del synth view ya dispara notas reales con ADSR.

## Cambios

### C++ DSP

- **`AdsrEnvelope`** (header-only, inline, RT-safe): stages Idle/Attack/Decay/Sustain/Release con rampas lineales. Setters de A/D/S/R llamados desde el audio thread tras drain del SPSC (sin atómicos — mismo thread).
- **`AdditiveSynth`**: instrumento polifónico de 8 voces × 16 partials.
  - Cada voz tiene su propio envelope ADSR y phase accumulators por partial.
  - Las **amplitudes de partials son compartidas** entre voces y se recomputan cuando cambia `tilt`. Fórmula: `(1-tilt)*fundamental + tilt*(1/n)`, normalizada para evitar clipping.
  - **Voice stealing** por round-robin (índice 0 si no hay voz libre).
  - **Anti-aliasing**: skip de partials cuya frecuencia × 2 supere Nyquist.

### Sistema de note events

`IModule` extendido con `handleNoteOn(midi, velocity)` / `handleNoteOff(midi)` con default no-op (efectos los ignoran). El SPSC del Graph ahora discrimina kind:

```cpp
struct ParameterEvent {
    enum class Kind : uint8_t { Param, NoteOn, NoteOff };
    Kind kind;
    NodeId nodeId;
    uint32_t paramOrMidi;
    float value;
};
```

El drain en `render()` switchea por kind y llama al método correcto.

### C ABI / Swift facade

```c
bool chips_engine_send_note_on(engine, node, midi, velocity);
bool chips_engine_send_note_off(engine, node, midi);
```

Swift:
```swift
engine.sendNoteOn(synthId, midi: 60, velocity: 1.0)
engine.setParameter(synthId, additive: .attack, value: 0.05)
```

### App

- `AudioCoordinator` ahora crea un nodo `additive_synth` (no más sine). Defaults musicales: vol 0.5, A 10ms, D 150ms, S 0.7, R 400ms, tilt 0.5.
- `SynthesizerSectionViewController`:
  - **Volume + Attack + Decay + Sustain + Release + Tilt (en knob TUNE)** cableados al synth real.
  - El teclado piano dispara `noteOn` / `noteOff` directos. La frecuencia la calcula el synth desde el MIDI note. Polyfonía: el teclado multi-touch + 8 voces ya permite acordes simples.
  - WAVE, SUB OSC, GLIDE, FINETUNE quedan como placeholders visuales (no tienen target en el motor todavía).

### Tests offline (3 nuevos)

- Synth silencioso sin notas.
- `sendNoteOn(69)` + render 4 bloques → RMS > 0.05.
- `sendNoteOff(69)` + render 16 bloques → silencio (release completo).

## Limitaciones

- **Tilt mapeado al knob "TUNE"**: el mockup tenía un display "-12" en el slot TUNE. Mi Tilt es funcionalmente útil pero conceptualmente distinto. Cuando tengamos pitch shift global y un display numérico, lo movemos.
- **Sin LFO**: el plan M4 menciona LFO con destinos asignables. Pospuesto para evitar inflar el PR.
- **Sin presets**: el plan menciona 6-8 presets. Pospuesto; el sistema de presets llega en M7 con la persistencia.
- **Anti-alias mejorable**: el corte por Nyquist es agresivo (skip total). Un fade-out suave por partial sería más musical. Suficiente para M4.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Local**: `xcodegen generate && open Chips.xcodeproj`, ⌘B y ⌘U.
- [ ] **Run**: pulsar Play, ir a Synthesizer, tocar el teclado → suena. Mover ATTACK, DECAY, etc. y notar el cambio en el sustain del envelope.
- [ ] **CI**: build + tests.

author: pmcfadin
body:
## Summary

- **Bug #1 (Snappy varint collision)**: The first 4 bytes of `static_columns_table`'s Snappy-compressed `Data.db` file (`0xC0 0x51 0x5C 0x00`) were misidentified as the `V5_0StaticColumns` magic number. This caused the file pointer to skip past part of the compressed stream before decompression, producing "expected valid offset" errors. Fixed by adding `V5_0StaticColumns` to the Snappy varint collision detection logic in `parse_header_with_version_detection()`, alongside the existing `V5_0WideRows` check (Issue #219).

- **Bug #2 (static row duplication)**: Static rows (flagged via `EXTENDED_IS_STATIC` in the row's extended flags byte) were emitted as standalone result entries, the same as clustering rows. With 100 partitions × (1 static row + 1 clustering row), CQLite returned 200 results instead of 100. Fixed by accumulating static cell values per-partition in `parse_block()` and merging them into each subsequent clustering row, suppressing standalone static row emission.

**Before fix**: 0 rows (decompression failure); would have been 200 (duplication bug alone)  
**After fix**: 100 rows (one per partition, `static_data` merged into each clustering row)

## Test plan

- [x] New Rust regression test `test_static_columns_table_row_count_issue480` asserts exactly 100 rows
- [x] `cargo test --package cqlite-core --lib` — 954 tests pass, 0 failures
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo clippy --package cqlite-core --lib --all-features` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --package cqlite-core` — applied
- [x] CLI query `SELECT * FROM test_basic.static_columns_table` returns 100 rows with `static_data` correctly populated in each row
- [x] Other tables (`simple_table` 1000 rows, `composite_key_table` 100 rows) not regressed

Closes #480

author: petergi
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to v1.4.1 (PR #13). User confirmed via screenshot that the workspace prompt **still** clips at "Use default workspace at" with the path missing — v1.4.1's Static→Label switch didn't fix wrapping after all.

## Why v1.4.1's fix didn't work

Label is intentionally short — its stock Textual styling sets `height: 1`, which overrides the `.prompt-question { height: auto }` CSS via specificity. Static was also single-line in this layout despite Rich Text's wrapping defaults — the Container chain didn't propagate width as expected.

## v1.4.2 fix

Switch the prompt question widget to `Markdown`, which lays text out as a block-level paragraph that reliably wraps at the widget's width with no fixed-line constraint. Side improvement: backslash-escape CommonMark-special chars in the question text via `_md_escape_for_prompt` so paths like `/Users/peter/_work_/foo` don't render the underscored segment in italic, brackets aren't parsed as link syntax, etc.

Five new unit tests in `cab-tui/tests/test_prompts.py::TestMarkdownEscape` lock the escape contract: workspace-path round-trip, underscored paths, brackets, empty string, and plain-alphanum.

## Test plan

body:
🎯 **What:** The database backup and verification service had a command injection vulnerability where a spaced-joined string of arguments was passed to \`exec\`.
⚠️ **Risk:** Although these arguments are sourced primarily from application config which is relatively trusted, if any of the properties (like dbname, host, etc) were ever influenced by user input, they could be crafted to inject arbitrary shell commands.
🛡️ **Solution:** Switched from \`exec\` to \`execFile\` (\`execFileAsync\`) passing an explicit array of arguments. This prevents shell evaluation of the commands and neutralizes command injection risks.

body:
## Summary

- Adds the partner-facing `useEmployeeStateTaxesForm` hook for the dynamic, API-driven employee state-tax withholding form. Unlike static-shape hooks (`useFederalTaxesForm`, `useEmployeeDetailsForm`, etc.), the field set is determined at runtime from the API response, so the hook returns iterable state groups with bound `Field` components and a discriminated variant union (`'select' | 'radio' | 'text' | 'number' | 'currency' | 'date'`).
- Migrates the existing `Employee.StateTaxes` component to use the new hook + a shared `EmployeeStateTaxesView`, preserving its public props (`employeeId`, `isAdmin`, `onEvent`) and emitted events (`EMPLOYEE_STATE_TAXES_UPDATED`, `EMPLOYEE_STATE_TAXES_DONE`).
- Fixes a snake_case-vs-camelCase comparison bug in the previous component that prevented `file_new_hire_report` from being promoted from the API's `Select` wire type to the canonical `Radio` UI variant. The new hook applies the promotion correctly and also marks the question `isDisabled` once an answer has been recorded server-side (lock-once-set).
- Surfaces a single localized error code (`REQUIRED`) across all six field variants, with partner override support via the standard `validationMessages` prop. The shared SDK convention (`buildFormSchema` + `superRefine`) is followed; field validators use `z.unknown()` to keep the schema lean and let the UI primitives + submit serializer handle type coercion.

### Public API additions

- `useEmployeeStateTaxesForm` (hook)
- `UseEmployeeStateTaxesFormProps`, `UseEmployeeStateTaxesFormReady`, `UseEmployeeStateTaxesFormResult`
- `EmployeeStateTaxesErrorCodes`, `EmployeeStateTaxesErrorCode`
- `EmployeeStateTaxesFormData`, `EmployeeStateTaxesFormOutputs`, `EmployeeStateTaxesFieldsMetadata`, `EmployeeStateTaxesFormFields`, `EmployeeStateTaxesQuestionMeta`, `EmployeeStateTaxesMetadataConfig`, `StateTaxValue`, `StateTaxFieldsGroup`, `StateTaxQuestionFieldEntry`, per-variant `*StateTaxFieldProps` types, `StateTaxQuestionVariant`
- `createEmployeeStateTaxesSchema`, `createStateFields`, `useStateFields`, `getQuestionVariant`

### Files

- New: `src/components/Employee/StateTaxes/shared/useEmployeeStateTaxesForm/` directory containing the hook, schema, fields factory + components, fixtures, unit tests, and barrel.
- New: `src/components/Employee/StateTaxes/shared/EmployeeStateTaxesView.tsx` — shared view that wraps `SDKFormProvider` and iterates over state groups + questions.
- New: `src/components/Employee/StateTaxes/StateTaxes.test.tsx` — fixture-driven integration tests covering single state, multi-state, admin/non-admin, byte-stable submit payloads, sanitized HTML, empty states, validation blocking, and the `file_new_hire_report` Radio promotion + lock.
- New: `docs/hooks/useEmployeeStateTaxesForm.md` — partner docs, including a "How this hook differs from other form hooks" comparison table that explains the dynamic-shape divergence.
- Removed: `Actions.tsx`, `StateForm.tsx`, `useStateTaxes.ts` (replaced by the hook + view).
- Modified: `StateTaxes.tsx` (now a thin `BaseBoundaries` + hook + view wrapper), `index.ts` barrels, `src/index.ts` (public re-exports), `src/i18n/en/Employee.StateTaxes.json` (added `validations.required`), `src/test/mocks/apis/employee_state_taxes.ts` (refactored to expose handler factories), `docs/hooks/hooks.md` (registry row).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green: `npm run test -- --run` (34 new state-taxes tests pass; full suite green).
- [ ] CI green: `npm run lint:check` (0 errors).
- [ ] CI green: `npm run build`.
- [ ] Storybook: render the migrated `Employee.StateTaxes` against CA-only, NY-only, multi-state (CA + NY), and TX (no-income-tax) employees.
- [ ] Manual: verify `file_new_hire_report` renders as a radio group for admins, is disabled when an answer is already recorded, and is hidden for non-admins.
- [ ] Manual: verify required-field error message appears for empty submissions and is localized via `Employee.StateTaxes.validations.required`.

author: ygdrasil-io
body:
## Summary

The first path-aware clip primitives. Up to now `SkCanvas.clipRect` was the only clip op ; arbitrary path / RRect clips silently degraded. This slice adds `clipPath(path, doAntiAlias)` and `clipRRect(rrect, doAntiAlias)` end-to-end with AA support.

## Implementation

**`SkCanvas.State.clipMask: ByteArray?`** — 8-bit alpha coverage map sized `clip.width() × clip.height()`, row-major. `0xFF` fully inside, `0` fully outside, intermediate = AA partial coverage. `null` = pure rect clip (zero per-pixel overhead). Shared by reference across save() — `clipPath` always allocates a fresh mask before AND-ing in.

**`SkCanvas.clipPath`** — rasterises the path into a temporary 8-bit alpha bitmap via an inner `SkBitmapDevice` with `WHITE + kSrc + AA` paint, extracts the alpha channel, AND-s it byte-wise with the existing mask (`(a*b + 127) / 255` rounding) for clip-stack composition. `clipRRect` delegates to `clipPath` via `SkPath.RRect`.

**`SkBitmapDevice`** — three new private fields (`activeClipMask` + bounds) bound by `setActiveClip` from a new `bindClip` helper called before every `s.device.draw…` dispatch. Per-pixel writers (`blend`, `blendF16`, `blendF16Premul`, `blendF16PremulMode`) modulate `src.alpha` by `clipCoverage(x, y) / 255` and bail early when `cov == 0` (unless the blend mode produces non-trivial output for transparent src). The kSrcOver branch in `blendF16PremulMode` is **inlined** rather than delegated to `blendF16Premul` to avoid double-applying the mask.

## Tests

| Suite | What |
|-------|------|
| `ClipPathTest` (6 unit tests) | rounded clipping, inverse fill, clip-stack composition, clipRRect masking, save/restore round-trip, empty-intersection collapse |
| `InverseClipGM` 99.30 % | kInverseWinding circle clip + drawRect — fills everywhere except inside the cubic-approximated circle |
| `Bug5252GM` 93.32 % | oval clipPath × 15×10 grid of stroked rect + cubic combos (skbug.com/5252) |

## Test plan

- [x] `:kanvas-skia:test --tests ClipPathTest` — 6/6 PASS
- [x] `:kanvas-skia:test --tests Phase7qClipPathTest` — 2/2 PASS
- [x] Full suite — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 0 regression on the 185-GM baseline

author: kbibelhausen
body:
## Why

The family binary-accent header was extracted from inline \`<style>\` blocks into \`/assets/header.css\` in PR #9. Without a guard, future content edits could silently re-inline the stripe CSS and break the shared design system. This lint runs on every PR to main and blocks regressions before they land.

## Three checks (\`.github/scripts/header-lint.sh\`)

- **Check 1 — Inline caution-stripe regression:** Fail if a \`<style>\` block contains a \`.caution-stripe\` selector AND \`repeating-linear-gradient()\` in the same block. Header stripe CSS belongs in \`/assets/header.css\` only.
- **Check 2 — Missing \`/assets/header.css\` link:** Fail if the file uses \`<div class="caution-stripe">\` but does not link \`/assets/header.css\`.
- **Check 3 — Forbidden 100%-opacity ink stripe:** Fail if any file contains \`border-top: 2px solid var(--ink)\`. The new system uses 1px @ 60% alpha outlines.

## Regression fixture test output (Check 1)

Injected \`.caution-stripe { background: repeating-linear-gradient(...) }\` into \`index.html\` inline style block:

\`\`\`
[header-lint] FAIL Check 1 (index.html): inline <style> block contains .caution-stripe selector with repeating-linear-gradient(). Header stripe CSS belongs in /assets/header.css only.

[header-lint] 1 check(s) failed. See messages above.
\`\`\`

Exit code: 1. Fixture branch deleted after confirmation.

author: masfour7
body:
## Problem

Users on Flutter 3.35+ (Dart 3.9) get a build failure caused by `flutter_math_fork: ^0.7.3` being incompatible with the newer toolchain.

Reported in #101 and #112.

## Fix

Bump the dependency constraint from `^0.7.3` to `^0.7.4`:

```yaml
# Before
flutter_math_fork: ^0.7.3

# After
flutter_math_fork: ^0.7.4
```

`flutter_math_fork` 0.7.4 maintains full API compatibility — this is a drop-in version bump with no code changes required.

## Verification

```bash
flutter pub get   # resolves cleanly on Flutter 3.35+
flutter build apk # no errors
```

Closes #101
Closes #112

author: yschimke
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #882. With pointer events now reaching the daemon over the streaming canvas, drag visibly stutters while wheel ("rsb") stays smooth. The asymmetry comes from input rate, not a paint bug:

- Wheel fires ~10–30 Hz — well under the painter's ~60 Hz rAF.
- pointermove fires ~120 Hz on typical mice and up to 1 kHz on gaming mice.

Posting every native pointermove overwhelms the daemon's render pipeline. Frames pile up faster than they can be produced, the painter's newest-wins drops most of them, and the user sees motion that lags and skips between cursor positions instead of cleanly tracking the gesture.

The fix stashes the latest pointermove position in `state.pendingMove` and flushes it once per `requestAnimationFrame`, so the daemon's render cadence stays in step with what the painter can display. pointerDown / pointerUp still go through immediately (no perceptible gesture begin/end latency); pointerUp explicitly flushes the pending move so the gesture's tail isn't dropped; pointercancel discards it.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` (524 passing — 4 new coalescing cases)
- [x] New cases in `interactiveInput.test.ts`: burst-of-moves collapses to one post per rAF; a fresh burst after the previous flush schedules a new rAF; pointerup flushes any pending move and the deferred rAF doesn't double-post; pointercancel drops the pending move silently.
- [ ] Manual smoke: with `composePreview.streaming.enabled = true`, drag a live preview slowly and quickly — the painted frames should track the cursor cleanly without the previously-visible mid-drag stutter.
